# What is an agent in AI? Rational, learning, autonomous and knowledge agents, n8n agents
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agent-in-artificial-intelligence/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


In artificial intelligence, an agent is anything that perceives its environment through sensors and acts upon it through actuators to achieve goals: a thermostat, a robot vacuum, a chess program or a language-model assistant that searches and books meetings. This definition, central to Russell and Norvig's textbook, underlies today's AI agents. I build AI systems with tools and guardrails, so this page explains agents and their role, rational, autonomous, learning and knowledge-based agents, agent functions and programs, and n8n AI agents with a tutorial.

## What is an agent in artificial intelligence?

An agent is a system that observes its environment, called perceiving, and takes actions that affect it, aiming to achieve objectives. Inputs come from sensors, such as cameras, text or API data; outputs are actions, such as moving, replying or calling tools.

Examples: a self-driving car perceives roads and steers; a spam filter perceives emails and sorts them; a game AI perceives the board and moves; an LLM agent perceives a user request and tool results, then calls tools and responds. Designing an agent means specifying its performance measure, environment, actuators and sensors, often summarised as PEAS. For a RAG support agent, for instance, the performance measure is correct, cited answers; the environment is user questions and documents; actuators are replies and ticket creation; sensors are messages and retrieval results.

## What is the role of an agent in artificial intelligence?

The agent is the central concept for building intelligent systems: it frames AI as the design of entities that act well in environments. Its role is to turn perceptions into good decisions and actions that achieve goals, under uncertainty and limited resources.

This framing unifies AI subfields: search, planning, learning, reasoning and perception all serve agents' decision-making. In modern applications, agents automate tasks such as customer support, coding, research and operations, coordinating tools and data. Thinking in agent terms clarifies requirements: what the system can observe, what it can do, and how success is measured.

## What is a rational agent in artificial intelligence?

A rational agent chooses, for each possible sequence of perceptions, the action expected to maximise its performance measure, given its built-in knowledge and what it has perceived. Rational does not mean omniscient or perfect; it means acting well with available information.

Rationality depends on four things: the performance measure defining success, the agent's prior knowledge, the actions available, and the percept sequence so far. For example, a rational delivery robot chooses routes that minimise expected delivery time and avoid collisions. Agents can also gather information when uncertain, such as asking clarifying questions, which is often the rational action.

## What is an autonomous agent in artificial intelligence?

An autonomous agent operates without constant human guidance, relying on its own perceptions and learned experience rather than only built-in instructions, and adapts its behaviour to its environment over time.

Autonomy varies by degree: a robot vacuum navigates rooms by itself; an AI coding agent may implement features with occasional human approval; fully autonomous systems, such as some industrial robots, act with minimal oversight. In practice, responsible deployments keep humans in the loop for consequential decisions, limit permissions and log actions, because autonomy increases both usefulness and risk.

## What is a learning agent in artificial intelligence?

A learning agent improves its performance through experience. It has a performance element that chooses actions, a critic that evaluates outcomes against a standard, a learning element that updates behaviour based on feedback, and a problem generator that suggests exploratory actions.

Examples include recommendation systems learning from user clicks, game agents trained with reinforcement learning, and spam filters adapting to new spam. Learning lets agents handle environments too complex to program completely. Modern LLM agents learn mostly during training, though systems can also improve through feedback loops, memory and fine-tuning on logged interactions.

## What is a knowledge-based agent in artificial intelligence?

A knowledge-based agent maintains a knowledge base of facts and rules, uses logical inference to derive new information, and decides actions by reasoning about what it knows. It tells the knowledge base what it perceives and asks it what to do.

Classic examples include expert systems for diagnosis and logic-based planners. Their strengths are explainability and correctness within known rules; their weaknesses are brittleness and the effort of encoding knowledge. Modern systems blend approaches: RAG gives language models access to knowledge bases at query time, and knowledge graphs support reasoning over relationships.

## What is an agent function in artificial intelligence?

The agent function is the abstract mathematical description of an agent's behaviour: a mapping from every possible sequence of perceptions to an action. It defines what the agent does in every situation, regardless of how that is implemented.

For simple environments, you could imagine the agent function as a table of percept histories and actions, but real environments make such tables impossibly large. That is why agents are implemented as programs that compute actions efficiently. The agent function is useful for reasoning about what behaviour is rational before deciding how to build it.

## What is an agent program in artificial intelligence?

The agent program is the concrete implementation of the agent function, running on a physical architecture such as a computer or robot. It takes the current perception as input and returns an action, often maintaining internal state to remember the past.

Agent program types include simple reflex programs with condition-action rules, model-based programs tracking world state, goal-based programs that plan, utility-based programs that optimise outcomes, and learning programs. An LLM agent's program is the loop that sends context to the model, executes chosen tools, records results and decides when to stop.

## What is an n8n agent?

An n8n agent is the AI Agent node in the n8n workflow automation platform: a language model that can choose and call tools, such as other n8n nodes, HTTP requests, databases or sub-workflows, with memory for conversation context, inside an automated workflow.

It works by giving the model a system message, connected tools with descriptions, optional memory and a chat model. When triggered, by a chat message or another event, the agent decides which tools to call, reads results and responds. This combines n8n's integrations and reliability with flexible AI decision-making, useful for support, research and operations workflows.

## What is a simple n8n AI agent tutorial?

Create a workflow with a chat trigger, add an AI Agent node, connect a chat model with your API credentials, add memory, and attach one or two tools, such as a web request to an API or a database query, then test in the chat panel.

Steps:

- Add a Chat Trigger node.
- Add an AI Agent node with a clear system message.
- Connect a chat model and a simple memory node.
- Add tools with descriptive names, such as "get_order_status".
- Test conversations and watch the execution log.
- Add approval steps before actions that change data.

n8n's official advanced AI tutorial walks through a full example. Once it works in the chat panel, connect a real trigger, such as an email or form, and monitor executions for the first few days.

# Does agentic AI use RAG? RAG vs agents, MCP, ChatGPT, design tips and LlamaIndex
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-and-rag/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Agentic AI often uses RAG: when an agent needs facts from documents, retrieval is one of its main tools, and agentic RAG lets the agent decide when, where and how to search. RAG grounds answers; agents plan and act. I built RAG.NextUpgrad with hybrid retrieval, fusion, reranking and a confidence gate, so this page explains RAG in AI, how it relates to agentic AI, ChatGPT's behaviour, RAG versus MCP, whether agentic RAG is worth it or dead, design, improvement and LlamaIndex.

## What is RAG in an AI context?

In AI, RAG means retrieval-augmented generation: before a language model answers, the system retrieves relevant information from documents or databases and includes it in the prompt, so answers are grounded in specific, current sources.

RAG addresses two weaknesses of language models: they do not know private or recent information, and they can hallucinate. By supplying evidence, RAG lets models cite sources and lets teams update knowledge by editing documents instead of retraining. Typical components are document parsing, chunking, embeddings, a search index, reranking and a prompt that asks for cited answers. It is the foundation of most enterprise assistants, support bots and document question answering tools.

## Does agentic AI use RAG?

Usually, yes. Most practical agents need knowledge beyond their training, so retrieval is one of their core tools, alongside actions like calling APIs, running code or browsing. An agent decides when to retrieve and what to search for.

For example, a support agent searches the help centre before answering, checks an order through an API, and drafts a reply; a coding agent searches the codebase before editing files. Some agents use keyword or file search instead of embeddings, which is still retrieval. Agents also use retrieval for memory, storing past interactions and fetching relevant ones later. So RAG is less an alternative to agents than one of the capabilities that makes them reliable.

## What is the difference between RAG and agentic AI?

RAG is a technique for grounding a model's answer in retrieved information. Agentic AI is a design where a model plans and takes multi-step actions with tools to achieve goals. RAG answers questions; agents complete tasks.

A RAG system follows a fixed flow: retrieve, then generate. An agent runs a loop: decide, act, observe, repeat, using tools that may include retrieval, databases, web search, code execution and external services. Agents handle tasks such as booking, filing tickets or multi-step research, while RAG handles knowledge questions efficiently. Agents cost more, take longer and are harder to test, so use plain RAG when a single retrieval and answer suffices.

## Is ChatGPT agentic RAG?

Partly. ChatGPT is a general assistant that can act agentically: it decides when to search the web, read uploaded files or run code, and features like Deep Research and agent mode iterate through searches and actions before answering.

When it searches the web or your files and cites results, it is doing retrieval-augmented generation, and when it chooses searches step by step, that resembles agentic RAG. But it is not a dedicated RAG system over your knowledge base, with controlled chunking, permissions and evaluation. For business applications needing reliable, auditable answers from specific documents, build a purpose-built pipeline, as I did with RAG.NextUpgrad, and use ChatGPT for open-ended research and drafting.

## When should you use RAG vs MCP?

They solve different problems. RAG retrieves relevant passages from large knowledge sources to ground answers. MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is a standard way to connect AI applications to tools and data sources. You can use MCP to expose a RAG system.

Use RAG when answers must come from large document collections, with ranking, citations and permission filters. Use MCP when you want an assistant such as Claude Desktop or Cursor to access tools and data through a standard interface, such as a database, file system or ticketing system. A common pattern combines them: build a RAG search service, then wrap it as an MCP server tool so any MCP-compatible assistant can query your knowledge base.

## Is agentic RAG worth it?

It is worth it when questions need multiple steps, multiple sources or recovery from failed searches, such as comparing documents, combining databases with text, or research tasks. For simple factual questions over one knowledge base, standard RAG is cheaper, faster and easier to trust.

Agentic RAG adds latency from repeated model calls, higher cost, and new failure modes such as loops, irrelevant tool use or over-confident synthesis. Measure before adopting: build an evaluation set, compare standard and agentic pipelines on accuracy, latency and cost, and adopt agentic steps only for question types where they clearly win. Many production systems use a router: simple questions go to fast RAG, complex ones to an agent.

## Is agentic RAG dead?

No. Claims that RAG or agentic RAG is dead usually react to long context windows or agentic search that greps files directly. Both are forms of retrieval, and retrieval remains essential when knowledge exceeds what fits efficiently in context.

What is changing is the implementation: agents increasingly mix tools, including keyword search, vector search, SQL queries and file reading, choosing whichever fits the question. Long context helps but stays slower and costlier at scale, and models can miss details buried in huge inputs. The durable idea is giving models the right evidence at the right time, whatever we call the technique. Teams that evaluate and combine methods will keep benefiting.

## How do you design agentic RAG?

Start from question types: list the questions users ask, decide which need one retrieval and which need several steps or tools, then design an agent with a small set of well-described tools, clear stopping rules and an evaluation set.

A solid design: a router that sends simple questions to standard RAG; an agent with tools for document search, structured data queries and perhaps web search; a relevance check on retrieved results; query rewriting when results are weak; a maximum number of steps; and an answer step that requires citations and allows refusal. Log every tool call for debugging. LangGraph, LlamaIndex workflows or plain Python with function calling all work for implementation.

## How do you improve agentic RAG?

Improve the retrieval tools first, since agents amplify weak search: use hybrid retrieval, reranking and good chunking. Then refine tool descriptions, add relevance grading, limit steps, and evaluate end to end on realistic multi-step questions.

Common fixes: give each tool a clear description with examples of when to use it; return compact, well-formatted results so the agent can reason; add a step budget and a fallback to a direct answer; cache repeated searches; and require citations in the final answer. Review traces of failures to see whether the agent chose the wrong tool, wrote poor queries or misread results, then fix that specific behaviour rather than prompting generally.

## How do you use LlamaIndex for RAG?

Load documents with a reader such as `SimpleDirectoryReader`, build a `VectorStoreIndex`, create a query engine with `index.as_query_engine()`, and call `query()` with a question. LlamaIndex handles chunking, embedding, retrieval and prompting.

Then customise: set the LLM and embedding model in `Settings`; connect a vector store such as Qdrant or pgvector; adjust chunk size and overlap with node parsers; add a reranker as a node postprocessor; and return source nodes for citations. For agentic RAG, wrap query engines as tools and use LlamaIndex agents or workflows so a model chooses which index to query. Evaluate with LlamaIndex's evaluation modules or your own question set.

# Agentic AI: CAPTCHAs, testing, hallucination, coding agents, ServiceNow and careers
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-captcha-testing-coding/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Agentic AI raises practical questions, from whether agents can pass CAPTCHAs to how to test them and which ones code best. Most answers come down to the same principles: clear permissions, careful evaluation and human oversight. I build AI products with guardrails such as RAG.NextUpgrad's confidence gate, so this page covers CAPTCHAs, capitalising the term, testing, why agentic AI matters, solutions, development, the engineer's role, ServiceNow, hallucination and coding agents. Can agentic AI solve CAPTCHAs? Some AI models can solve simple CAPTCHAs, but responsible agents are designed not to. Browser agents from major AI labs, such as OpenAI's Operator, pause and hand control to the user when they meet a CAPTCHA, since CAPTCHAs exist to confirm a human is present. Bypassing CAPTCHAs usually violates website terms of service and can enable abuse, such as spam or credential attacks. Websites increasingly use behavioural signals and risk scoring instead of puzzles, and some offer verified access for legitimate automated agents. If you build agents that interact with websites, prefer official APIs, respect robots.txt and rate limits, and design for human handoff when verification appears. Treat CAPTCHA encounters as a signal that the site wants human involvement. Should agentic AI be capitalised? No. Agentic AI is a common noun phrase, so write agentic AI in running text, capitalising only AI as an acronym. Capitalise Agentic at the start of a sentence or in title-case headings. Also asked as: should agentic ai be capitalized · how to do agentic ai testing The same applies to generative AI and conversational AI. Capitalise it only as part of a proper name, such as a product or company that includes the word. Style guides generally avoid capitalising technology categories, since doing so implies a brand. Consistency matters most: choose one style for documents and websites and apply it everywhere. In headings, follow your chosen headline style, such as sentence case, which capitalises only the first word and proper nouns. How do you test agentic AI? Test agents with realistic task suites: define goals with clear success criteria, run the agent many times, and measure task completion, correctness, steps taken, cost, latency and safety violations. Review full traces, not only final answers. Combine several layers: unit tests for each tool, scenario tests with mocked tools for predictable checks, and end-to-end tests against sandboxed real systems. Include adversarial cases, such as prompt injection in web pages or documents, and ambiguous instructions where the agent should ask for clarification. Use model-based graders carefully, spot-checking them against human judgement. Run tests on every prompt, model or tool change, since small edits can shift behaviour unexpectedly. Track metrics over time. Why is agentic AI the future? Agentic AI is widely seen as the next phase because it moves AI from answering questions to completing work: researching, coding, processing documents and operating software, which is where most economic value lies. Also asked as: why agentic ai is the future Models now reliably call tools, follow multi-step plans and work for longer periods, while protocols such as the Model Context Protocol make connecting tools easier. Businesses want outcomes, not chat, so agents that resolve tickets or ship code changes fit real workflows. Challenges remain: reliability over long tasks, security, cost and accountability. The likely future is not fully autonomous AI but collaborative agents handling well-defined work under human supervision, with autonomy growing as trust is earned. What are agentic AI solutions? Agentic AI solutions are products that use agents to complete business tasks, such as customer service agents that resolve requests, coding agents that fix bugs, research agents that write reports, and IT agents that handle routine tickets. Vendors include major AI labs, enterprise platforms such as Salesforce Agentforce, ServiceNow and Microsoft Copilot Studio, and many startups focused on specific industries. Solutions differ in autonomy, integrations, security controls and pricing models. When evaluating one, run a pilot on real tasks, measure resolution rates and errors, check data handling and audit logs, and confirm how the agent escalates to humans. Prefer solutions that start narrow and expand once results are proven. What is agentic AI development? Agentic AI development is the engineering work of building agents: designing goals and tools, writing instructions, choosing models, implementing the control loop, adding memory and retrieval, and testing, securing, deploying and monitoring the system. It blends software engineering with AI skills. Developers write tool integrations with APIs and databases, define permission boundaries, and handle errors and retries. They build evaluation suites, trace agent runs to debug failures and tune prompts and tool descriptions based on evidence. Frameworks such as LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK and the Claude Agent SDK speed development, while the Model Context Protocol simplifies connecting tools. Good development starts with the simplest design that meets the goal. What does an agentic AI engineer do? An agentic AI engineer designs, builds and maintains AI agents: integrating tools and data, writing prompts and guardrails, building evaluation suites, monitoring production behaviour and improving reliability, cost and safety over time. Also asked as: what does agentic ai engineer do Daily work might include adding a new tool for an agent, investigating a failed run from its trace, testing a new model version against the evaluation suite, or adding an approval step for a risky action. Required skills include Python or TypeScript, API design, LLM behaviour, retrieval, security awareness and communication with the teams whose workflows the agent supports. The role overlaps with AI engineer and agentic AI developer titles, which companies often use interchangeably. What is agentic AI in ServiceNow? ServiceNow's agentic AI adds AI agents to its platform for IT, HR, customer service and other workflows. Agents can investigate incidents, resolve routine requests and coordinate tasks, managed through an orchestration layer with governance controls. These agents work within ServiceNow's existing data and workflows, such as incident records, knowledge articles and the configuration database, which gives them context about the organisation. Administrators control which actions agents may take and when humans must approve. Typical uses include summarising incidents, suggesting resolutions, automating password resets and routing requests. Organisations adopting it should start with high-volume, low-risk processes, measure outcomes and expand gradually. Check ServiceNow's current documentation for features, since releases change quickly. What is hallucination in agentic AI? Hallucination in agentic AI happens when an agent invents facts, tool results, file contents or completed actions, such as claiming a test passed when it never ran. Because agents act, hallucinations can cause real damage, not just wrong text. Agents may also call tools that do not exist, pass invented parameters or misreport outcomes in final summaries. Reduce these risks by grounding decisions in actual tool outputs, validating parameters against schemas, verifying results with independent checks, such as rerunning tests, and requiring evidence for claims in reports. Retrieval with citations and confidence thresholds, as in RAG.NextUpgrad, help agents decline rather than guess. Logs of every tool call make hallucinated claims easy to catch during review. Which agentic AI is best for coding? Leading coding agents include Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot's agent mode, Cursor's agent, Google's Antigravity and Gemini CLI, and open-source tools such as Cline, Aider and OpenHands. The best choice depends on your workflow and models. Terminal-based agents suit developers comfortable with command lines and large refactors; IDE agents suit those who want inline review; cloud agents run tasks in parallel and open pull requests. Compare them on your own repository with real issues, measuring correctness, how much review each change needs and how well they follow project conventions. Benchmarks such as SWE-bench Verified help shortlist models. Whatever you use, review every diff, run tests and keep changes small.

# Agentic AI internals, architecture, jobs, tools, platforms, careers and courses
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-internals-architecture-careers/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Agentic AI systems pursue goals by planning, acting with tools and checking results, built from a language model wrapped in orchestration, memory and guardrails. Understanding the internals clarifies what agents can and cannot replace. I build AI products with retrieval and safeguards, such as RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page covers how agentic AI works internally, its architecture, replacing humans, agentic tools and developer platforms, becoming a developer, generative AI comparisons, courses and Cloudflare's role. How does agentic AI work internally? Internally, an orchestrator loop sends the model its instructions, the goal, history and tool schemas. The model returns either a final answer or a structured tool call; the orchestrator executes the tool, appends the result, and calls the model again. Around this loop sit state stores that track progress, memory that retrieves relevant past information, permission checks that decide which tools may run, and limits on steps, time and spending. Errors are fed back so the model can recover. Each step is traced for debugging. Context management summarises or trims history as it grows, since long runs can overflow the context window. The model reasons; the surrounding code controls and records. What does agentic AI architecture look like? A typical architecture has layers: an interface where users set goals, an orchestrator or planner, the language model, a tool layer connecting APIs and data, memory and retrieval, guardrails and approvals, and observability for logs, metrics and evaluation. Also asked as: how agentic ai works architecture Patterns vary: a single agent with tools suits focused tasks; a router directs requests to specialised agents; an orchestrator delegates subtasks to worker agents and merges results. Tools often connect through the Model Context Protocol. Durable state lets long tasks pause and resume, such as waiting for human approval. Security spans every layer: authentication, least-privilege tool access and isolation of untrusted content. Version prompts and tools so changes can be rolled back, and start with the simplest architecture that meets the need. Can agentic AI replace humans? Agentic AI can replace some tasks people do, especially repetitive, well-defined digital work, but not people's judgement, accountability, relationships or ability to handle novel situations. Most realistic deployments pair agents with human oversight. Agents struggle with ambiguous goals, unexpected situations and long tasks where errors compound, and they cannot take legal or ethical responsibility. Roles built mainly on routine digital tasks will change most, while roles centred on judgement, care, leadership and physical work change less. The practical future is collaboration: agents handle volume and drudgery, people set direction, review outputs and handle exceptions. Workers who learn to direct agents gain leverage rather than losing relevance. What does agentic AI tool mean? An agentic AI tool is software that acts autonomously toward goals for you, such as a coding agent that edits files and runs tests, a research agent that searches and writes reports, or a browser agent that completes online tasks. The term also describes the tools agents use: functions, APIs and services an agent can call, such as search, email or databases. Context usually makes the meaning clear. When evaluating agentic tools, check what actions they can take, what data they access, how they ask for approval, and how they log activity. Strong tools show their plans and progress, making it easy to review and correct their work before consequences occur. What does an agentic AI developer platform mean? An agentic AI developer platform provides the building blocks to create, deploy and manage agents: model access, tool integrations, orchestration, memory, evaluation, monitoring and security, so developers do not build every component from scratch. Also asked as: what does agentic ai developer platform mean Examples include cloud offerings such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Google's Vertex AI Agent Builder and Microsoft's Foundry agent services, frameworks such as LangGraph with LangSmith, and SDKs from model providers, such as the OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK. Choose by your existing cloud, required integrations, governance needs and how much control you want. Platforms speed development, but understanding the underlying agent loop helps you debug and avoid lock-in. How do you become an agentic AI developer? Learn Python and APIs, then LLM fundamentals, tool calling and the agent loop by building one by hand. Next, learn a framework such as LangGraph, retrieval, memory, evaluation and security, and build portfolio agents that complete real workflows end to end. Also asked as: how to become agentic ai developer Employers look for evidence: agents with clear tools, guardrails, logs and measured success rates, documented in READMEs that explain design decisions and failure handling. Contribute to open-source agent projects, write about what you learn and join hackathons with agent themes. Software engineering fundamentals matter as much as AI knowledge, since agents are production systems. Free courses from Hugging Face, Microsoft and LangChain Academy cover the core skills. Is agentic AI part of generative AI? Agentic AI builds on generative AI rather than being a strict subset. It uses generative models to reason and decide, then adds tools, memory, planning and autonomy to take actions, which goes beyond generating content. Generative AI focuses on producing outputs, such as text, images or code, in response to prompts. Agentic AI uses those capabilities inside a loop that pursues goals and interacts with external systems. Not every agent uses generative AI; classic agents used planning algorithms or reinforcement learning. Today, however, most commercial agentic AI depends on large language models, so the two fields are closely linked in practice. Generative AI vs agentic AI vs AI agents: what is the difference? Generative AI creates content from prompts. Agentic AI describes systems that pursue goals autonomously, planning and acting. AI agents are the individual systems that do this, often built on generative models plus tools and memory. An example clarifies: a generative model writes a reply when asked; an AI agent reads a support ticket, checks the order system, drafts a reply and requests approval; agentic AI is the broader approach of building such autonomous, goal-driven systems, possibly with many agents. In everyday use, agentic AI and AI agents overlap heavily. Focus on what a system can actually do and how it is supervised, rather than its label. What is the best generative AI and agentic AI course? Strong free options include DeepLearning.AI's generative AI and agents courses, the Hugging Face LLM and Agents courses, Microsoft's Generative AI for Beginners and AI Agents for Beginners, and LangChain Academy for LangGraph. A good combined path starts with how language models work and prompting, then retrieval and RAG, then tool calling, agents, evaluation and deployment. Paid programmes on Coursera or elsewhere add structure and certificates but should be checked for recency. Whatever you choose, build projects at each stage, such as a RAG assistant, then an agent that completes a workflow with tools and human approval, measuring results as you go. Why is Cloudflare seen as strong in agentic AI? Cloudflare offers infrastructure suited to agents: a global edge network, Workers for serverless code, Durable Objects for stateful agents through its Agents SDK, hosting for remote MCP servers, an AI Gateway for model traffic and Workers AI for inference. Also asked as: why cloudflare wins in agentic ai It also handles a large share of web traffic, giving it a role in how agents access websites, through bot management, verified agent identity proposals and pay-per-crawl options for publishers. Supporters argue this combination positions it well as agents browse and act on the web. Competitors, including major clouds and other edge providers, offer alternatives, so choose based on your latency, state, integration and cost needs rather than narratives.

# Agentic AI tutorials: ethics, no-code, Python, LangGraph, GitHub, YouTube and PDFs
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-tutorials-ethics-langgraph/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Agentic AI means systems where a language model plans steps, calls tools and acts toward a goal, rather than only answering. You can learn it from scratch in a few months with Python, or start without code using automation platforms. I build AI products with guardrails such as RAG.NextUpgrad's confidence gate, so this page covers whether agents can make ethical decisions, beginner and no-code paths, Python and LangGraph tutorials, GitHub, YouTube and PDF resources, and implementing decision-making. Can agentic AI make ethical decisions? Agentic AI can follow ethical rules and policies it is given, and modern models are trained to refuse harmful actions, but it does not have moral understanding or accountability. Ethical responsibility stays with the people who design, deploy and oversee it. Agents can apply explicit constraints, such as never sharing personal data or requiring approval before payments, and models trained with methods such as Constitutional AI reason about harms. But they can misread context, be manipulated through prompt injection, or pursue goals in unintended ways. For high-stakes decisions in hiring, lending, healthcare or law, keep humans in the loop, log every action, test for bias and follow regulations such as the EU AI Act's human oversight requirements. What is a good agentic AI tutorial for beginners? Start with Anthropic's Building effective agents article, the free Hugging Face Agents Course and Microsoft's AI Agents for Beginners lessons. Then build a simple agent that uses one tool, such as a calculator or web search, through an LLM API. Also asked as: agentic ai tutorial github · agentic ai tutorial youtube Beginners should first understand the core loop: the model receives a goal and tool descriptions, decides to call a tool, receives the result and continues until it can answer. Next, learn the common patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallel calls, orchestrator and workers, and evaluator loops. Build small projects, such as a research assistant that searches and summarises with citations. Add frameworks only after you understand what they automate for you. How do you learn agentic AI from scratch? Learn Python and APIs first, then LLM basics such as tokens, prompts and structured outputs. Next, learn function calling, the agent loop, memory, retrieval, the Model Context Protocol, evaluation and guardrails, building a project at each step. Also asked as: how to learn agentic ai from scratch A three-month plan: month one, Python, HTTP APIs, JSON and an LLM provider's SDK; month two, tool calling, a hand-written agent loop, RAG for knowledge and a framework such as LangGraph; month three, multi-step agents with human approval, tracing, evaluation on realistic tasks and deployment with FastAPI. Read failure cases, such as looping and prompt injection, as carefully as success stories. Publish projects on GitHub with clear READMEs explaining design decisions. Can you learn agentic AI without coding? Yes, to a useful level. No-code platforms such as n8n, Zapier Agents, Make and Microsoft Copilot Studio let you build agents from visual blocks, connecting models to email, spreadsheets, calendars and business apps. Also asked as: can i learn agentic ai without coding Consumer tools also offer agent features: custom GPTs, Claude Projects and agent modes that browse, research and work with files. These suit automating personal and business workflows. Limits appear with complex logic, custom integrations, evaluation and scaling, where code gives more control and lower cost. A practical path is to start no-code to understand agent design, then learn basic Python when you hit those limits. Understanding prompts, tools and guardrails matters in both approaches. What does a Python tutorial for agentic AI cover? A Python agent tutorial defines tools as functions with JSON schemas, sends them to an LLM with the user's goal, executes any tool the model requests, returns the result, and loops until the model gives a final answer. Writing this loop by hand in about fifty lines teaches what frameworks hide. Then try frameworks: the OpenAI Agents SDK and the Claude Agent SDK for provider-native agents, LangGraph for explicit graphs and state, CrewAI for role-based multi-agent setups, smolagents from Hugging Face for code-writing agents, and PydanticAI for typed outputs. Add error handling, step limits and logging early. Test with realistic tasks and record how often the agent completes them correctly. What does a LangGraph tutorial for agentic AI cover? LangGraph tutorials teach building agents as graphs: define a state object, add nodes for model calls and tools, connect them with edges and conditional routing, then compile and run the graph with a checkpointer for memory. Also asked as: langgraph tutorial agentic ai Key concepts include the ReAct pattern, where the model alternates between reasoning and tool calls; persistence, which saves state between turns; interrupts for human approval before risky actions; streaming of intermediate steps; and subgraphs for multi-agent systems. LangChain Academy's free Introduction to LangGraph course covers these with notebooks. LangGraph suits production agents because explicit graphs make behaviour easier to test, debug and control than fully autonomous loops. Where can you find agentic AI tutorials on GitHub? Good repositories include microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners, the Hugging Face agents-course repository, langchain-ai/langchain-academy, Anthropic's cookbook with agent patterns, and the examples folders of the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph. Many repositories include notebooks you can run on Google Colab, with exercises that build progressively more capable agents. Community collections list agent frameworks, papers and projects, which help you discover tools. When using any repository, check recent activity and dependency versions, since agent frameworks change quickly. Fork a tutorial, extend it with your own tool or data source, and document what you changed, which turns learning into a portfolio project. What are good agentic AI tutorials on YouTube? Useful channels include DeepLearning.AI, with short course content on agents; LangChain's channel, with LangGraph tutorials; Hugging Face; Anthropic's talks on building effective agents; and Microsoft Reactor sessions on AI agents. Prefer recent videos that build working agents step by step and discuss failures, not only demos. Follow along in your own code rather than watching passively, and pause to modify each example. Conference talks from engineers who run agents in production explain practical lessons about evaluation, cost and reliability that tutorials often skip. Combine videos with official documentation, since frameworks update faster than recorded content. Keep a notes file of patterns you can reuse. Is there an agentic AI tutorial PDF? Yes. Useful free PDFs include OpenAI's A practical guide to building agents and Google's Agents whitepaper. Anthropic's Building effective agents article can also be saved as a PDF from your browser. These guides cover when to use agents, choosing models, designing tools, writing instructions, orchestration patterns, guardrails and human oversight. They are short enough to read in an afternoon and complement hands-on courses. Be cautious with unofficial PDFs shared on social media, which may be outdated or repackaged from other sources. After reading, implement one pattern from each guide in code, since agent design principles only become clear when you see agents fail and recover. How do you implement decision-making capabilities in agentic AI? Combine LLM reasoning with explicit structure: routing prompts that classify requests, planning steps that break goals into tasks, rules that constrain actions, confidence thresholds that trigger fallbacks, and human approval for high-impact decisions. Also asked as: agentic ai - implementing decision-making capabilities - tutorial Common patterns include ReAct, where the model reasons before each tool call; evaluator loops, where a second prompt checks outputs; and state machines that limit which actions are allowed at each stage. Use structured outputs so decisions are machine-checkable. In RAG.NextUpgrad, a confidence gate decides whether evidence is strong enough to answer or to decline, a simple but effective decision rule. Log decisions with reasons, and evaluate them on realistic scenarios before deployment.

# Agentic AI uses: maintenance, enterprise platforms, search, testing, suppliers, voice
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-uses-maintenance-testing-voice/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Agentic AI is moving from demos into real operations: monitoring equipment, running enterprise workflows, searching knowledge, writing tests and managing suppliers. Each use works best with clear goals, good tools and human oversight. I build AI products with retrieval, live speech-to-text and guardrails, such as RAG.NextUpgrad and the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, so this page covers maintenance, enterprise platforms, what agentic AI means, semantic search, single agents, test cases, suppliers, evaluating search, freezes and voice agents. How does agentic AI contribute to predictive maintenance? Agentic AI turns predictions into action: machine learning models flag equipment likely to fail from sensor data, and agents then investigate, check maintenance history and manuals, verify spare parts, draft work orders and schedule technicians for approval. Agents connect to maintenance management and ERP systems, summarise relevant manual sections for technicians, and update records after repairs. They reduce the time between an alert and a planned fix, preventing unplanned downtime. Humans approve work orders and safety-critical decisions. Success depends on reliable sensor data, accurate failure models and well-designed tool permissions, so pilots usually start with one asset class and measured downtime reduction. Start with assets whose failures are costly and well documented. How is agentic AI transforming enterprise platforms? Enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft 365, SAP and Workday now embed AI agents that resolve service requests, update records, draft responses and automate workflows using each platform's data and permissions. Also asked as: how agentic ai is transforming enterprise platforms Because agents operate inside existing systems, they inherit governance, audit trails and access controls, which eases adoption. Companies start with high-volume tasks, such as IT tickets, sales follow-ups and HR questions, measuring resolution rates and time saved. Challenges include data quality, integration across platforms, cost and trust. Training staff to work with agents matters as much as the technology. Successful deployments define clear scopes, keep humans approving consequential actions and monitor outcomes continuously. What is this agentic AI everyone keeps talking about? Agentic AI means AI systems that pursue goals with some independence: they plan steps, use tools such as search, email or databases, check results and keep going, instead of only answering questions. Also asked as: what is this &quot;agentic ai&quot; i keep hearing about It became widely discussed from 2024 as language models grew reliable at using tools, enabling products such as coding agents, research agents and customer service agents. The idea is simple: give a model a goal, tools and a loop. Agents differ from chatbots mainly in their ability to act. The hard parts are reliability, safety and knowing when humans should step in. Treat bold claims with healthy scepticism, and judge agentic products by measurable results on real tasks. What is semantic searching with agentic AI? It means an agent uses semantic search as a tool, deciding what to search, reformulating queries, searching multiple times and combining results, rather than running one fixed search per question. For example, asked a complex policy question, an agent might search for the main topic, notice a missing exception, search again with different terms, then cross-check related documents before answering with citations. This agentic retrieval handles multi-part questions better than single-pass RAG, at higher cost and latency, so limit search rounds to control costs. A strong base matters: RAG.NextUpgrad's hybrid retrieval and reranking make each search more accurate, so agents need fewer attempts. Can agentic AI operate as a single agent? Yes, and it often should. A single agent with well-designed tools handles most tasks effectively and is simpler to build, test and debug than multi-agent systems, which add coordination overhead and new failure modes. Multi-agent designs help when tasks split naturally into independent parts, such as researching several topics in parallel, or when different steps need different tools and context. Even then, an orchestrator often coordinates simpler workers. Start with one agent, measure where it fails, and add agents only if the evidence shows a clear improvement. Simpler systems are also cheaper to run and maintain. Anthropic's guidance on building effective agents makes the same recommendation. Can an AI agent help generate test cases? Yes. AI agents can read code or requirements, write unit and integration tests, include edge cases, run the tests, and fix failures, which speeds up building test suites for both new and legacy code. Also asked as: can ai agent help in generating test cases Review generated tests carefully: agents sometimes write tests that pass by asserting current behaviour, including bugs, or that check trivial details. Ask for tests derived from requirements, not just from code. Mutation testing helps measure whether tests actually catch faults. Agents are also useful for generating test data, accessibility checks and regression tests from bug reports. Combine AI-generated tests with human judgement about what truly matters to users. How can an AI agent help with supplier management? AI agents can monitor supplier performance metrics, extract key terms and deadlines from contracts, flag risks from news or delivery delays, draft requests for quotation, compare responses, and prepare onboarding and compliance documents for review. Also asked as: how ai agent help us with supplier management They connect to procurement, ERP and email systems to track orders and follow up on late deliveries. Document extraction with schema validation, similar to DocuLens AI's approach, keeps contract data accurate. Humans should approve supplier selection, contract changes and payments. Clear audit trails help procurement teams trust agent outputs. Start with a narrow workflow, such as contract summarisation or delivery follow-ups, measure time saved and accuracy, then expand to broader procurement tasks. How do you evaluate the relevance of a search made by an AI agent? Build a test set of realistic queries with judged relevant documents, then measure whether the agent's searches retrieve them, using metrics such as precision and recall at k, mean reciprocal rank and nDCG. Also asked as: how to evaluate the relevance of a search made with an ai agent Also inspect the agent's search behaviour through traces: the queries it wrote, how it reformulated them and which results it used. Check that final answers are supported by retrieved sources, since relevant retrieval can still be misused. Include queries with no relevant answer to test abstention. LLM-based judges can score relevance at scale, but validate them against human judgements on a sample. Track these metrics over time, especially after changing prompts, models or indexes. Why does an AI agent get stuck or freeze? Agents get stuck in loops repeating the same failing action, wait on slow or hung tools, hit rate limits, overflow their context window, pause for approvals nobody sees, or lack clear criteria for when the task is done. Also asked as: why ai agent stuck or freeze Fixes include step and time limits, timeouts on every tool call, retries with exponential backoff, detection of repeated actions, summarising long histories and explicit success criteria in instructions. Surface approval requests clearly to users. Logs and traces reveal where the agent stalled. If a model keeps misusing a tool, improve the tool's description and error messages, since agents learn what to do next from the feedback they receive. How do you build a voice-controlled local AI agent safely? Combine local speech-to-text, such as Whisper through faster-whisper, a local language model through Ollama, text-to-speech such as Piper, and a simple interface such as Streamlit, with tools restricted to a safe allowlist and confirmations for actions. Also asked as: how i built a voice-controlled local ai agent with streamlit, local stt, and safe tool execution Running everything locally keeps conversations private and works offline. Safety matters because voice commands can be misheard: require confirmation before executing commands, sandbox file and system access, and log every action. Never let the model run arbitrary shell commands. Live speech-to-text, which I built into the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, shows how transcription quality shapes everything downstream, so test microphones and noisy conditions carefully before trusting voice control.

# Agentic AI vs generative AI: how agentic AI works, roadmap and certifications
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-vs-generative-ai/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Generative AI produces content, such as text, images, code or audio, in response to a prompt. Agentic AI uses those same models as a reasoning engine inside a loop that plans steps, calls tools, observes results and keeps going until it reaches a goal. In short, generative AI answers; agentic AI acts. This page explains how agentic AI works, what it can do, where it is used, why it matters, how it started, a learning roadmap, how to build it, and which frameworks and certifications are worth your time.

## What is the difference between agentic AI and generative AI?

Generative AI creates output when asked: a chatbot reply, an image, a code snippet. Agentic AI pursues a goal over several steps, deciding what to do next, using tools such as search, code execution or APIs, and checking its own progress.

An example makes it concrete. Ask a generative assistant "how do I fix this failing test?" and it explains. Ask a coding agent to "fix the failing test" and it reads the code, runs the test, edits files, re-runs the test and reports the diff. Agentic systems are built on generative models, so the two are layers rather than rivals. The difference that matters in practice is risk: an agent can change real systems, so it needs permissions, limits and review.

## How does agentic AI work?

An agentic system gives a language model a goal, instructions and a set of tools, then runs a loop: the model reasons about the next step, requests a tool call, the system executes it, and the result goes back to the model, until the task is done.

Around that loop sit the parts that make it reliable:

- **Planning**: breaking a goal into steps, sometimes written down first.
- **Tools**: functions with clear descriptions and schemas.
- **Memory**: the conversation so far plus stored notes or files.
- **Guardrails**: step limits, cost limits, permission checks and human approval for risky actions.
- **Observability**: logs of every decision and tool call.

The ReAct pattern, interleaving reasoning and actions, is the core idea most agents still follow.

## What are the capabilities of agentic AI?

Agentic AI can plan multi-step tasks, use tools and APIs, read and write files, browse the web, run code, coordinate with other agents, and adapt when a step fails. With the right setup, it can complete tasks that previously needed a person to click through several systems.

Typical capabilities in today's systems:

- Researching a question across many sources and writing a cited report.
- Making code changes across a repository and running tests.
- Triaging and resolving support tickets with lookups in internal systems.
- Filling forms and operating web apps through a browser.
- Running scheduled workflows, such as summarising new documents daily.

Limits are real: agents still make mistakes, can get stuck in loops, and are vulnerable to prompt injection from content they read. Good design keeps a person in control of consequential actions.

## Where is agentic AI used?

Agentic AI is used most in software development, customer support, IT operations, research and analysis, sales and marketing operations, and business workflow automation.

Examples:

- **Coding**: agents that fix issues and open pull requests, such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot's coding agent and Codex.
- **Support**: agents that look up orders, issue refunds within policy and escalate the rest.
- **IT**: agents that reset access, check system status and file tickets.
- **Research**: deep research modes that read many sources and synthesise findings.
- **Back office**: invoice processing, document review and data entry with validation.

In each, the strongest results come from narrow scope, clean data and a human approving anything irreversible.

## Why is agentic AI important?

Agentic AI matters because it moves AI from giving advice to doing work, which can automate multi-step tasks that were too varied for traditional rule-based automation. That changes how software is built and how many jobs are done.

For students and engineers, it is important for two reasons. First, demand: companies want people who can build reliable agents, connect them to real systems and evaluate them. Second, leverage: using coding agents well makes a developer far more productive, and interviewers increasingly expect familiarity with them. The caution is equally important: agents can act on wrong assumptions quickly, so the skills that matter are judgement, testing, security and knowing when not to automate.

## When did agentic AI start?

The idea of intelligent agents is decades old in AI research, but agentic AI built on large language models started around 2022 and 2023, with methods such as ReAct and tool-using models, and early open-source agents that chained model calls with tools.

From there, model providers added native tool calling, which made agents far more reliable, and coding agents and research agents became mainstream products by 2025. Standards such as the Model Context Protocol, introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, made it easier to connect agents to tools and data. The term "agentic AI" itself became widely used in 2024 as the industry shifted focus from chatbots to systems that take actions.

## What is a roadmap for learning agentic AI?

Learn in layers: programming and APIs first, then how language models work, then tool calling and retrieval, then one agent framework, then evaluation, safety and deployment. Build a project at each stage.

A practical roadmap:

- **Foundations**: Python, Git, HTTP APIs, JSON, async basics.
- **LLM basics**: prompting, structured outputs, tokens, cost and limits.
- **Tool calling**: write a loop that lets a model call your functions.
- **RAG**: build document Q&A with citations; agents need good retrieval.
- **Frameworks and MCP**: try LangGraph or a provider's agent SDK, and connect tools through MCP.
- **Evaluation and safety**: test sets, step logs, permissions, prompt injection defences.
- **Deploy**: a small agent behind an API, with monitoring.

## How do I make agentic AI?

Start with a narrow goal, a model with tool calling, two or three well-described tools, and a loop with a step limit. Log every step, test with real tasks, and add human approval before any action that changes data or sends messages.

A first build: an agent that answers questions about your college timetable and can look up rooms through a small API. Define tools such as `get_timetable(course, day)` and `find_free_room(time)`, write instructions that say when to use each and to admit when it cannot find something, and run twenty test questions. Then add one capability at a time. Simple, well-tested agents beat ambitious ones that fail unpredictably, which is the same lesson from shipping any production AI system.

## Which agentic AI framework is best?

There is no single best framework. LangGraph suits complex, stateful agents with explicit control flow; provider SDKs from OpenAI and Anthropic are lightweight and close to their models; CrewAI and AutoGen focus on multi-agent collaboration; LlamaIndex is strong for document-heavy agents.

Choose by your needs: how much control you need over each step, whether you may switch model providers, how you will persist state and resume, and how well you can trace and debug runs. Many experienced builders start with a plain loop over a model's tool-calling API and add a framework only when they need its features. Learn one framework well rather than skimming five; the underlying concepts transfer.

## Which agentic AI certification is best?

There is no single industry-standard certification yet. Useful options include Hugging Face's free AI Agents Course, short courses on agents from DeepLearning.AI, and agent-related learning paths from cloud providers such as Microsoft, Google and AWS.

Judge a certification by whether it makes you build: tool calling, retrieval, evaluation and deployment, not just watching videos. Cloud provider certifications help if you target roles on that cloud. For hiring, a deployed agent project with a clear README, a demo video and an honest section on failure cases is more convincing than a certificate. If you take a course, turn its final project into something original before putting it on your CV.

# Agentic AI vs traditional AI, automation, multi-agent systems, and vibe coding
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-vs-traditional-vibe-coding/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Agentic AI differs from earlier AI and automation because it pursues goals by planning and acting with tools, rather than predicting a label or following fixed rules. The same shift is changing software development, from vibe coding to disciplined agentic engineering. I build AI products with guardrails, such as RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page compares agentic AI with traditional AI, automation, prompting and multi-agent systems, AI engineering roles, vibe coding and agentic coding, and shows how to build workflows. What is the difference between agentic AI and traditional AI? Traditional AI usually makes a single prediction or decision from input, such as classifying an image, recommending a product or detecting fraud. Agentic AI pursues goals across multiple steps, planning, using tools, observing results and adapting until the task is done. Traditional systems are narrow and trained for one task, often reliable and easy to evaluate with fixed metrics. Agentic systems are general and flexible, built on language models that can handle new tasks through instructions, but they are harder to test and can fail unpredictably. Many products combine both: a traditional classifier routes requests reliably, while an agent handles open-ended steps. Choose based on how variable the task is and how costly mistakes are. Agentic AI vs workflow automation: what is the difference? Traditional workflow automation follows fixed rules: when an email arrives, extract fields and create a ticket. Agentic AI decides steps dynamically, handling unstructured inputs and exceptions that rules cannot anticipate, but with less predictability. Rule-based tools such as Zapier, n8n and robotic process automation are reliable, cheap and auditable for structured, repetitive processes. Agents add value when inputs vary, such as free-text customer requests or messy documents. The best designs are hybrid: deterministic workflows handle the predictable path, while an LLM step classifies, extracts or drafts where judgement is needed, with humans approving risky actions. Claims that agents simply beat automation ignore the cost of errors and debugging. What is the difference between prompt engineering and agentic AI? Prompt engineering is the skill of writing instructions that get reliable outputs from a model. Agentic AI is a system design where models plan and act with tools over multiple steps. Agents rely on good prompts, but need much more. Building agents adds tool design, state management, memory, error handling, permissions, evaluation and monitoring. Prompts still matter inside agents: system instructions, tool descriptions and output formats shape behaviour at every step. Many agent failures trace back to vague tool descriptions or missing context, which are prompt problems. So prompt engineering is a foundation skill, while agentic AI engineering is the broader discipline of making autonomous systems reliable in production. What is the difference between agentic AI and multi-agent systems? Agentic AI describes any system that acts toward goals with autonomy, whether it uses one agent or many. Multi-agent systems specifically involve several agents, often with different roles, that coordinate, delegate or debate to complete tasks. Also asked as: difference between agentic ai and multi agent systems Multi-agent designs include an orchestrator delegating to specialist workers, agents reviewing each other's output, and parallel agents researching different subtopics. They can improve results on complex tasks but add cost, latency and coordination failures. Multi-agent research predates language models, with roots in distributed AI and robotics. Frameworks such as LangGraph, AutoGen and CrewAI support multi-agent patterns. Start with a single agent and add more only when the task clearly benefits. What is the difference between an AI engineer and an agentic AI engineer? An AI engineer builds applications with AI models broadly: RAG systems, classifiers, fine-tuned models and APIs. An agentic AI engineer specialises in systems where models act autonomously, focusing on tools, orchestration, guardrails and evaluation of multi-step behaviour. Also asked as: difference between ai engineer and agentic ai engineer In practice, the roles overlap heavily, and many job titles use them interchangeably. Agentic specialists spend more time on tool design, permission boundaries, tracing agent runs, handling failures mid-task and preventing prompt injection. Both need strong software engineering, LLM understanding and evaluation skills. If you are starting out, build general AI engineering skills first, such as RAG and evaluation, then specialise in agents through projects that complete real workflows end to end. What is the difference between vibe coding and agentic coding? Vibe coding, a term Andrej Karpathy coined in 2025, means describing what you want to an AI and accepting generated code without reading it closely. Agentic coding uses AI agents that plan, edit, run tests and iterate, with developers directing and reviewing the work. Vibe coding suits quick prototypes, personal tools and learning experiments, where speed matters more than maintainability. Agentic coding, with tools such as Claude Code or Codex, can produce production-quality changes when developers provide clear specifications, keep tests passing and review diffs. The difference is mostly discipline, not tools: the same agent can be used carelessly or rigorously. For anything users depend on, review the code and understand what it does. What is the difference between vibe coding and traditional coding? In traditional coding, developers write and understand every line, designing structure and debugging directly. In vibe coding, developers describe intentions in natural language and let AI write the code, often without reviewing it in depth. Vibe coding lets non-programmers build working prototypes quickly, which is genuinely empowering. But code that nobody understands is hard to debug, secure and extend, and it may hide vulnerabilities, such as exposed secrets or missing access checks. Traditional coding builds deep understanding that remains essential for reviewing AI output. Most professional developers now blend both: AI writes much of the code, while they design, review, test and own the result. What is the difference between vibe coding and agentic engineering? Agentic engineering is a term some engineers use for building software with coding agents in a disciplined way: clear specifications, tests, code review, version control and accountability. Vibe coding skips most of that discipline in exchange for speed. Agentic engineering treats agents as fast but fallible collaborators. Engineers write precise task descriptions, maintain project instructions, require passing tests, keep changes small and review every diff before merging. They also design guardrails, such as restricted permissions and sandboxed execution. This approach captures most of the speed benefit while keeping quality and security high. Vibe coding remains useful for throwaway prototypes, but production systems need the engineering mindset. How do you build agentic AI workflows? Map the process first, then decide which steps need deterministic logic and which need model judgement. Implement the predictable steps as code, insert LLM steps with tools where inputs vary, add human approval for risky actions, and log everything. Also asked as: how to build agentic ai workflows Use patterns from Anthropic's Building effective agents: prompt chaining for fixed sequences, routing for classifying inputs, parallel steps for independent work, orchestrator and workers for complex tasks, and evaluator loops for quality checks. Frameworks such as LangGraph make state and branching explicit, while n8n suits no-code builders. Build an evaluation set of realistic cases, measure completion and error rates, and expand autonomy only as reliability is proven. What is an example agentic AI workflow? An invoice processing workflow: receive an invoice email, extract fields with a document model, validate them against the purchase order database, flag mismatches, draft a query to the supplier about discrepancies, and route approved invoices for payment after human sign-off. Deterministic code handles fetching emails, database lookups and routing, while model steps handle reading varied invoice layouts and drafting supplier messages. Schema validation catches extraction errors, similar to how DocuLens AI validates extracted fields. Every step is logged with its inputs and outputs for audit. Humans approve payments and supplier messages. This hybrid design captures the flexibility of agents where documents vary, while keeping control over money and external communication.

# How AI agents are built: LLMs, chatbots, tools, research agents, buying and risks
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/ai-agents-built-llm-chatbot-risks/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


An AI agent is software that uses a language model to plan steps, call tools and act toward a goal, rather than only replying to messages. Most agents run on an LLM, but the agent is the system around it: prompts, tools, memory and guardrails. I build AI products such as RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page covers how agents are built, their relation to LLMs, chatbots, tools and software, research agents, getting or buying one, and whether agents can go rogue.

## How is an AI agent built?

An AI agent is built from a language model, a set of tools it can call, instructions that define its goal, memory for context, and a loop that lets it plan, act, observe results and repeat until the task is done.

Developers write tool definitions, such as search, database queries or code execution, with clear schemas so the model knows when to use each. Frameworks such as LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK and the Claude Agent SDK handle the loop, state and retries, while the Model Context Protocol standardises tool connections. Good builds add guardrails: limits on steps, approval before risky actions, logging of every call and evaluations on realistic tasks. Start with a simple workflow and add autonomy only where it clearly helps.

## Does an AI agent use an LLM?

Most modern AI agents use a large language model as their reasoning engine: it reads the goal, decides which tool to call next, interprets results and writes the final answer.

The term agent is older than LLMs. Classic AI defines an agent as anything that perceives its environment and acts on it, from thermostats to game-playing programs and robots with planning algorithms. Reinforcement learning agents, such as those that learned to play Go, use neural networks without language models. So an agent does not strictly need an LLM, but language models made general-purpose agents practical because they can follow natural language instructions and use many tools without task-specific training.

## Is an AI agent an LLM?

No. An LLM is a model that predicts text from input. An AI agent is a system that wraps a model with tools, memory, instructions and a control loop, so it can take actions rather than only generate responses.

Think of the LLM as the reasoning component and the agent as the complete worker: it can search the web, query a database, write and run code, or update a ticket, then check the outcome. The same LLM can power a simple chatbot, a summariser or an agent, depending on what surrounds it. That distinction matters for reliability: agent failures often come from tool design, missing context or loop limits rather than the model itself, so improving the system often matters more than switching models.

## Is an AI agent a chatbot?

Not necessarily. A chatbot answers in a conversation, while an agent pursues a goal by taking actions with tools. Many products combine both: a chat interface on the front, with agent capabilities behind it.

For example, a basic support chatbot answers questions from a script or knowledge base. A support agent can also look up an order, issue a refund within policy and update the customer record. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini started as chatbots and now include agent features such as web browsing, code execution and computer use. Some agents have no chat interface at all, running in the background on schedules or triggers, such as monitoring alerts or processing incoming documents.

## Is an AI agent a tool?

An AI agent uses tools rather than being one in the narrow sense, but from a user's view it works like a powerful tool that completes multi-step tasks. In agent design, tools are the functions an agent can call.

Examples of agent tools include web search, calculators, code interpreters, file readers, email or calendar access and company APIs. The agent decides which tool to use, with what inputs, and when to stop. Agents can also become tools for other agents: a coordinator agent might delegate research to a specialist agent and receive its summary as a tool result. When evaluating agents, review their tools closely, since tool permissions define what the agent can actually change in the real world.

## Is an AI agent software?

Yes. An AI agent is software: code that combines a model, prompts, tools, memory and control logic, running on servers, laptops or phones. It can ship as an app, a browser extension, an API or a background service.

Calling it an app or software depends on packaging. Consumer agents often appear inside apps such as ChatGPT or Claude, while business agents run as services connected to tools like CRMs, help desks or code repositories. Developers can build their own agents in Python or TypeScript with open-source frameworks. Like any software, agents need testing, version control, monitoring, security reviews and updates, with extra attention to unpredictable model behaviour, which traditional software testing does not fully cover.

## Which AI agent is best for research?

Strong research agents include the deep research modes in ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity, which search many sources, read them and write cited reports. For academic literature, tools such as Elicit and Consensus focus on papers.

Choose by your research type. General web research suits deep research modes, which take several minutes and produce structured reports with links. Academic work benefits from tools that search scholarly databases and extract findings from papers. Whatever you use, open the cited sources and verify key claims, since agents can misread sources or cite weak ones. Compare two tools on the same question and judge depth, source quality and accuracy. Retrieval with citations, as in RAG.NextUpgrad, makes checking answers practical.

## Where can you get an AI agent?

You can use agents inside assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot, through developer platforms that let you build your own, or from vendors offering ready agents for support, sales, coding and operations.

Coding agents include GitHub Copilot's agent mode, Claude Code, Cursor and OpenAI Codex. No-code builders, such as n8n, Zapier and Microsoft Copilot Studio, let non-developers assemble agents from templates and connectors. Developers can build from scratch with LangGraph, CrewAI, the OpenAI Agents SDK or the Claude Agent SDK, connecting tools through the Model Context Protocol. Start with the agent features in tools you already use, then build custom agents only when a specific workflow justifies the effort and maintenance.

## How do you buy an AI agent?

Most AI agents are bought as subscriptions: consumer assistant plans that include agent features, per-seat business licences, or usage-based billing for API calls and completed tasks. Enterprise agents are usually bought through vendor sales teams after a pilot.

Before buying, define the task and success measure, such as tickets resolved or hours saved, then run a pilot with real data. Check security and data handling: where data is stored, whether it trains models, access controls and audit logs. Confirm integrations with your existing tools and what happens when the agent fails. Compare total cost, including usage charges, against the measured benefit. Avoid vendors promising full autonomy without human review for high-stakes actions.

## Can an AI agent go rogue?

AI agents can behave unexpectedly, such as misreading instructions, looping, taking unintended actions or following malicious instructions hidden in web pages or documents. They do not have intentions of their own, but poor design can still cause real damage.

The main risks are prompt injection, excessive permissions, unchecked loops and hallucinated actions, such as deleting the wrong files or sending emails to the wrong people. The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications lists excessive agency as a key risk. Reduce it with least-privilege tool access, human approval for irreversible actions, step and spending limits, sandboxed execution, input filtering and detailed logs. Test agents against adversarial inputs before deployment, and keep a way to stop them instantly.
