# Can you make AI? Building an AI as a beginner, and making AI images and videos
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/can-you-make-ai/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Yes, you can make AI. As a beginner, the fastest route is to build an AI application on top of an existing model through an API, such as a chatbot that answers from your college notes; with some Python, you can also train small machine learning models yourself. You can also make AI images and videos with free tools. This page covers building your first AI, why learning AI and ML is worth it, and how to make AI photos and videos with ChatGPT, Gemini and Adobe Express, including what is free.

## Can you make your own AI?

Yes. You can build AI applications by connecting to models such as Gemini, GPT or Claude through their APIs, and you can train your own smaller models with Python libraries such as scikit-learn and PyTorch. Training a large model like ChatGPT from scratch is beyond individuals.

Three levels of "making AI":

- **Use a model through an API**: build a chatbot, summariser or document assistant. Hours to days.
- **Train a small model**: a spam classifier or image recogniser on your own data. Days.
- **Fine-tune an open model**: adapt a model to your task with LoRA on a single GPU. Days to weeks.

Most real products are the first kind, done well. That is how I built RAG.NextUpgrad and DocuLens AI: existing models, with retrieval, validation and careful engineering around them.

## How do I make an AI as a beginner?

Learn basic Python, get a free API key from Google AI Studio, and build one small, useful AI app: for example, a study assistant that answers questions from your notes and cites the page.

A beginner path over a few weeks:

- **Week 1**: Python basics, variables, functions, lists and dictionaries.
- **Week 2**: call an LLM API and print a response; then add a simple web interface with Streamlit.
- **Week 3**: add your documents, split them into chunks and retrieve the relevant ones for each question.
- **Week 4**: deploy it for free and share it with friends for feedback.

Alongside, do a short machine learning course to understand training and evaluation. Build first, then fill gaps in theory as you need it.

## Why learn AI and ML?

Because AI and machine learning are becoming part of almost every software product and many non-technical jobs, and people who can build with AI are in demand. Learning them also teaches durable skills: data handling, statistics, programming and careful evaluation.

For students, AI skills open roles such as AI engineer, ML engineer, data scientist and AI product developer, and make every other engineering role more productive. Even outside tech, knowing how models work helps you use them well and spot their mistakes. The field rewards builders: a student who ships one real AI project learns more than one who completes many courses. Start with a problem you care about, and let it pull you through the learning.

## Can you make AI images?

Yes. Gemini, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot can all generate images from a text description for free within daily limits, and dedicated tools such as Adobe Firefly and Canva's AI features do the same.

Write prompts with subject, setting, style, lighting and composition, for example "a flat illustration of students at a hackathon, laptops and sticky notes, bright colours, top-down view". Ask for changes in follow-up messages instead of starting over. For text inside images, such as posters, newer models do much better than older ones but still make mistakes, so check spelling. Respect copyright and trademarks: avoid generating logos or characters you do not own, and label AI images when they could mislead.

## Can you make AI photos?

Yes. You can generate realistic photos from text, and edit your own photos with AI: change the background, adjust lighting, extend the frame, remove objects or apply a style. Gemini, ChatGPT, Adobe and many phone apps offer these features.

For edits, upload the photo and describe the change precisely, such as "replace the background with a plain light grey studio wall, keep the person unchanged". Faces can shift slightly in AI edits, so check carefully before using images for anything official; never use AI edits for ID or passport photos. Never generate or edit photos of real people in ways they have not agreed to. Many tools add visible or invisible watermarks to mark AI images, which is a good thing for trust.

## Can you make AI videos?

Yes. Text-to-video and image-to-video models, such as OpenAI's Sora, Google's Veo, Adobe Firefly and others, generate short clips from a prompt or a still image. Longer videos are built by editing several clips together.

Generated clips are short, so plan a video as a sequence of shots. Describe each shot like a director: subject, action, setting, camera movement, lighting, style and sound. Expect to generate several takes and choose the best. For explainer or tutorial videos, real screen recordings and your own voice usually work better than generated footage, with AI clips as B-roll. Label AI-generated video when you publish it, and check your platform's rules on disclosure.

## Can you make AI videos for free?

Partly. Free options exist but come with tight limits, watermarks or short clip lengths. Some apps offer a few free generations a day, and video editors such as Clipchamp, CapCut and Adobe Express include free AI features.

Ways to make AI-assisted videos without paying:

- Write the script with a free chatbot and record your own voice and screen.
- Generate images for scenes for free, then animate them with simple pans and zooms in a free editor.
- Use free daily credits in video generation tools for a few key shots.
- Use free text-to-speech for narration, labelled as synthetic where relevant.

Free offers change frequently, so check each tool's current plan page.

## Can you make AI videos with ChatGPT?

ChatGPT itself writes, plans and creates images, while video generation comes from OpenAI's Sora, available through its own app and website for eligible users and regions. ChatGPT can still produce scripts, storyboards and prompts for Sora.

A workflow: ask ChatGPT for a 30-second script and a shot list, then turn each shot into a detailed Sora prompt, generate the clips, and edit them together with narration and captions in a video editor. ChatGPT can also write `ffmpeg` commands to assemble images into a slideshow video. Availability and limits for Sora depend on your plan and country and have changed since launch, so check OpenAI's current information.

## Can you make AI videos on Gemini for free?

Video generation in Gemini, powered by Google's Veo models, has mainly been part of paid Google AI plans with daily limits, though Google has run trials and student offers. Free accounts can still use Gemini to plan videos and generate images.

If you have access, choose the video option in Gemini, write a detailed scene description and generate a short clip with sound. Without access, use Gemini for scripts, shot lists and still images, then assemble a video in a free editor. Google has offered free plan periods to eligible students in some countries, including India, so check the official Gemini pages for current offers. Generated videos carry Google's SynthID watermark.

## Can you make AI videos with Adobe Express?

Yes. Adobe Express includes AI features powered by Adobe Firefly, including generating short video clips from text prompts, plus templates, animation, captions and editing tools to turn them into finished social videos.

Adobe Express is beginner-friendly: pick a template, generate or add clips, add text and music, and export for Instagram, YouTube Shorts or presentations. Free accounts get limited generative credits, and paid plans include more. Adobe trains Firefly on licensed and public-domain content and positions it as designed for commercial use, which matters for business projects; still, read the current terms. As with any AI video, review the output for errors and label it where appropriate.

# Career after BCA: options, opportunities, and choosing the right path
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/career-after-bca/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


A career after BCA can go in several directions: a software or IT job, an MCA or other master's degree, a specialised path such as data science, AI or cybersecurity, government and banking exams, or building a startup. BCA is a solid base, and what you do during the three years decides which doors open. I completed my BCA at VSICS from 2023 to 2026 while shipping five production AI applications and leading engineering at SCULT INDIA, so this page combines the options with practical advice on building a career during the course, choosing a path, and admissions.

## What are the career options after BCA?

The main options after BCA are a job in software development, web and app development, data analysis, testing, IT support or cloud; higher studies such as MCA, MBA or an MSc; specialised programmes in data science, AI or cybersecurity; government and banking jobs; and entrepreneurship.

How they compare:

- **Job right away**: start earning and learning; best if you have projects and an internship.
- **MCA**: deepens computer science and improves eligibility for some recruiters and roles.
- **MBA**: suits product, business analysis or management interests, usually better after some work experience.
- **Specialisations**: data science, AI, cloud or security through courses and projects.
- **Government exams**: open to graduates from any stream.
- **Startup or freelancing**: if you have a real problem to solve and the appetite for risk.

## Is BCA a good career option?

Yes, if you treat it as a foundation and build real skills alongside it. BCA gives you programming and computer applications from year one, costs less and takes less time than a BTech, and leads to the same software roles when you can show what you have built.

Its limits are real: some mass recruiters prefer BTech or MCA, and campus placements vary widely by college. You overcome that with a portfolio: two or three deployed projects, internships, hackathons and a clean GitHub. The degree opens the door to interviews; skills get you through them. If you want pure engineering roles at core hardware companies or certain government technical posts, check eligibility, as some require an engineering degree.

## How do I make a career in BCA?

Use the three years deliberately: master fundamentals and one programming language, build projects that match a target role, get at least one internship, join a community and hackathons, and prepare for interviews before final year.

A year-by-year plan:

- **Year 1**: Python or Java, Git, SQL and one small deployed project.
- **Year 2**: data structures, web development or data skills, a first hackathon, a community role.
- **Year 3**: one serious project in your target area, an internship, interview practice, applications.

This is the roadmap I gave first-years at the VSICS induction seminar in July 2025: foundations and AI tools first, then hackathons and internships, then placements or a startup. Consistency across three years beats a last-semester rush.

## How do I choose a career after BCA?

Test before you commit. Try short projects, internships or courses in two or three areas that interest you, notice what you enjoy and where you get good feedback, then choose the path that combines interest, ability and demand.

Questions that help:

- Which projects did you finish without being forced to?
- Do you prefer building products, analysing data, solving security puzzles or managing people?
- What do job listings in that area ask for, and how far are you from it?
- Do you need to earn immediately, or can you study further?

Talk to people two to five years ahead of you in each path. Their honest account of daily work is more useful than any ranking of "best careers".

## What are the career options in the BCA course itself?

During the BCA course, you can already work in ways that build a career: internships, freelance web or app projects, teaching assistant or tutoring roles, open-source contributions, hackathons, community leadership and content creation about what you learn.

These count as experience on a resume and in interviews. Freelance work for local businesses teaches client communication, deadlines and deployment. Tutoring sharpens fundamentals. Hackathons build teamwork and give stories for interviews; three first prizes and a top-three finish shaped my own path. Choose one or two activities and do them well rather than ten superficially.

## What career opportunities does a BCA open?

A BCA opens roles across IT services, product companies, startups, banking and fintech, e-commerce, government and education, in positions such as software developer, web developer, data analyst, QA engineer, support engineer, cloud associate and, with the right projects, junior AI engineer.

Opportunities grow with specialisation. Students who add strong skills in an area, such as building RAG applications, cloud deployment or data analysis, compete for better roles. Remote work and freelancing for international clients are also open to skilled BCA graduates. Postgraduate study widens options further: MCA for deeper technical roles, MBA for management and product, and data science programmes for analytics careers.

## How does the BCA course prepare you for a career?

The BCA course teaches programming, databases, operating systems, networks, web development and software engineering, plus a final project, which together form the base for software roles. It does not, by itself, teach deployment, real-world teamwork or how to present your work.

Fill the gaps yourself: learn Git and GitHub early, deploy every project, write READMEs, use AI tools well while understanding their output, and practise explaining your work. Treat the final-year project as a portfolio piece: choose a real problem, ship it, measure something, and document it. Employers judge the project, not the marksheet line that says you completed one.

## What is the best BCA college through CUET?

There is no single best college for everyone. Many central and state universities and their colleges admit BCA students through CUET; compare them on faculty, labs, internships, placement records for BCA specifically, location and fees.

How to compare:

- Check the list of participating universities and programmes on the official CUET website for your year.
- Look for the BCA programme's own placement and internship data, not the university average.
- Ask current students about teaching quality, labs and coding culture.
- Check whether clubs, hackathons and communities are active.
- Confirm UGC recognition and the programme structure, three or four years.

A college with an active tech community often matters more for your career than its name.

## When does BCA college start?

BCA classes in India usually start between July and September, depending on the university's admission process, CUET results and counselling schedule. Private colleges admitting on class 12 marks may start earlier.

Use the gap after class 12 well: learn basic Python, create a GitHub account, and build one tiny project, such as a calculator or a to-do app. Join an online community and follow a free course. Students who arrive with a little momentum find the first semester much easier and have more time later for projects, hackathons and internships. Check your university's academic calendar for exact dates.

## Where can you study BCA?

You can study BCA at central, state and private universities and their affiliated colleges across India, as well as at autonomous colleges, and through recognised distance and online programmes from approved universities.

Check that the university is recognised by the UGC and, for online or distance programmes, that it is approved to offer them. Compare the syllabus, practical labs, internship support and placement records. Location matters for internships and networking, but remote work and online communities have reduced that gap. Whatever college you choose, the projects, skills and network you build during the three years will matter most for your career.

# What can a career mentor help with? When and how to find one, at work, mid-career, abroad
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/career-mentor-help-find/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


A career mentor helps you make better decisions about your direction: choosing roles and skills, preparing for interviews and promotions, navigating workplace challenges, and building a network. I have mentored more than 200 students since 2023 and lead a 14-member engineering team at SCULT INDIA, so this page covers what career mentors do, why they matter, when and how to find one at work, mid-career, as a nontraditional student or abroad, mentor courses, public speaking and a common interview question.

## What can a career mentor help with?

A career mentor helps with direction and decisions: clarifying goals, choosing between roles or studies, identifying skill gaps, reviewing resumes and portfolios, preparing for interviews, negotiating offers, handling difficult workplace situations, and planning promotions or career changes.

They also offer what is hard to get elsewhere: honest outside perspective, introductions to people and opportunities, and lessons from their own mistakes. A mentor will not make decisions for you or find you a job, but they can help you see options you missed and test your reasoning. The more specific your questions, the more useful they become, such as asking how to present a hackathon project in an interview rather than how to get a job.

## Why is having a mentor important to your career?

A mentor accelerates growth by sharing knowledge that takes years to learn alone: how organisations work, what decision-makers value, and which opportunities are worth taking. Mentored people often gain confidence, clarity and access to networks sooner.

Mentors also act as advocates: a respected mentor who knows your work may recommend you for projects, roles or speaking opportunities. They help you recover from setbacks by putting them in perspective. In fast-changing fields like AI, a mentor helps filter noise, pointing you toward durable skills rather than every new tool. Mentorship is not a shortcut around effort; it multiplies the effort you already put in by aiming it better.

## When should you get a mentor?

Get a mentor whenever you face decisions you have not made before: choosing a degree or first job, starting at a new company, moving into leadership, switching careers or starting a business. Earlier is better, but it is never too late.

Students benefit from mentors when choosing projects, internships and specialisations, as early guidance prevents years of drift. New employees benefit during the first months, when understanding unwritten norms matters most. Experienced professionals benefit before promotions or transitions. You may need different mentors at different stages, so revisit your mentoring relationships each year. A sign you need one: you are repeatedly unsure what to do next, or you keep making the same kind of mistake.

## How do you get a mentor at work?

Identify someone whose work or career path you admire, ideally a level or two ahead, start with a specific request such as feedback on a project or advice on a skill, and build the relationship through follow-ups rather than a formal ask.

Also ask your manager to recommend mentors and check whether your company runs a mentoring programme. Make it easy for busy people: propose a short, focused conversation, come prepared with questions, and share how you applied their advice. Offer help in return, such as research, documentation or a perspective on new tools. Over time, regular conversations become mentorship naturally. Avoid asking strangers directly to be your mentor; trust builds through useful interactions first.

## How do you find a mentor mid-career?

Mid-career mentors are often peers or people one or two steps ahead in your field, leaders in adjacent functions, or experienced professionals in professional associations. Look for people who have made the transition you are considering.

At this stage, mentorship is more reciprocal: you bring experience too, so frame conversations as exchanges. Professional communities, conferences, alumni networks, industry meetups and online groups are good places to meet them. Consider paid coaching for structured goals, like moving into leadership, alongside informal mentors. Reverse mentoring with younger colleagues helps you stay current with tools such as AI. Be clear about your goal, since a vague request for career help is hard to answer.

## How do you get a mentor as a nontraditional student in your 30s?

Use your experience as an advantage. Professors, alumni and industry professionals often appreciate mature students who bring work experience and clear goals. Ask faculty for guidance, join student and professional communities, and connect with people who also changed careers later.

Look for mentors who made a similar transition, since they understand balancing study with work or family. Online communities, career-changer groups and mentoring platforms such as ADPList connect you beyond campus. Be direct about your timeline and constraints; mentors can then give practical advice. Peers can be mentors too, even if younger: a classmate strong in programming can help you technically while you help them with professional skills. Age diversity enriches mentoring in both directions.

## How can you find a mentor or co-founder in the US while living outside it?

Build visible work and join online communities where US-based founders and engineers gather: open-source projects, founder forums, startup accelerator communities, discussions on X and LinkedIn, and online events. Relationships start from contributions and conversations, not cold requests.

Platforms such as Y Combinator's co-founder matching and mentoring sites help connect founders across borders. Global hackathons, online programmes and remote internships let US-based people see your work. When you reach out, be specific: share a project, your goal and one clear question. For co-founders, test collaboration on a small project before committing, and get proper legal advice on company structure and equity, since cross-border companies add tax and immigration complexity.

## How do you become a career mentor, and do courses help?

You can become a career mentor through experience and practice; formal courses are optional but helpful. Courses on coaching and mentoring teach listening, questioning, goal-setting and feedback frameworks, and some offer certifications for professional coaching careers.

Look for programmes from recognised coaching bodies, universities or professional associations, and check whether they include practice sessions with feedback. Many organisations train volunteer mentors for their own programmes, which is a free way to learn. The most important preparation is real mentoring: start with juniors or students in your field, ask for feedback, and reflect on what helped. I learned mentoring mainly by doing it, through campus sessions and community work with students.

## Does public speaking help your career?

Yes. Public speaking builds visibility, credibility and leadership presence. People who explain ideas clearly in meetings, demos and talks are more likely to be trusted with responsibility, invited to opportunities and remembered by decision-makers.

Speaking also improves thinking: preparing a talk forces you to structure ideas and anticipate questions. For engineers, it helps in pitching projects, presenting designs, interviewing and leading teams. Start small with team demos, college sessions or meetups, then grow to conferences. Speaking at 20+ campus sessions has helped me explain technical ideas simply, which also improves my writing and leadership. Practise with feedback, record yourself, and focus on serving the audience rather than impressing them.

## How should you answer how a mentor has influenced your career?

In interviews, answer with a specific story: who the mentor was in general terms, a challenge you faced, the advice or example they gave, what you did differently, and the result. Keep it to about one or two minutes.

Use the STAR structure: situation, task, action, result. Focus on what you learned and how you still apply it, such as giving clear feedback, testing ideas with users, or asking for help early. Interviewers use this question to assess coachability and self-awareness, so show that you seek feedback and act on it. If you have mentored others, briefly mention how you pass the lesson on, which signals leadership potential and shows the advice outlasted the conversation.

# Careers after BCA: is it useless, engineers or not, fresher jobs and companies hiring
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/careers-after-bca-jobs/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


BCA, Bachelor of Computer Applications, leads to careers in software development, web and mobile apps, data analysis, cloud, cybersecurity, testing and AI engineering, especially when combined with strong projects. It is not useless; outcomes depend on skills. I am a BCA student at VSICS who has led engineering at SCULT INDIA since 2024, so this page covers BCA careers, its value, employability, whether graduates are engineers, entrance tests, BCA versus computer science, fresher jobs, hiring companies and job search.

## What are the careers in BCA?

Common careers after BCA include software developer, web developer, mobile app developer, data analyst, cloud and DevOps engineer, cybersecurity analyst, QA and test engineer, technical support, UI developer and, increasingly, AI and machine learning engineer.

Other paths include IT consulting, database administration, network administration, product management after experience, technical writing and entrepreneurship. Many graduates continue to MCA or an M.Sc in data science or computer science for deeper specialisation, or an MBA for management roles. Government jobs open to any graduate, such as banking and civil service exams, are also options. Choose a direction by your interests, then build two or three projects in that area during the degree.

## Is BCA useless?

No. BCA is a recognised undergraduate degree that teaches programming, databases, networking and software development, and many graduates build strong tech careers. It feels useless only when students rely on the syllabus alone without building skills and projects.

The degree's lighter structure leaves time for self-learning, internships and hackathons, which employers value. Its limitations are real: some campus drives and government technical posts prefer B.Tech, and theory depth is lower than in engineering programmes. Compensate with fundamentals, data structures, operating systems and databases, plus a specialisation such as AI, cloud or web. My own path, leading a 14-member engineering team while still in BCA, came from building outside the syllabus.

## Are BCA graduates unemployed?

Some are, as with every degree, but BCA graduates with practical skills find jobs across IT services, startups and product companies. Unemployment usually reflects missing skills, weak portfolios and limited job search effort, not the degree itself.

The entry-level market is competitive, and AI tools have raised the bar for routine coding roles, so employers look for candidates who can build and ship working software. To stand out: deploy two or three real projects, contribute to open source, complete internships, practise problem solving for online assessments, and improve communication. Graduates who start preparing in the second year, not after results, usually transition to jobs far more smoothly.

## Are BCA students called engineers?

Not by degree. BCA is a Bachelor of Computer Applications, not an engineering degree like B.E. or B.Tech, so BCA graduates are not graduate engineers in the formal sense.

In industry, however, job titles depend on the role: companies routinely hire BCA graduates as software engineers, associate engineers or developers, and the title reflects the work they do. Some government and public sector positions require an engineering degree, so check eligibility for those. What matters in most tech careers is the ability to design, build and maintain software, which BCA graduates can demonstrate through projects, internships and experience. An engineering mindset counts more than the degree name.

## Is BCA a graduation degree?

Yes. BCA is a recognised undergraduate, or graduation, degree in India, traditionally three years and now also offered as a four-year honours programme under the National Education Policy's undergraduate framework.

As a graduation degree, it makes you eligible for postgraduate study such as MCA, M.Sc and MBA, and for jobs and competitive exams requiring any bachelor's degree, including banking, civil services and many government recruitment exams. Check that your university is recognised by the University Grants Commission and that the programme follows applicable regulations. A four-year honours or research version may allow direct entry to some postgraduate and research programmes, depending on university rules.

## Do you need a CET for BCA?

It depends on the university and state. Many colleges admit BCA students on 12th marks, some universities run their own entrance tests, some states have introduced common entrance tests for BCA, and central universities use CUET UG.

Check the admission notice of each college you are considering for eligibility, exam requirements and deadlines, since rules changed after BCA came under AICTE's approval framework in some institutions. Typical eligibility is 12th pass, with some colleges requiring mathematics or computer science. If an entrance test applies, preparation usually covers mathematics, reasoning, English and basic computer awareness. Apply to a mix of entrance-based and merit-based colleges so you have options.

## What is the difference between BCA and computer science?

BCA focuses on computer applications: programming, databases, web development and software engineering with a practical slant. A B.Sc in computer science goes deeper into theory, mathematics and algorithms, and B.Tech CSE adds engineering subjects and more depth.

In practice, both lead to software careers. Computer science programmes suit students interested in algorithms, research, systems and further study in CS theory. BCA suits students who want to build applications quickly and are comfortable learning theory on their own as needed. For AI careers, either works if you strengthen mathematics, especially linear algebra, probability and statistics, alongside programming. Compare the actual syllabi of the colleges you are considering, since course names vary.

## What jobs can BCA freshers get?

BCA freshers commonly join as trainee software engineers, junior developers, web developers, QA testers, technical support engineers, data analysts, IT support executives and associate consultants, often through campus drives or IT services company hiring programmes.

Startups hire freshers for full-stack, frontend and backend roles when they show deployed projects. Internships during the final year often convert into offers. Prepare for online assessments with aptitude and coding practice, keep a GitHub profile with clear READMEs, and have a short portfolio site. Fresher roles in AI are competitive but reachable with real projects, such as a RAG app with citations or a fine-tuned model with evaluation results.

## Which companies hire BCA graduates?

Large IT services firms such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Tech Mahindra, Cognizant, Accenture and Capgemini regularly hire BCA graduates, along with global capability centres, product companies, startups and banks' technology teams.

Hiring routes include campus placements, off-campus national hiring programmes run by these companies, internships that convert to offers, and referrals. Eligibility rules vary: some programmes require minimum marks or specific degree streams, so read each notification. Startups and product companies often care more about skills and projects than degree type, which suits BCA graduates with strong portfolios. Check company career pages and professional networks regularly, since fresher hiring is seasonal, and focus applications on roles matching your projects.

## How do you find jobs after BCA?

Combine channels: campus placements, company career pages, job portals, LinkedIn, referrals from seniors and alumni, internships that convert, and startup job boards. Apply with a tailored resume and links to deployed projects.

A weekly routine helps: apply to targeted roles, message two or three people working where you want to work, practise coding and aptitude questions, and improve one portfolio project. Attend hackathons and meetups, where companies often scout talent. Prepare a short story for each project: problem, approach, your role and results. Hackathon wins, such as first prizes, make strong resume lines because they show you can deliver under pressure, so list them clearly with the event and year.

# Where is the ChatGPT archive? ChatGPT sites, detectors, how it works, agents and courses
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-archive-detectors-agents/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Archived ChatGPT chats are kept in your settings: open Settings, find the archived chats option, and select Manage to view, unarchive or delete them. Archiving hides chats from the sidebar without deleting them. I build AI products and teach students to use AI tools responsibly, so this page covers the archive, third-party ChatGPT sites, how AI detectors really work, how ChatGPT works technically, work versus personal use, ChatGPT agents and building them, and free courses including Hindi resources.

## Where is the ChatGPT archive?

In ChatGPT, open Settings, go to the General or Data controls section depending on your app version, and choose Archived chats, then Manage. You will see all archived conversations and can open, unarchive or delete them.

To archive a chat, open its menu in the sidebar and choose Archive. Archived chats keep their content and can be found through search in some versions. Archiving is useful for decluttering without losing history. If you want chats gone permanently, delete them instead. Settings locations change across app updates, so check OpenAI's help article if menus look different. For long-term records, export your data from data controls, which emails you an archive of your conversations, useful before deleting old chats.

## How do ChatGPT sites work?

Third-party "ChatGPT" websites and apps usually send your messages to OpenAI's API or other model providers, then show the responses in their own interface, sometimes adding features such as templates, document tools or extra models.

Some are legitimate products built on AI APIs; others are low-quality or scams that collect personal data, charge for access to free features, or show excessive ads. The official ChatGPT is at chatgpt.com and in OpenAI's official apps. Before using third-party sites, check who runs them, their privacy policy, and whether you really need them. Never enter passwords or sensitive data into unknown AI sites.

## How do ChatGPT detectors work?

AI text detectors estimate whether text was machine-written by looking at statistical patterns, such as how predictable each word is to a language model, often called perplexity, and how much sentence structure varies, sometimes called burstiness, or by using classifiers trained on human and AI text.

They are unreliable: they produce false positives, flagging human writing, especially by non-native English writers, and false negatives when AI text is edited or paraphrased. OpenAI withdrew its own AI text classifier in 2023 because of low accuracy. Detectors should never be used as sole proof of misconduct. Better approaches for educators include process-based assessment, drafts, oral explanations and clear AI-use policies.

## How does ChatGPT work technically?

Technically, ChatGPT is a transformer neural network that converts text into tokens and predicts the next token based on all previous tokens in the context, repeating to generate responses. Attention layers let it weigh relationships between all parts of the input.

It is pretrained on huge text datasets to learn language and knowledge, then fine-tuned with supervised examples and reinforcement learning from human feedback to follow instructions. At inference, it runs on GPU clusters, may call tools such as web search or code execution, and streams tokens back to you. Reasoning models add internal step-by-step thinking before answering.

## What is ChatGPT doing, and why does it work?

"What Is ChatGPT Doing and Why Does It Work?" is a widely read 2023 essay by Stephen Wolfram explaining that ChatGPT generates text one word at a time by predicting likely continuations, and that training on huge amounts of text captures much of the structure of language and knowledge.

The essay explains embeddings, neural networks and training in accessible terms, and argues that language has more regularity than we assumed, which is why prediction produces coherent text. It remains a good conceptual introduction, though models have since added tools, reasoning modes and multimodality. Pair it with hands-on experiments to build intuition, such as comparing answers at different temperature settings through the API, which shows the probabilistic nature of generation directly.

## When should I use ChatGPT for work vs a personal chat?

Use a work or business ChatGPT workspace, provided by your organisation, for company tasks and information, since business plans offer admin controls and data protections. Use personal accounts for personal tasks, and avoid putting confidential work data into personal accounts.

Organisations often set policies on which AI tools are approved and what data can be shared. Business workspaces may connect to company apps and keep work history separate from personal history. If your organisation does not provide an approved tool, ask before using personal AI accounts for work, especially with client data, code or personal information about others.

## What are ChatGPT agents?

ChatGPT agents are features that let ChatGPT carry out multi-step tasks for you, using tools such as a virtual browser, code execution and connected apps, rather than only answering. Agent mode can research, compare options, fill forms and create files, asking permission before important actions.

Custom GPTs are related but simpler: specialised assistants with instructions, knowledge files and optional actions that call APIs. Agents work best on clear, bounded tasks with checkable results. Supervise them, review outputs, and be careful granting access to accounts or payments, since agents can make mistakes or be misled by malicious web content.

## How do I create AI agents using ChatGPT?

For no-code assistants, create a custom GPT with instructions, knowledge files and actions connecting to APIs through OpenAPI schemas. For developer-built agents, use OpenAI's APIs and agent tools to define tools, run the agent loop and add guardrails.

Steps for a custom GPT: describe its role and tasks, upload reference documents, add actions for APIs it should call, test with real requests, and refine instructions. For developer agents: define narrow tools with clear schemas, cap steps, log actions, require approval for consequential steps, and evaluate on real tasks. Start with one narrow job before expanding.

## Is there a free ChatGPT course with a certificate?

Several free courses offer certificates or badges: Microsoft Learn's generative AI paths, Google's AI essentials resources at times, and platforms such as Coursera and edX where auditing is free and certificates may be paid or available through financial aid.

OpenAI also publishes learning resources and guides. Check each course's current terms, since free certificate offers change. Certificates help a little; employers value practical skills more: show how you used ChatGPT to complete real projects, such as research reports, automations or a small app, with documented results.

## Is there a free ChatGPT course in Hindi?

Yes. Many educators publish free ChatGPT tutorials in Hindi on YouTube, covering prompting, studying, writing and work uses, and some learning platforms offer Hindi-language AI courses. ChatGPT itself also understands and replies in Hindi.

Choose recent tutorials, since features change quickly, and prefer instructors who show real tasks rather than hype. A practical approach: learn prompting basics in Hindi, then practise with your own tasks, asking ChatGPT to explain concepts in Hindi or Hinglish. For deeper learning, combine Hindi tutorials with official English documentation, which is usually most current.

# What is ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Classic, and the best ChatGPT for students?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-business-classic-students/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT Business is OpenAI's plan for teams and small organisations, with a shared workspace, admin controls and business data kept out of model training by default. ChatGPT Classic is a custom GPT made by OpenAI that gives you a plain chat model without extra tools. This page explains both, how ChatGPT compares with Google search, how students can get the most from it, which model suits writing, what a hallucination looks like, and how to write custom instructions that make every answer more useful.

## What is ChatGPT Business?

ChatGPT Business, formerly called ChatGPT Team, is OpenAI's plan for teams. It gives each member ChatGPT with higher limits, plus a shared workspace, admin console, single sign-on and connectors to work tools.

The main reasons organisations choose it over personal accounts are control and data protection: admins manage who has access, which features and connectors are allowed, and the workspace's data is not used to train OpenAI's models by default. Teams can share custom GPTs and projects. It suits startups, agencies, college departments and small companies. Large organisations with stricter compliance needs usually choose ChatGPT Enterprise. Plan features change, so check OpenAI's pricing page for the current comparison.

## How does ChatGPT Business work?

An admin creates a workspace, invites members by email or single sign-on, and sets policies. Each member then uses ChatGPT as usual, but inside the workspace, with shared GPTs, projects and connected apps available to the team.

Admins see a console for managing seats, billing, domain verification, connector permissions and data retention settings. Members can build custom GPTs for team workflows, such as a proposal writer that follows the company template, and share them only within the workspace. Connectors let ChatGPT search approved sources such as Google Drive, SharePoint or GitHub with each user's own permissions. Personal accounts stay separate, so a member's private chats are not mixed with the workspace. Before using it for client data, check your contracts and the workspace's data settings.

## What is ChatGPT Classic?

ChatGPT Classic is a custom GPT published by OpenAI in the GPT store. It gives you a chat model without the extra capabilities of standard ChatGPT, such as web browsing, image generation or code execution.

Some people prefer it for focused writing or reasoning tasks where they do not want the assistant searching the web or calling tools, and for a cleaner, more predictable conversation. You open it from the GPTs section by searching for "ChatGPT Classic". It still follows your custom instructions and the usual usage limits. Because GPT store listings change, check whether it is available and which model it currently uses on your account.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT and ChatGPT Classic?

Standard ChatGPT can choose tools during a conversation: search the web, run code, analyse files, generate images and use memory. ChatGPT Classic is a plain conversational model without those tools.

That makes Classic predictable but limited. It cannot look up current information, so its knowledge ends at the model's training data, and it cannot calculate with code or produce files. Standard ChatGPT is better for most tasks, especially research, data analysis and anything recent. Classic can be useful when you want pure writing or brainstorming without the model deciding to browse, or when comparing how a model answers from its own knowledge alone.

## ChatGPT vs Google: which should I use?

Use Google to find specific pages, official sources, recent news, prices, local results and exact facts. Use ChatGPT to explain concepts, compare options, summarise, draft and solve problems step by step. They work best together.

Google points you to sources; ChatGPT synthesises an answer, sometimes with sources if search is on. The risk with ChatGPT is a confident answer with no reliable source; the risk with Google is spending time sifting through pages. A good workflow: ask ChatGPT to explain a topic and list what to verify, then use Google to check the key facts on official or primary sources. For exam dates, admission rules, laws and medical information, always go to the official site. Google itself now shows AI summaries, so the line between them is blurring.

## What is the best ChatGPT for students?

For most students, the free ChatGPT plan with good prompts is the best start. Use it as a tutor rather than an answer machine, and upgrade only if limits regularly block your study.

Ways to make it a tutor:

- Ask it to explain step by step and then quiz you, instead of giving answers outright.
- Use the study or tutoring mode if your plan offers one, which guides you through problems with questions.
- Create a Project for each subject with your syllabus and notes.
- Paste your own answer and ask for marking against a rubric.

Check your college's rules on AI use in assignments; submitting generated work as your own can count as misconduct.

## How does ChatGPT help students?

ChatGPT helps students understand concepts faster, practise with instant feedback, organise study plans, improve writing and debug code. The benefit comes when you use it to learn, not to skip learning.

Practical uses:

- "Explain normalisation in databases with an example from a college library system."
- "Give me ten questions on operating systems scheduling, one at a time, and grade my answers."
- "Make a two-week revision timetable for these five subjects with these exam dates."
- "Here is my paragraph; point out unclear sentences but do not rewrite it."
- "Why does this Python code give a KeyError?"

I tell first-year students the same thing in sessions: use AI tools early, but build the foundations yourself, because interviews and projects test what you understand.

## Which ChatGPT model is best for writing?

For most writing, the default model is excellent. For long, structured pieces such as reports, research summaries or technical documentation, a reasoning or thinking mode can organise arguments better. The prompt matters more than the model.

Good writing prompts state the audience, purpose, tone, length and structure, and include your own notes or draft. Ask for an outline first, agree on it, then write section by section. To keep your own voice, give ChatGPT a sample of your writing and ask it to edit lightly. For creative writing, try several drafts and combine the best parts. Always fact-check, because fluent writing can hide wrong claims.

## What is an example of a ChatGPT hallucination?

A classic example is invented citations: ask for research papers on a topic and ChatGPT may list plausible titles, authors and journals that do not exist. In a well-known 2023 US case, lawyers were sanctioned after filing a brief with court cases a chatbot had made up.

Other common hallucinations: wrong dates or numbers stated confidently, a library function that does not exist, a quote attributed to the wrong person, or details about a small company or person that sound right but are invented. Hallucinations happen because the model generates the most plausible text, not verified facts. Reduce them by turning on search, asking for sources and opening them, asking "how confident are you and what should I verify?", and checking code by running it.

## What is an example of ChatGPT custom instructions?

Custom instructions tell ChatGPT who you are and how you want answers, so you do not repeat context in every chat. Here is an example for a computer science student:

```
About me: second-year BCA student in India. I know Python and basic SQL,
learning web development with Next.js and FastAPI.

How to respond: explain like a patient senior. Give a short answer first,
then details. Use examples in Python. For code, explain each part briefly.
When I ask about facts, say what I should verify. Do not write my
assignments; help me understand and check my work.
```

Keep instructions short and specific, update them as your goals change, and test them on a few typical questions to see whether answers improve.

# Does ChatGPT need internet? OpenAI vs Claude, resumes, bans, research and function calling
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-internet-research-function-calling/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Yes, ChatGPT needs an internet connection, because it runs on OpenAI's servers rather than on your device; offline AI requires a local open-weight model instead. I build AI products across several model providers, so this page covers internet needs, how ChatGPT relates to OpenAI and differs from Claude, using it for resumes, where it is banned, schools, using it for research and Deep Research, the best models for research, and function calling.

## Does ChatGPT need internet?

Yes. ChatGPT runs on OpenAI's cloud servers, so the app and website need an internet connection to send your messages and receive answers. Without a connection, you can only view previously loaded conversations in some apps.

If you need AI offline, run an open-weight model locally with tools such as Ollama or LM Studio; OpenAI itself released open-weight gpt-oss models in 2025 that can run on capable personal hardware. Local models are private and work without connectivity, but are usually less capable than the largest cloud models and need enough RAM or GPU memory. For travel, download a small model in advance and test it before you lose connection.

## Are ChatGPT and OpenAI the same?

No. OpenAI is the company; ChatGPT is one of its products, a chat assistant built on OpenAI's GPT models. OpenAI also offers an API for developers, image and speech models, and other products.

The distinction matters for developers: the ChatGPT app has its own plans, features and data controls, while the OpenAI API is billed separately and gives programmatic access to models for building applications. Data handling also differs: according to OpenAI's policies, API data is not used for training by default, while consumer ChatGPT settings let you control whether chats help improve models. When people say they used OpenAI, they usually mean ChatGPT or the API.

## Are Claude AI and ChatGPT the same?

No. Claude is made by Anthropic, and ChatGPT by OpenAI. Both are AI assistants built on large language models, with similar uses such as writing, coding and analysis, but different models, training approaches, features and policies.

Each has strengths that change with new releases: users often compare them on coding, long-document analysis, writing style, reasoning and tool features such as web search, file analysis and agents. Many professionals use both and pick per task. For developers, both offer APIs with tool calling, so applications can switch or route between them; building with multi-provider fallback, as in RAG.NextUpgrad, reduces dependence on one vendor. Test both on your real tasks before committing.

## Should you use ChatGPT for your resume?

Yes, as an editor, not an author. ChatGPT is useful for tightening bullet points, matching wording to a job description, fixing grammar and suggesting structure, but the content must be your real experience, in your voice.

Good prompts: paste one bullet and ask for three stronger versions with action verbs and measurable results; or paste a job description and ask which of your real skills to emphasise. Never let it invent achievements, numbers or tools you have not used, since interviewers will ask about them. Remove personal details such as phone numbers before pasting. Generic AI phrasing is easy to spot, so edit outputs until they sound like you.

## Where is ChatGPT banned?

ChatGPT is not officially available in some countries, including China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, because of OpenAI's supported-country list or local restrictions. Italy briefly blocked it in 2023 over privacy concerns before access was restored.

Beyond countries, many organisations restrict ChatGPT: some companies block it to protect confidential data, some schools and exam boards limit its use, and regulated industries may allow only approved enterprise versions. OpenAI publishes a list of supported countries and territories, which changes over time. Using VPNs to bypass restrictions may violate terms of service or local laws. If you work with sensitive data, follow your organisation's AI policy rather than assuming general availability means permission.

## Should ChatGPT be banned in schools?

Most educators now favour guided use over blanket bans. Bans are hard to enforce, miss chances to teach AI literacy, and widen gaps between students with and without access at home. Clear rules work better than prohibition.

Some school systems banned ChatGPT in early 2023 and later reversed course. Effective policies define when AI is allowed, such as brainstorming or feedback, and when it is not, such as graded essays written in class; require students to disclose AI use; and redesign assessments with oral explanations, in-class work and personal reflection. Teaching students to question AI outputs, check sources and protect privacy prepares them better than pretending the tools do not exist.

## How do you use ChatGPT for research?

Use ChatGPT to explore a topic, generate search terms, summarise papers you provide, explain methods, and draft outlines. Turn on web search for current information, and always check claims against the original sources it cites.

A workflow: ask for an overview and key debates; request search queries and important authors; upload papers and ask for structured summaries with page references; compare findings across papers in a table; then verify each important claim yourself. Watch for fabricated citations, especially without web search. For academic work, follow your institution's rules on AI use and disclosure, and never present AI-generated text as your own analysis.

## When should you use ChatGPT Deep Research?

Use Deep Research for questions that need many sources and synthesis, such as market overviews, literature scans, comparing products or policies, or background research before writing. It browses the web for several minutes and returns a cited report.

Do not use it for quick facts, simple definitions or tasks where you already have the documents, since normal chat or file analysis is faster. Write a specific brief: the question, scope, time period, regions, sources to prefer and the format you want. Review the report critically: check key citations, look for missing perspectives, and ask follow-up questions. Deep Research saves hours of searching, but it does not replace expert judgement.

## Which ChatGPT model is best for research?

For research, use ChatGPT's reasoning models with web search enabled, and Deep Research for multi-source reports. Reasoning models think before answering, which helps with analysis, comparisons and technical explanations.

Model names and options change frequently, so choose by capability rather than name: the strongest available reasoning model for complex analysis, a faster model for quick lookups and drafting, and Deep Research when you need breadth across many sources. Whatever the model, accuracy depends on sources, so ask for citations, open them, and verify. For research on your own documents, upload them to a Project so answers are grounded in your material, and keep a log of prompts and sources for reproducibility.

## What is function calling in OpenAI's models?

Function calling lets developers describe functions to an OpenAI model with names, descriptions and JSON schemas. When useful, the model returns a structured request to call a function with arguments, and the application runs it and sends back the result.

OpenAI introduced function calling in 2023, and it underpins tools, agents and structured outputs. For example, a support app defines a get_order_status function; when a user asks where their order is, the model returns a call with the order ID, the app queries its database, and the model writes the answer. The model never executes code itself. Validate arguments, restrict permissions and handle errors, since models can produce wrong or unexpected calls.

# ChatGPT release date, limits, lag, hallucinations, history, settings and video
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-limits-lag-history-video/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


OpenAI released ChatGPT to the public on 30 November 2022 as a free research preview, and it has since grown into an assistant with usage limits, memory, settings and media features. I build AI products that ground answers in sources, such as RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page covers ChatGPT's release, why it has limits, why it lags and hallucinates, deleting chats and history, finding settings and archived chats, and whether ChatGPT can make or watch videos.

## When was ChatGPT released to the public?

ChatGPT was released to the public on 30 November 2022 as a free research preview by OpenAI, built on a model from the GPT-3.5 series fine-tuned for conversation with reinforcement learning from human feedback.

It spread faster than almost any consumer app before it, and competing assistants followed quickly, such as Google's Bard, later renamed Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude. OpenAI launched the paid ChatGPT Plus plan in February 2023 and GPT-4 in March 2023, followed by voice, image understanding, image generation, search, memory and agent features over the next years. The original research preview framing explains the early warnings about mistakes, which remain relevant today: always verify important answers.

## Why does ChatGPT have limits?

ChatGPT limits messages because every response uses expensive computing power, especially on advanced models. Limits share capacity fairly among users, prevent abuse and differ by plan, with free users getting fewer messages on the most capable models.

There are several kinds of limits: message caps per time window, which reset after a few hours; context limits, the maximum text a conversation can hold; file upload limits; and limits on features such as image generation or deep research. When you hit a cap, ChatGPT may switch you to a smaller model until it resets. To reduce hitting limits, write clear, complete prompts, start new chats for new topics and use lighter models for simple tasks.

## Why does ChatGPT lag so much?

ChatGPT usually lags because of very long conversations, heavy server load at peak times, slower reasoning models, browser issues or a weak internet connection. Long chats force the page to render a lot of text, which slows browsers noticeably.

Fixes: start a new chat for new topics, since long threads slow both the interface and responses; refresh the page or try the desktop or mobile app; disable browser extensions that modify pages; clear the cache; and check the OpenAI status page for outages. Reasoning models deliberately think before answering, so pauses there are expected. If hanging happens only on one device or network, test another to isolate the cause. Updating your browser also helps, since older versions handle heavy pages poorly.

## Why does ChatGPT hallucinate so much?

ChatGPT hallucinates because language models generate likely-sounding text rather than looking up verified facts. When it lacks knowledge, training and evaluation often reward confident guesses over admitting uncertainty, so it may invent details, citations or numbers.

Hallucinations increase with obscure topics, recent events, exact figures, long quotes and requests for sources. Reduce them by enabling search so answers cite live sources, asking it to say when it is unsure, providing documents to answer from, and verifying claims in the original sources. Grounding helps most: RAG.NextUpgrad answers from retrieved documents with citations and a confidence gate that declines when evidence is weak, a pattern that cuts invented answers. Treat ChatGPT as a draft partner, not an authority.

## Can you delete ChatGPT history?

Yes. Delete a single chat from its menu in the sidebar, or remove everything with the delete all chats option in Settings. Deleted chats disappear from your history immediately and are scheduled for removal from OpenAI's systems.

OpenAI's help centre explains its retention timelines, including exceptions for security or legal obligations, so check it for current details. For conversations you do not want saved at all, use Temporary Chat, which does not appear in history or create memories. Memory is separate from chat history: review and delete saved memories under Settings, Personalization. You can also turn off the setting that lets your content improve models, under Data controls, and export your data before deleting.

## Should you delete ChatGPT?

Delete your ChatGPT account only if you no longer need it or have privacy concerns that settings cannot address. Deleting an account is permanent, removes your chats and cannot be undone, so export your data first.

Alternatives often meet privacy goals without deletion: turn off model training on your content, use Temporary Chat, delete specific conversations, clear memory and avoid sharing sensitive personal, financial or health details. If you are deleting the mobile app only, your account and history remain on the web. Students and professionals should also check institutional rules about AI tools for confidential work. To delete the account, use the delete account option in Settings and follow the confirmation steps.

## Where do you find ChatGPT settings?

On the web and desktop app, click your profile name or icon at the bottom of the left sidebar, then choose Settings. On mobile, open the sidebar menu and tap your name or profile icon.

Settings are grouped into sections such as General, for theme and language; Personalization, for custom instructions and memory; Data controls, for training preferences, export and archived chats; Security, for multi-factor authentication; and Account or subscription details. Voice options and connected apps have their own sections. The interface changes often, so if a menu has moved, search OpenAI's help centre for the setting by name. Reviewing personalization and data controls once is worthwhile for every regular user.

## Where do you find ChatGPT archived chats?

Open Settings, find Archived chats in the Data controls or General section, and select Manage. A list of archived conversations appears, where you can open, unarchive or delete them.

Archiving hides a chat from the sidebar without deleting it, which keeps history tidy while preserving useful conversations. To archive, open a chat's menu in the sidebar and choose Archive. Unarchiving returns the chat to the sidebar with its full history. Archiving suits finished projects you may need again, while deletion suits chats you never want back. On mobile, the same option sits in Settings. If you cannot find it, update the app, since menu locations change between releases.

## Can ChatGPT generate video?

ChatGPT itself focuses on text, code and images. OpenAI's video generation lives in Sora, a separate app and website that creates short videos from text prompts or images, with availability that varies by country and plan.

Inside ChatGPT, you can still plan videos: write scripts, storyboards, shot lists, captions and prompts for video tools, and generate still images for thumbnails or frames. Other video generators include Google's Veo, Runway and Kling. Generated video should be labelled where platforms require it, and you should avoid realistic depictions of real people without consent. For editing existing footage, ChatGPT can write FFmpeg commands or suggest cuts, which you then run in your own editor.

## Can you send ChatGPT a video?

Video support is limited and varies by app and plan. A reliable approach is to share key frames as images, or the transcript or audio, which ChatGPT handles well. On mobile, voice mode with video lets ChatGPT see your live camera feed.

For analysis of recorded clips, extract frames at regular intervals with a tool such as FFmpeg and upload the most informative ones, along with context about what happens between them. For talks or lectures, upload the transcript; YouTube often provides one. Gemini handles uploaded video natively and may suit long clips better. Avoid uploading private recordings of other people without consent, and check file size limits before uploading anything large.

# What is ChatGPT PDF? Chat with PDF tools, upload limits, and exporting chats to PDF
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-pdf-chat-with-pdf/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


"ChatGPT PDF" usually means uploading a PDF to ChatGPT, or to a chat-with-PDF tool, and asking questions about it: summaries, explanations, specific facts or comparisons. Behind the scenes, the tool extracts the text and uses retrieval or the model's long context to answer. I built the OCR and Speech Workspace, which does document-scoped RAG with page citations, so this page covers how chat-with-PDF works, using and building one, ChatGPT upload problems and limits, making PDFs, exporting chats, and the ChatGPT API endpoint.

## What is ChatGPT PDF?

It refers to using ChatGPT with PDF files: uploading a PDF and asking questions, summarising it, extracting tables or comparing documents. Separate "chat with PDF" websites and features in Adobe Acrobat, Claude and Google's NotebookLM do the same.

ChatGPT can also create PDFs, such as reports or formatted documents, by writing them with its code tools. The quality of PDF chat depends on text extraction: digital PDFs with real text work well, while scanned PDFs need OCR, and complex tables or charts may be misread. Always check important answers against the page itself, because summaries can miss qualifications or misread numbers.

## How does chat with PDF work?

The tool extracts text from the PDF, using OCR for scanned pages, splits it into chunks, and when you ask a question, retrieves the most relevant chunks and gives them to a language model to answer. Good tools cite the page each answer came from.

Some tools instead put the whole document into a long-context model, which works for shorter PDFs. Retrieval scales better to long documents and many files. Quality depends on parsing tables and layout, chunking along sections, combining keyword and semantic search, and instructing the model to answer only from the retrieved text. The OCR and Speech Workspace uses page-batched OCR with Mistral, then retrieval scoped to the chosen document, with page citations on every answer.

## How do I use chat with PDF?

Upload the PDF to ChatGPT or a chat-with-PDF tool, wait for processing, then ask specific questions. Ask for page references so you can verify answers, and break big tasks into smaller questions.

Effective prompts:

- "Summarise this report in ten bullet points with page numbers."
- "What are the eligibility criteria on page 4? Quote them exactly."
- "List every deadline mentioned in this document in a table."
- "Explain section 3 in simple language for a first-year student."
- "Compare the two uploaded contracts' termination clauses."

Check numbers, dates and legal wording against the original, and avoid uploading confidential documents to services whose data policies you have not reviewed.

## How do I make my own chat with PDF app?

Build a small RAG pipeline: extract text from PDFs with a parser or OCR, chunk by sections with page numbers, embed the chunks, store them in a vector index, retrieve relevant chunks for each question, and prompt a model to answer with citations.

A minimal stack: Python, a PDF parser such as PyMuPDF, an OCR service for scans, an embedding model, a vector store such as pgvector or Chroma, a language model API, and a simple web interface with FastAPI and a front end. Then improve: hybrid keyword and vector search, a reranker, a refusal rule when evidence is weak, and an evaluation set of questions with known answers. Start with ten real documents from your target users.

## Why can't I upload a PDF to ChatGPT?

Common causes are file size or page limits, reaching your plan's upload cap, a password-protected or corrupted PDF, a slow or interrupted connection, browser extensions, or a temporary service problem. The error message usually hints at which.

Fixes to try:

- Check the file opens normally and is not password protected.
- Compress large PDFs or split them into smaller files.
- Wait if you have hit an upload limit, or check your plan.
- Refresh, try another browser, the app, or disable extensions.
- Check OpenAI's status page for incidents.

For scanned PDFs that upload but give poor answers, run OCR first so the file contains real text.

## How many PDFs can I upload to ChatGPT?

ChatGPT limits the number of files per message, per conversation and over time, as well as file size, and the limits vary by plan. OpenAI's help centre lists current values, which have changed over time.

Free plans have tighter upload limits than paid plans. Custom GPTs and Projects let you attach a set of reference files that persist across chats, each with its own limits. For large collections, such as hundreds of documents, a dedicated RAG system or tools such as NotebookLM are often better suited than uploading files one conversation at a time. Check the official file uploads FAQ before planning a workflow around specific limits.

## How long does ChatGPT take to make a PDF?

Usually seconds to a minute. ChatGPT writes the content, then generates a downloadable PDF file with its code tools. Longer documents, images, tables or complex formatting take longer, and busy periods can slow responses.

For best results, first agree on the content and structure in the chat, then ask: "Create a PDF of this with headings, a table and page numbers." If the file is not generated or the link expires, ask it to regenerate. For professional layouts, it is often better to have ChatGPT produce the content and format it yourself in Google Docs or Word, then export to PDF.

## How do I convert a ChatGPT chat to PDF on mobile?

The simplest way is to share the chat as a link, open it in your phone's browser, then use the browser's print option and choose "Save as PDF". You can also copy individual responses into a document and export that.

On Android in Chrome, use the menu, Share, then Print and Save as PDF. On iPhone, open the shared link in Safari, tap Share, then Print, and save the preview as a PDF, or use "Save to Files" where available. To export all your data, use ChatGPT's data controls export, which emails an archive. Remove personal details before sharing any chat publicly.

## How do I export a WhatsApp chat to PDF?

WhatsApp exports chats as a text file, with or without media, from the chat's menu: More, then Export chat. Open the text file in Google Docs or Word, format it, and export it as a PDF.

Steps:

- Open the chat, tap the menu, choose More, then Export chat.
- Choose with or without media; media is attached as separate files.
- Save to Google Drive or email it to yourself.
- Open the text file in a document editor and export as PDF.

Third-party apps promise one-tap PDF exports, but they get access to private conversations, so prefer the manual method for sensitive chats and get consent before sharing others' messages.

## What is the API URL for ChatGPT gpt-3.5-turbo?

The Chat Completions endpoint is `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`, called with a POST request containing the model name, such as gpt-3.5-turbo, and a list of messages, with your API key in the Authorization header.

gpt-3.5-turbo is now a legacy model; newer models are cheaper or more capable, and OpenAI also offers the newer Responses API. For PDFs, current OpenAI APIs accept file inputs directly for supported models, so you can send a PDF and ask questions about it. Keep API keys in environment variables, never in front-end code, and check the API reference for current models and endpoints.
