# Why does ChatGPT pick 73? Plus: is ChatGPT Plus worth it, and why it is slow
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-picks-73-plus-and-speed/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT picks 73, 17, 37 or 42 when you ask for a random number because language models predict the most likely next token, and in human writing those numbers are the ones people choose when they try to sound random. The model is reproducing our bias, not rolling dice. This page also covers ChatGPT Plus: whether you can get it free, what it offers, how it compares with Go and Pro, whether to buy it, and why ChatGPT can be slow on your laptop or get slower during a chat.

## Why does ChatGPT pick 73?

Because it is predicting what a person would most likely write, not generating randomness. In human text, "random" picks cluster on numbers that feel random, such as those ending in 7 and odd primes like 37 and 73, and the model learned that pattern.

When you ask "pick a number between 1 and 100", the model assigns a probability to every possible answer. Training on human writing, plus tuning to give confident answers, concentrates that probability on a few favourites. Sampling at the default temperature then picks one of those favourites most of the time. Ask in a fresh chat and you will often see the same few numbers. That is a useful reminder of how these models work: they produce the most plausible text, which is not the same as the most correct or most random.

## Why does ChatGPT always pick 17?

For a 1 to 20 range, 17 plays the same role 73 plays for 1 to 100: it is the number people most often name when asked for a random one, so it dominates the model's predictions. Humans avoid round numbers and the edges of a range, and odd primes feel "more random".

If you need real randomness, do not ask the model to imagine it. Ask ChatGPT to run code instead, for example "use Python's random module to pick a number from 1 to 100", which uses a pseudo-random generator rather than the model's preferences. In your own apps, generate random values in code and pass them to the model if needed. The same lesson applies to anything that must be unbiased, such as shuffling a list, sampling test data or choosing a winner: use code, then let the model explain the result.

## Where is ChatGPT Plus free?

ChatGPT Plus is a paid plan and is not generally free in any country. OpenAI has run limited promotions, for example offers for students in some markets, and in India it offered ChatGPT Go, a lighter paid plan, free for a period to eligible users.

Promotions are announced by OpenAI and claimed inside ChatGPT or through official partners, never through third-party sites. Beware of "free Plus" offers that ask for your login, sell shared accounts or require an app download: they risk your account and your data, and shared accounts break OpenAI's terms. The free tier is also more capable than many people assume, with access to strong models within limits, so try it seriously before paying.

## What does ChatGPT Plus offer?

ChatGPT Plus offers higher usage limits than the free tier, access to more capable models and reasoning modes, and more use of features such as deep research, image generation, advanced voice, file analysis, agent mode and Codex.

The practical gain is fewer interruptions: on the free tier you can run out of the best model and fall back to a lighter one, while Plus lets you work with stronger models for longer. Exact limits and the feature list change often, so check OpenAI's pricing page for the current details. Plus is an individual plan; teams use business plans with admin controls and data protections.

## Should I buy ChatGPT Plus?

Buy it if the free tier's limits regularly interrupt work that matters to you, such as daily coding, research or writing, and the time saved is worth the cost. If you use ChatGPT a few times a week for quick questions, the free tier is enough.

A simple test: for two weeks, note every time the free tier blocked you or gave a weaker answer that cost you time. If it happens daily, Plus is likely worth it. Also compare the alternatives: Go if you mostly need higher limits on everyday tasks, and the free tiers of Claude, Gemini and Copilot, which you can combine at no cost. For students, the biggest improvement usually comes from better prompts and checking answers, not from a paid plan.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT Go and Plus?

ChatGPT Go is a lower-cost paid plan with higher limits than the free tier for everyday features such as messages, image generation and file uploads. Plus adds access to more capable models and reasoning modes, more advanced features and higher limits again.

Go was launched first in India and then expanded to other countries, aimed at people who use ChatGPT daily but do not need the most advanced models or agent features. Plus suits people who need deep research, stronger reasoning, agent mode or Codex regularly. Because OpenAI adjusts what each plan includes, compare them on the official pricing page for your country before choosing.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT Plus and Pro?

Pro is the top individual plan for very heavy professional use. It has much higher limits than Plus and access to OpenAI's most capable reasoning modes, with priority access to new features. Plus is the mainstream paid plan.

Choose Pro only if you hit Plus limits constantly on work that earns money, or you need the strongest reasoning for hard technical, scientific or analytical problems every day. For almost every student and most developers, Plus is the sensible ceiling. Pro does not make ChatGPT infallible; it gives more capacity and the strongest models, but you still need to verify answers.

## Why is ChatGPT slow?

ChatGPT is slow when OpenAI's servers are under heavy load, when you use a reasoning model that thinks before answering, or when your conversation is very long. Network problems and browser issues add to it.

Check these first:

- **Status**: OpenAI's status page shows outages and degraded performance.
- **Model**: reasoning modes spend seconds to minutes thinking on purpose; use a faster mode for simple tasks.
- **Peak hours**: responses slow when many users are active, and free-tier users feel it first.
- **Chat length**: very long chats take longer to process and render.
- **Network**: VPNs, proxies and weak Wi-Fi delay streaming responses.

If only one chat is slow, start a new one with a short summary of the earlier context.

## Why is ChatGPT so slow on my laptop?

Usually because the browser tab is struggling, not the AI. Very long conversations with code blocks and images create a heavy page, and extensions, low memory or an outdated browser make it worse.

Fixes that work:

- Start a new chat; long chats are the most common cause.
- Close other heavy tabs and apps to free memory.
- Disable extensions, especially ad blockers and page modifiers, or try a private window.
- Update the browser, or try the ChatGPT desktop app.
- Clear the site's cache and cookies if the page behaves oddly.
- Turn off a VPN or switch networks to rule out connection issues.

If ChatGPT is fast on your phone but slow on your laptop, the problem is local to the laptop's browser.

## Why does ChatGPT slow down during a conversation?

Because every reply processes the whole conversation so far. As a chat grows, the model has more text to read before answering, and the browser has more messages to render, so each response takes longer.

Long chats also get worse, not only slower: early instructions can be lost or weakened when the context is very long, and the model may mix up details from different parts of the conversation. Keep one chat per task. When a chat gets long, ask ChatGPT for a short summary of decisions and facts, copy it into a new chat, and continue there. For ongoing projects, use a Project in ChatGPT with files and instructions, so you do not need one endless chat.

# What is a ChatGPT project? Using, sharing and collaborating, plus Atlas, plugins, training
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-projects-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


A ChatGPT project is a workspace that groups related chats, uploaded files and custom instructions, so ChatGPT keeps the same context across many conversations about one piece of work, such as a semester course, a client account or an app you are building. Projects make long-running work far more organised than scattered chats. I build AI products and use AI workspaces daily, so this page covers projects, using and sharing them, collaborating, ChatGPT Atlas, how ChatGPT is trained, plugins, and fixing ChatGPT when it stops responding.

## What is a ChatGPT project?

A ChatGPT project is a folder-like workspace in ChatGPT that holds chats, files and instructions for one topic. Chats inside a project can use the project's files and instructions, and ChatGPT can reference earlier project conversations, so you do not repeat background every time.

Typical uses: studying a subject with lecture notes uploaded, managing a client with their brief and documents, planning an event, writing a long report, or developing software with specifications. Projects are similar in purpose to Claude's projects and Gemini's Gems with files: reusable context for focused, ongoing work. For students, one project per subject, with the syllabus and notes uploaded, turns ChatGPT into a consistent study assistant that remembers the course context across weeks.

## How do I use projects in ChatGPT?

Create a new project from the sidebar, name it, add files such as notes or documents, write project instructions describing the goal, audience and preferred style, then start chats inside it or move existing chats into it.

Tips:

- Keep each project focused on one goal.
- Write instructions like a brief: role, context, rules and output format.
- Upload only relevant, up-to-date files and remove outdated ones.
- Name chats clearly so you can find them later.
- Ask ChatGPT to summarise progress periodically within the project.

Projects work best when instructions and files are curated, not dumped.

## What is the difference between a ChatGPT project and a chat?

A chat is a single conversation; once you start a new chat, earlier context is not automatically included, apart from any memory features. A project groups many chats with shared files and instructions, so context persists across conversations on the same topic.

Use regular chats for quick, unrelated questions. Use projects when you will return to the same work repeatedly, need consistent instructions, or rely on reference documents. Projects also keep your sidebar organised. For one-time tasks, a project adds unnecessary setup; for semester-long courses or ongoing client work, it saves significant time.

## Can a ChatGPT project be shared?

Yes, on supported plans, OpenAI offers shared projects, letting you invite collaborators who can use the same files, instructions and project chats. Availability and permissions depend on your plan and workspace settings, so check OpenAI's current help article.

Before sharing, review what is inside: files, chat history and instructions may contain information others should not see. For team accounts, administrators can control sharing. If shared projects are not available on your plan, you can share individual chats through links, or create a custom GPT with the same instructions and files for others to use.

## How do I share a project in ChatGPT?

Open the project, use its share or invite option, and add collaborators by email or link according to your plan's options, choosing their permissions. Collaborators then see the project's files, instructions and shared chats.

If you only need to share results, share a specific chat link instead, which gives read access to that conversation. Remember that shared content may include uploaded files and details from conversations. For sensitive work, use team or enterprise plans with admin controls and data protections rather than personal accounts.

## How do I collaborate using a ChatGPT project?

Agree on the project's purpose, keep shared instructions and files current, use clear chat names for different workstreams, and record decisions in a summary document inside the project so everyone works from the same context.

Collaboration tips:

- Assign an owner who maintains instructions and files.
- Keep one "status" chat or document summarising decisions.
- Upload final versions only, with dates in file names.
- Review AI-generated content before sharing it outside the team.
- Avoid uploading confidential data unless your plan's data controls allow it.

Projects support teamwork, but human review and clear ownership keep the work accurate.

## What is ChatGPT Atlas?

ChatGPT Atlas is OpenAI's web browser with ChatGPT built in, launched in 2025, starting with macOS. It lets you ask ChatGPT about the page you are viewing, use optional browser memories for context, and run agent mode to complete tasks on websites.

Atlas integrates assistance directly into browsing: summarising articles, comparing products across tabs, drafting replies and filling forms with agent mode under your supervision. As with any AI browser, review privacy settings, be careful with agent access to logged-in accounts, and watch for prompt injection on untrusted websites. Check OpenAI's site for current platform availability. Atlas is part of a wider shift towards AI browsers, alongside Copilot in Edge and Gemini in Chrome, where assistants work directly on the pages you visit.

## How is ChatGPT trained?

ChatGPT's models are trained in stages: pretraining on large amounts of text to learn language and knowledge by predicting the next token, then supervised fine-tuning on example conversations written by people, then reinforcement learning from human feedback, where people rank responses and the model learns to prefer helpful, safe answers.

Newer models add training for reasoning, tool use, safety and multimodal inputs, and draw on licensed, public and human-created data. Training happens before release, so models have a knowledge cut-off; web search and file uploads supply newer or private information at use time. OpenAI's system cards describe training and safety work for each model.

## What were ChatGPT plugins?

ChatGPT plugins, introduced in 2023, let ChatGPT call external services, such as travel booking, shopping and data tools, through APIs. OpenAI phased them out in 2024 in favour of custom GPTs with actions, and later apps and connectors integrated into ChatGPT.

The idea lives on: GPTs can call APIs through actions, and connectors link ChatGPT to services such as cloud storage and business apps. For developers, building on current options means defining actions with OpenAPI schemas or using newer app frameworks OpenAI provides. Old plugin tutorials are outdated, so follow current documentation.

## Why is ChatGPT not responding?

ChatGPT may not respond because of service outages, high demand, usage limits, long conversations, large uploads, browser extensions, network problems, or an outdated app. Check OpenAI's status page first to rule out incidents.

Fixes:

- Refresh the page or restart the app.
- Start a new chat if the conversation is very long.
- Disable extensions or try a private window.
- Clear the browser cache or update the app.
- Check your internet connection or switch networks.
- Wait if you have hit a usage limit.

If one model fails, switching to another model sometimes works while issues are resolved.

# ChatGPT questions answered: launch, agents, PPT files, water use, sources, and Astra
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-questions-answered/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT, OpenAI's AI assistant, launched on 30 November 2022 and became one of the fastest-growing consumer apps ever. Today it writes, analyses files, searches the web, creates images and documents, and runs agent tasks. I build AI products across several model providers, so this page answers common ChatGPT questions: its launch, response length, official sites, making PowerPoint files, how agents work and building your own, water use, where its information comes from, Apple Intelligence, and claims about "ChatGPT 6 Astra".

## When was ChatGPT launched?

OpenAI launched ChatGPT as a free research preview on 30 November 2022. It reached an estimated 100 million users within about two months, making it one of the fastest-adopted consumer applications in history.

It was first based on a model from the GPT-3.5 series, fine-tuned for conversation with reinforcement learning from human feedback. Paid plans, GPT-4 access, plugins, image generation, voice, custom GPTs, search and agent features followed over the next years. ChatGPT's launch triggered the wave of generative AI products and investment that shaped the technology industry since. For students and developers, it also changed how people learn to code, research topics and draft documents, which is why AI literacy is now treated as a basic skill.

## How long can ChatGPT answers and chats be?

ChatGPT's response length is limited by the model's output token limit and the conversation's context window, both of which vary by model and plan. Long answers may stop partway; asking it to continue usually resumes them.

For long documents, ask for an outline first, then generate section by section, or use Canvas for long-form editing. Very long conversations eventually exceed the context window, and earlier details may be forgotten or summarised; start a new chat with a summary when that happens. Developers using the API set maximum output tokens explicitly and pay for input and output tokens.

## What are the official ChatGPT sites?

The official ChatGPT site is chatgpt.com, and OpenAI's official apps are available in Apple's App Store, Google Play and as desktop apps for macOS and Windows from OpenAI. OpenAI's company site is openai.com.

Many websites and apps use "ChatGPT" in their names without being OpenAI products; some are legitimate tools using OpenAI's API, while others are scams that collect data or payments. Check the publisher name in app stores, avoid entering passwords or payment details on look-alike sites, and use official sources for downloads and subscriptions.

## Can ChatGPT make a PPT?

Yes. ChatGPT can generate PowerPoint files by writing and running code, producing a downloadable .pptx with slides, titles, bullet points and simple layouts, and its agent mode can create presentations as part of larger tasks.

For best results, agree on the outline first, then ask for the deck with specifics: number of slides, audience, style, speaker notes and any data or charts. Generated decks usually need design polish in PowerPoint or Google Slides. Check facts and figures carefully, and add your own visuals and examples so the presentation reflects your voice. If your college or company has a slide template, upload it and ask ChatGPT to follow its layout to save formatting time.

## How do ChatGPT agents work?

ChatGPT's agent mode gives the model a virtual computer with a browser, terminal and connectors, so it can plan and carry out multi-step tasks, such as researching options, filling forms or creating documents, while asking permission before consequential actions.

It combines web browsing, code execution and integration with connected apps, deciding which tool to use at each step and showing its progress. You can interrupt, take over or redirect at any time. As with any agent, results need review, sites may block automated browsing, and prompt injection on web pages is a risk, so avoid giving it sensitive credentials or unrestricted access.

## Can you create AI agents in ChatGPT?

You can create custom GPTs in ChatGPT with instructions, knowledge files and actions that call external APIs, which act as specialised assistants. For developers, OpenAI also provides tools and APIs to build agents with tool use, orchestration and evaluation.

A custom GPT suits repeatable assistants, such as a study helper or a company FAQ bot. For agents that run workflows across systems, use OpenAI's developer tools, other agent frameworks such as LangGraph, or automation platforms such as n8n. Start with a narrow task, define tools carefully, add approval steps, and test with real examples before sharing.

## Why does ChatGPT use water?

ChatGPT runs in data centres whose servers produce heat, and many data centres use water for cooling, directly through evaporative cooling or indirectly through electricity generation. Each query therefore has a small water and energy footprint.

In 2025, OpenAI's chief executive estimated that an average ChatGPT query uses a tiny fraction of a teaspoon of water and a fraction of a watt-hour of energy, though methods and assumptions vary across studies. Training large models and generating images or video use much more. Totals matter at global scale, which is why companies report on efficiency, renewable energy and water recycling.

## Where does ChatGPT get its information?

ChatGPT's knowledge comes from training on large datasets, including publicly available internet text, licensed data and data created by human trainers, up to a cut-off date. When search is used, it also retrieves current web pages and cites them. Files you upload are another source.

It does not look facts up in a database by default; it generates answers from learned patterns, which is why it can be confidently wrong. Use search mode and ask for sources when facts matter, and check the cited pages. For your own organisation's information, grounded systems such as RAG, which answer only from your documents with citations, are more reliable.

## Can you use Apple AI like ChatGPT?

Partly. Apple Intelligence offers writing tools, summaries, image features and a more capable Siri on supported devices, focused on personal tasks and privacy. For open-ended conversations and broad questions, it can hand requests to ChatGPT through Apple's integration, with your permission.

So Apple Intelligence is not a direct ChatGPT replacement, but it covers many everyday tasks inside apps, and the ChatGPT integration fills gaps. You can use the integration without an OpenAI account, or sign in to use your plan's features. Supported devices, languages and regions are limited, so check Apple's availability list.

## What is ChatGPT 6 Astra?

Treat "ChatGPT 6 Astra" claims with caution: OpenAI's official announcements are the reliable source for its model names and releases, and the "Astra" name is best known from Google DeepMind's Project Astra, a research prototype of a universal AI assistant that sees and hears through a device's camera and microphone.

Rumoured model names often spread on social media and video channels before or without any official confirmation, sometimes mixing names from different companies. Check openai.com and OpenAI's release notes for current ChatGPT models, and Google DeepMind's pages for Project Astra. Be wary of sites selling access to unannounced "next" models, which are often scams.

# Will ChatGPT shut down? Outages, Projects and RAG, images, watermarks, health and energy
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-shutdown-projects-images/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT is not shutting down: OpenAI keeps developing it, although individual models are retired and replaced over time. Most problems people hit, outages, image failures or weak answers, have specific causes and fixes. I build AI products with multi-provider fallback, such as RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page covers what ChatGPT is best for, shutdown rumours, outages, Projects and whether they use RAG, image generation and watermarks, medical advice, and ChatGPT's environmental impact.

## What is ChatGPT best used for?

ChatGPT is best for drafting and editing text, explaining concepts, brainstorming, summarising documents, writing and debugging code, analysing data with code, translating, and planning tasks. It is a strong first-draft and thinking partner.

It is weaker where precision and accountability matter without verification: exact citations, recent facts without search, legal or medical decisions, and arithmetic in long reasoning chains. Use web search or uploaded documents for current or specific information, and check important claims. Students get the most value by asking it to explain and quiz rather than to produce finished assignments. Professionals benefit from giving it context, examples and a clear format for the output they want.

## Will ChatGPT shut down?

There is no sign that ChatGPT will shut down. OpenAI continues to release new models and features, and ChatGPT has hundreds of millions of weekly users. Rumours usually come from model retirements, outages or misleading social media posts.

What does change is which models are available: OpenAI retires older models, as it did when GPT-4 was removed from ChatGPT in 2025, and introduces new defaults. Features also move between plans. If your workflow depends on a specific model's behaviour, keep prompts and outputs documented so you can adapt. For applications, build in flexibility to switch providers, since any service can change terms or availability, which is why multi-provider fallback is good engineering.

## Is ChatGPT down right now?

Check OpenAI's official status page first: it lists incidents affecting ChatGPT, the API and specific features such as image generation or voice. Outage trackers and social media can confirm whether others see the same problem.

If the status page shows no incident, the problem is likely local: refresh, log out and in, clear the site's cache, disable browser extensions, try a private window or another browser, update the app, or switch networks and turn off VPNs. Partial outages often affect one feature, such as file uploads or images, while text chat works. During major incidents, wait rather than retrying repeatedly, and use an alternative assistant for urgent work.

## What are ChatGPT Projects?

Projects in ChatGPT are workspaces that group related chats, uploaded files and custom instructions around one topic, such as a course, research paper or product. Chats inside a project share that context automatically.

Use a project for ongoing work: upload reference documents once, set instructions such as tone or format, and start new chats that already know the background. Projects can also reference earlier chats within the same project, which helps continuity. They are useful for students organising subjects and professionals running long tasks. Keep files current, remove outdated versions to avoid confusion, and avoid uploading sensitive data unless your plan and settings meet your privacy requirements.

## Do ChatGPT Projects use RAG?

Effectively, yes. When project files are too large to fit into the conversation, ChatGPT searches them and pulls relevant passages into context, a retrieval-augmented approach. Smaller files may be read more fully.

This explains common behaviour: ChatGPT may miss details in a long file if its search does not retrieve the right section, and it answers better when you name the document or section you mean. For precise work, ask it to quote the passage it used, and verify. For applications needing guaranteed coverage, auditable citations and control over chunking and ranking, build your own RAG pipeline, as I did with RAG.NextUpgrad, rather than relying on a chat product's retrieval.

## Why is ChatGPT not generating images?

Common reasons: you reached the image limit for your plan, the request conflicts with content policies, image generation is temporarily degraded, or the chat or model you are using does not support it. Error messages usually hint at which.

Fixes: check the status page for image incidents; start a new chat and ask explicitly to create an image; rephrase prompts that might be read as violating policy, such as requests involving real people or copyrighted characters; wait for limits to reset; and update the app or try the web version. Long, complex prompts can time out, so simplify first, then refine with follow-up edits. If Gemini fails similarly, the causes and fixes are much the same.

## Which ChatGPT is best for images?

Use the image generation built into ChatGPT, which runs on OpenAI's latest GPT image models and is available across plans with different limits. Paid plans offer more generations and faster processing.

For understanding images, such as reading a chart or explaining a photo, any current ChatGPT model with vision works, with reasoning models better at complex analysis. For generating images, ChatGPT handles text in images, editing and iterative refinement well. For developers, the OpenAI API exposes image models for programmatic generation and editing. Compare with alternatives such as Gemini, Midjourney and open models when you need specific styles, and check usage rights for commercial projects.

## Do ChatGPT images have watermarks?

ChatGPT images generally have no visible watermark, but they carry C2PA metadata, a provenance standard that records they were created with OpenAI's tools. Tools that read Content Credentials can show this information.

Metadata is easy to lose: screenshots, re-saving and many social platforms strip it, so its absence does not prove an image is human-made. OpenAI and other companies also research invisible watermarking and detection classifiers, but none is perfect. For honest use, label AI-generated images in your work, especially in journalism, education and advertising. If you need to verify an image, check Content Credentials with a verification tool, but combine that with other evidence.

## Should ChatGPT be used for medical advice?

Use ChatGPT to understand medical information, prepare questions for your doctor or learn about a diagnosis, not as a replacement for professional care. It can be wrong, lacks your full history, and cannot examine you.

It can explain test terminology, summarise general guidelines and help you organise symptoms before an appointment. It should not decide medication changes, interpret urgent symptoms or replace emergency services. Language models can state errors confidently, so verify information with trusted health sources and clinicians. Protect privacy: avoid sharing identifiable health details unless you understand how they are stored. If symptoms are severe or sudden, contact a doctor or emergency services immediately rather than asking a chatbot.

## Why is ChatGPT considered bad for the environment?

Running AI models requires data centres that consume electricity and water for cooling, and training large models uses significant energy. As usage grows, total consumption grows, which raises concerns about emissions and local water use.

Per-query estimates vary: in 2025, OpenAI's CEO stated an average ChatGPT query uses about 0.34 watt-hours, while the International Energy Agency projects global data centre electricity demand to roughly double by 2030, with AI a major driver. Impact depends on the electricity source and cooling method. Individuals can reduce waste by avoiding unnecessary regenerations; companies can choose efficient models, cache results and use cleaner power. Smaller, task-specific models often meet needs with far less energy.

# Which ChatGPT version is best, who created it, and why it keeps freezing
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-versions-and-freezing/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


The best ChatGPT version for most people is the default model ChatGPT picks for you, with a reasoning or thinking mode for hard problems; the specific model names change every few months. ChatGPT was created by OpenAI, launched in November 2022, and built by pre-training a GPT model on large amounts of text and then training it to follow instructions with human feedback. This page also explains ChatGPT Enterprise, what you get without paying, practical uses, and how to fix ChatGPT freezing in Chrome or on a Mac, and Cursor freezing too.

## Which ChatGPT version is best?

For everyday tasks, the default model in ChatGPT is the best balance of speed and quality. For hard maths, complex code, data analysis or careful planning, use the reasoning or thinking option, which takes longer but makes fewer mistakes.

OpenAI now routes many requests automatically, sending simple questions to fast models and hard ones to reasoning models, so manual model picking matters less than it did. Rules of thumb: use a fast mode for rewriting, summarising and quick facts; use thinking for anything with several steps where a wrong step is costly; use deep research when you need a cited report from many sources. Model names and availability per plan change often, so check the model picker in your account rather than lists online.

## Who is the founder of ChatGPT?

ChatGPT was created by OpenAI, the AI research company founded in December 2015 by a group that included Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, Ilya Sutskever, Wojciech Zaremba, John Schulman and Elon Musk. Sam Altman is OpenAI's chief executive.

No single person invented ChatGPT; it was built by OpenAI's research and engineering teams on years of earlier work, including the transformer architecture published by Google researchers in 2017 and OpenAI's own GPT models from 2018 onwards. Elon Musk left OpenAI's board in 2018. Microsoft became OpenAI's major partner and investor, which is why Microsoft's Copilot products use OpenAI models.

## How was ChatGPT created?

ChatGPT was created in two broad stages: pre-training a large GPT language model on a huge body of text to predict the next word, then fine-tuning it to follow instructions and hold conversations, using examples written by people and reinforcement learning from human feedback.

In the feedback stage, human reviewers ranked several model answers to the same prompt; a reward model learned those preferences, and the language model was trained to produce answers the reward model scored highly. OpenAI described this method in its 2022 paper on InstructGPT, ChatGPT's predecessor. ChatGPT launched as a research preview on 30 November 2022 and reached a very large user base within weeks. Since then OpenAI has added newer models, reasoning modes, tools such as search and code execution, voice, images and memory.

## What is ChatGPT Enterprise?

ChatGPT Enterprise is OpenAI's plan for large organisations. It adds enterprise security and admin controls, single sign-on, data that is not used to train OpenAI's models by default, higher limits, and connectors to company tools.

Organisations choose it so employees can use ChatGPT on work data without the risks of personal accounts: admins manage users, set which features and connectors are allowed, and see usage analytics, while compliance features help meet company policies. Smaller teams use the business plan with similar protections. For students, the relevant point is that the ChatGPT you use at an internship may have different features and rules from your personal account, so read the company's AI policy before pasting anything into it.

## How does ChatGPT treat you without premium?

Free users get the same core ChatGPT with capable models, but with lower limits. When you hit a limit, ChatGPT falls back to a lighter model or asks you to wait, and some advanced features are limited or unavailable.

On the free tier you can chat, search the web, upload files and images, use voice and create images within limits. What you notice is rationing: the strongest model and features such as deep research run out sooner, and responses may slow at peak times. Quality on simple tasks is very similar. Make the free tier go further with one clear, complete prompt instead of many follow-ups, new chats per task, and the fast model for simple work.

## What are some examples of using ChatGPT?

People use ChatGPT to explain concepts, write and edit text, write and debug code, analyse data and documents, plan projects, practise interviews and languages, and brainstorm ideas.

Examples that work well for students and developers:

- "Explain recursion with a real-life analogy, then give me three practice problems."
- "Here is my error and the code around it. What is wrong and how do I fix it?"
- "Turn these lecture notes into a one-page summary and ten quiz questions."
- "Review my resume against this job description and list the gaps."
- "Act as an interviewer for a junior Python developer role and grade my answers."
- "Analyse this CSV and plot monthly totals."

Check facts and run code before relying on it.

## Why does ChatGPT keep freezing?

ChatGPT usually freezes because the conversation is very long, the browser is short of memory, an extension interferes with the page, or OpenAI's service is having problems. Starting a new chat fixes most cases.

Work through these:

- Check OpenAI's status page for incidents.
- Start a new chat and paste a short summary of the old one.
- Close other heavy tabs and apps.
- Try a private window to rule out extensions.
- Update the browser or use the desktop app.
- Switch networks or turn off a VPN.

If freezing happens only in one chat with lots of code blocks or images, that chat has simply become too heavy for the page to render smoothly.

## Why does ChatGPT keep freezing on Chrome?

On Chrome, freezing usually comes from a very long chat, an extension such as an ad blocker or grammar checker modifying the page, too many open tabs using memory, or a corrupted site cache.

Fixes for Chrome:

- Open ChatGPT in an Incognito window; if it works, disable extensions one by one.
- Clear cookies and cached data for chatgpt.com from site settings.
- Update Chrome and restart it.
- Check that hardware acceleration is on in Chrome's system settings.
- Use Chrome's task manager to see whether the ChatGPT tab uses unusual memory.

If none of this helps, compare with another browser or the desktop app to see whether the problem is Chrome-specific.

## Why does ChatGPT keep freezing on my Mac?

On a Mac, freezing usually comes from a very long conversation, low memory with many apps open, an outdated browser or ChatGPT app, or a browser extension. The same fixes apply: new chat, fewer apps, updates, no extensions.

Specific steps:

- Update the ChatGPT Mac app, or your browser, and macOS.
- Open Activity Monitor and check memory pressure; quit heavy apps if it is high.
- If the desktop app freezes, quit it fully and reopen it, or sign out and back in.
- Try ChatGPT in Safari or Chrome to see whether the problem is the app or your account.
- Start a new chat for long-running work.

Older Macs with limited memory struggle with very long chats full of code, so keeping conversations short helps most.

## Why does Cursor AI keep freezing?

Cursor usually freezes while indexing a very large project, when heavy extensions run alongside it, when memory is short, or when the editor is out of date. Excluding big folders from indexing fixes most cases.

Steps that help:

- Add a `.cursorignore` file listing folders such as `node_modules`, build outputs, datasets and logs, so Cursor does not index them.
- Update Cursor to the latest version.
- Disable extensions one at a time to find a misbehaving one.
- Close projects you are not using and check memory use.
- Open the developer tools or logs from the Help menu to see the actual error.

If one long agent session hangs, stop it, start a new chat and give a smaller task.

# ChatGPT vs Claude: differences, strengths, when to use each, and how they compare
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-vs-claude/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT and Claude are both AI assistants built on large language models: ChatGPT by OpenAI and Claude by Anthropic. Both write, analyse, code, summarise and answer questions, with apps and developer APIs. The differences lie in their models, features, writing style, safety approaches and integrations, and each leads on different tasks at different times. I build AI products that call several providers, so this page compares them fairly, explains when to use each, and clears up ChatGPT versus AI generally, n8n versus Claude, and Apple Intelligence versus ChatGPT.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT and Claude?

They are competing products from different companies. ChatGPT, from OpenAI, uses OpenAI's GPT models and includes features such as image generation, voice conversations, web search, custom GPTs and agents. Claude, from Anthropic, uses Claude models and includes projects, artifacts, web search, skills and Claude Code for software development.

Users often describe differences in style: Claude's writing is frequently described as natural and careful, and it is popular for long documents and coding; ChatGPT has a very broad feature set and multimodal tools. Both companies release new models often, so specific capability gaps change within months. Compare current versions on your own tasks rather than relying on older reviews.

## Are ChatGPT and Claude the same?

No. They are separate assistants from different companies, built on different models trained with different data, methods and safety approaches. They look similar because both are chat interfaces to large language models.

Neither uses the other's model. Their answers to the same prompt can differ in content, structure and tone, and each has different limits, pricing plans, privacy settings and integrations. Some third-party tools let you use both in one interface. For developers, their APIs are similar in concept, with messages, system prompts and tool calling, but differ in details, so code must be adapted when switching.

## How does Claude AI differ from ChatGPT?

Claude differs in its models, its training approach, which Anthropic calls Constitutional AI, and its product features, such as artifacts for interactive outputs, projects for shared context, skills, and Claude Code for agentic coding in the terminal.

ChatGPT differs with native image generation, advanced voice mode, a large custom GPT ecosystem, and deep integration with OpenAI's other tools. Both offer web search, file analysis and connectors to apps. Context window sizes, usage limits and model options vary by plan. In my experience building with both APIs, the more important differences show up in specific tasks, such as following long, detailed instructions or producing structured output, which is why I test both.

## What does Claude AI do better than ChatGPT?

Many users and developers prefer Claude for coding, especially agentic coding with Claude Code, for working with long documents, and for writing that follows nuanced instructions and tone. Claude is also known for careful, well-structured responses.

These are tendencies, not guarantees: ChatGPT is also strong at coding and writing, and leads in other areas such as integrated image generation and voice. Benchmarks and leaderboards shift with each release. The fair approach is to run your own comparison: give both the same five real tasks from your work, judge accuracy and usefulness, and choose based on results rather than reputation.

## When should I use ChatGPT vs Claude?

Use whichever performs better on the task at hand. Common patterns: Claude for coding, long documents, careful writing and analysis; ChatGPT for image generation, voice conversations, custom GPTs and its wide plug-in ecosystem.

Practical suggestions:

- Drafting long reports or editing documents: try Claude first.
- Creating images or using voice on the go: ChatGPT.
- Coding in the terminal: Claude Code or OpenAI's Codex, depending on preference.
- Research with citations: both offer web search; check sources either way.
- Building products: evaluate both APIs on your own test set.

Many professionals use both and switch depending on the job.

## Should I use Claude AI or ChatGPT?

If you can only choose one, pick based on your main use: if you mostly code or work with long documents and writing, Claude is a strong choice; if you want images, voice and the broadest feature set, ChatGPT is a strong choice. Free plans let you try both.

Consider also: which integrates with tools you already use, privacy and data settings, usage limits on your budget, and team features if you work with others. For students, both free plans are useful for learning; remember to verify facts and follow your institution's rules on AI use. Revisit your choice every few months, since both improve quickly.

## How do Claude and ChatGPT compare overall?

Overall, they are close competitors at the frontier: each new model release from one is soon matched or exceeded in some areas by the other. Independent leaderboards that rank models by human preference and benchmarks show them trading places across tasks.

For businesses, compare on: accuracy on your tasks, cost per task, latency, context length, tool-calling reliability, data and compliance terms, and availability on your cloud platform. Claude is available through Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft offerings; OpenAI models through OpenAI and Microsoft Azure. RAG.NextUpgrad uses multi-provider fallback, which avoids betting everything on one provider.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT and AI?

AI, artificial intelligence, is the broad field of making computers perform tasks that need human-like intelligence, including vision, speech, planning and language. ChatGPT is one specific AI product: a chatbot built on OpenAI's large language models.

Other AI includes recommendation systems, face recognition, fraud detection, self-driving systems and medical image analysis, much of which has nothing to do with chatbots. Generative AI, which creates text, images, audio and video, is the branch that ChatGPT and Claude belong to. Saying "AI" when meaning "ChatGPT" is common, but the field is much larger.

## What is the difference between n8n and Claude?

n8n is a workflow automation platform that connects apps and runs multi-step processes on triggers and schedules. Claude is an AI model and assistant. They complement each other: n8n can call Claude to handle steps that need language understanding.

For example, an n8n workflow can receive a support email, send it to Claude to classify and draft a reply, then create a ticket and notify a team channel. n8n provides the triggers, integrations, retries and logs; Claude provides the reasoning and writing. Claude can also connect to tools directly through its own integrations, but for scheduled, reliable automations across many apps, a workflow tool like n8n is often the better backbone.

## What is the difference between Apple AI and ChatGPT?

Apple Intelligence is Apple's set of AI features built into iPhone, iPad and Mac, using Apple's own models on the device and on Apple's private cloud servers. ChatGPT is OpenAI's assistant. Apple integrates ChatGPT as an optional extension for some requests, such as Siri questions needing broader knowledge.

Apple Intelligence focuses on personal, privacy-preserving tasks: writing tools in any app, notification summaries, photo clean-up, Genmoji and a more capable Siri with personal context. ChatGPT is a general assistant for broad questions, long conversations, coding and creative work. With the integration, Apple asks before sending a request to ChatGPT, and you can use it without an OpenAI account.

# ChatGPT vs Copilot: the difference, and how to use Copilot in Teams
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-vs-copilot-teams/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot are both AI assistants, and Copilot runs largely on OpenAI's GPT models, but they are different products: ChatGPT is OpenAI's standalone app with its own tools, while Copilot is Microsoft's assistant built into Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft 365. The right choice depends on where your work lives. This page compares them, explains why Copilot sometimes seems weaker, and covers Copilot in Microsoft Teams: where to find it, how it works in chats and meetings, and where meeting transcripts are stored.

## ChatGPT vs Copilot: which should I use?

Use Copilot when your work is in Microsoft 365, such as Outlook, Word, Excel and Teams, or your organisation provides it with data protection. Use ChatGPT as a broad assistant with custom GPTs, projects, memory, strong image generation and coding agents.

For a student, ChatGPT is often the more flexible learning and side-project companion, while Copilot is the natural choice inside a college or company Microsoft 365 account, where it can see your documents and meetings with your permissions. Many people use both: Copilot for work documents and meetings, ChatGPT for exploration and personal projects. Test both on three of your real tasks before deciding.

## Is Copilot the same as ChatGPT?

No. They share technology, since Microsoft builds Copilot largely on OpenAI's models, but they are separate products from different companies, with different apps, features, integrations, accounts and privacy terms.

Copilot adds Microsoft's own layers: grounding with Bing search, access to your Microsoft 365 data through Microsoft Graph for work accounts, enterprise data protection, and integration into Windows and Office. ChatGPT adds OpenAI's layers: custom GPTs, projects, memory, canvas, Codex and its app ecosystem. The same underlying model can therefore behave differently in each, because the instructions, tools and context around it differ.

## Do Copilot and ChatGPT use the same model?

Often from the same family, but not necessarily the same version at the same time. Copilot uses OpenAI's GPT models hosted by Microsoft, along with Microsoft's own models and, in some features, models from other providers. ChatGPT uses OpenAI's latest models directly.

Microsoft decides which model serves each Copilot request and does not always show it, while ChatGPT lets you choose between modes in many plans. New OpenAI models usually reach ChatGPT first or at the same time, and Microsoft adopts them on its own schedule after testing. In practice, differences in answers come as much from system instructions, safety settings and grounding as from the model version.

## When should I use Copilot vs ChatGPT?

Use Copilot for tasks tied to Microsoft 365 content and Windows: summarising a Teams meeting, drafting a reply in Outlook, analysing an Excel table, or asking about your organisation's files. Use ChatGPT for open-ended learning, writing, coding, image work and anything outside Microsoft 365.

Examples:

- "What did we decide in yesterday's project meeting?": Copilot in Teams.
- "Turn this Word report into a ten-slide deck": Copilot in PowerPoint.
- "Teach me recursion and quiz me": ChatGPT or Copilot both work.
- "Build a small web app with tests in my repository": ChatGPT's Codex or GitHub Copilot.
- "Generate and edit an illustration": ChatGPT.

When company data is involved, use the tool your organisation has approved.

## Why is Copilot worse than ChatGPT?

Copilot is not inherently worse, but it can feel that way because it may use faster models for some requests, applies more conservative instructions, and often lacks the context you assumed it had. Precise prompts and attached context close most of the gap.

Common reasons and fixes:

- **Missing context**: open the document or attach the file before asking.
- **Vague request**: state the goal, audience, format and length.
- **Wrong product**: Microsoft 365 Copilot needs a licence for work data; free Copilot cannot see your work files.
- **Search-heavy answers**: Copilot often grounds in web results, which can make answers shorter and more cautious.

For deep reasoning tasks, choose Copilot's deeper or thinking mode if available.

## Where do I find Copilot in Teams?

In Microsoft Teams, Copilot appears in the left app bar or as Copilot Chat, in chats and channels as a Copilot button, and in meetings as a Copilot button in the meeting controls. Which ones you see depends on your licence and your organisation's settings.

Copilot Chat, available to many work and school accounts, is a general assistant grounded in the web and your uploaded files. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot licence adds Copilot inside chats, channels and meetings, with access to your Teams messages, files and meeting transcripts within your permissions. If you see no Copilot at all, check that Teams is updated and ask your IT team whether Copilot is enabled for your account.

## How does Copilot work in Teams?

In Teams, Copilot uses a language model with access to the content you are allowed to see: chat and channel messages, files and meeting transcripts. It summarises conversations, answers questions about them and drafts messages.

In a chat or channel, ask "summarise the last week of this conversation" or "what decisions were made about the launch date?", and Copilot answers with references to the messages. In meetings, it works from the live transcript. It respects permissions, so it will not reveal content from chats you are not part of. Like any assistant, it can misattribute who said what or miss nuance, so check important points against the transcript before acting on them.

## How do I use Copilot in Teams?

Open a chat, channel or meeting and select the Copilot button, then ask in plain language: summarise, list action items, find what someone said, or draft a reply. You can also use Copilot Chat from the app bar for questions across your work content.

Useful prompts:

- "Summarise the unread messages in this channel and highlight anything that needs my reply."
- "List the action items from this chat with owners and deadlines."
- "Draft a polite reply asking for the report by Friday."
- "What files were shared in this chat about the hackathon?"

Be specific about time ranges and people. Copilot's drafts are starting points; edit them so they sound like you and contain only facts you can stand behind.

## How do I use Copilot in a Teams meeting?

Turn on transcription when the meeting starts, then open Copilot from the meeting controls. During the meeting you can ask for a recap, open questions or action items; afterwards, the meeting recap shows notes and tasks generated from the transcript.

Organisers can also allow Copilot to work only during the meeting without keeping a transcript, depending on organisation settings, in which case after-meeting recaps are limited. Good prompts: "What have I missed in the last ten minutes?", "What are the unresolved questions?", and "Draft a follow-up email with decisions and owners." Tell participants when transcription is on; many organisations require it. Review the recap before sharing, because summaries can drop qualifications or merge points.

## Where are Copilot Teams transcripts stored?

Meeting recordings and transcripts are stored in Microsoft 365 within your organisation's tenant, typically in the meeting organiser's OneDrive for regular meetings and in the channel's SharePoint site for channel meetings, governed by retention and access policies.

Who can see a transcript depends on meeting settings and permissions, usually the organiser and attendees. Copilot reads the transcript to answer questions and build recaps, and Copilot interactions themselves are stored under the organisation's compliance settings. Admins control whether transcription is allowed, how long recordings and transcripts are kept, and who can download them. For sensitive meetings, check with the organiser before turning transcription on, and follow your organisation's data policy.

# ChatGPT vs Gemini: the difference, which is better, and when to use each
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-vs-gemini/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


ChatGPT and Gemini are both AI assistants that chat, answer questions, write, code and work with images and files. ChatGPT is made by OpenAI and runs on its GPT models; Gemini is made by Google and runs on its Gemini models. They are close in capability, and the better choice depends mostly on the task and on which ecosystem you already use. This page explains what each is, how they differ, which is better for what, when to use Claude instead, what this kind of tool is called, and why opinions online disagree so much.

## What are ChatGPT and Gemini?

ChatGPT is OpenAI's AI assistant, launched in November 2022. Gemini is Google's AI assistant, launched as Bard in 2023 and renamed Gemini in early 2024. Both are chat interfaces built on large language models.

You talk to either in plain language by typing or speaking, and they respond with text, code, images or actions such as searching the web. Both have free tiers and paid plans, apps for phones and the web, and developer APIs. Under the hood, both are transformer-based models trained on large amounts of text, code, images and audio, then tuned to follow instructions and behave safely. They make similar kinds of mistakes, so the same verification habits apply to both.

## Are ChatGPT and Gemini the same?

No. They are different products from different companies, built on different model families: GPT models from OpenAI and Gemini models from Google. They overlap heavily in what they do, but differ in strengths, features and integrations.

The overlap is why people treat them as interchangeable for everyday tasks such as explanations, summaries and drafts, where both perform well. The differences show in the details: which tools each can use, how each connects to your other apps, how each handles very long documents or video, and how each phrases and structures answers. Your data also goes to different companies under different privacy terms, which matters for work and personal information.

## What is the difference between ChatGPT and Gemini?

The biggest differences are ecosystem and features. Gemini is built into Google's products, such as Gmail, Docs, Drive, Android, Maps and YouTube. ChatGPT is a standalone assistant with its own ecosystem of custom GPTs, apps, projects, memory and coding tools.

Practical differences that matter:

- **Integration**: Gemini works naturally with Google Workspace; ChatGPT connects to many services through connectors and apps.
- **Media**: Gemini handles video input natively through its API; ChatGPT offers strong image generation and voice.
- **Coding**: ChatGPT has Codex; Google has Gemini Code Assist and Antigravity.
- **Plans**: both have free tiers and paid plans with different bundles, such as Google's plans including cloud storage.

Both change features often, so compare current versions.

## How is Gemini different from ChatGPT under the hood?

Gemini models were designed from the start to handle text, images, audio and video together, and support very long context windows. GPT models also handle multiple types of input, with OpenAI pairing them with separate models for images, video and speech.

Both families come in tiers: fast, cheaper models for everyday use and larger reasoning models for hard problems, and both apps route requests between them. Google grounds Gemini answers with Google Search, while ChatGPT uses its own search integration. The training data, model sizes and exact architectures are not public for either. For most users these differences show up indirectly, as speed, how well long files are handled, and how current the answers are.

## ChatGPT vs Gemini: which is better?

Neither is better at everything. Both are top-tier assistants, and benchmark leadership changes with each model release. The better one for you is the one that gives better results on your actual tasks, in the apps you already use.

A fair test takes twenty minutes: pick five tasks you do often, such as explaining a concept, summarising a PDF, debugging code, drafting an email and planning a week, and run the same prompts in both. Judge accuracy, clarity and how much editing each answer needs. Many people end up using both: Gemini for anything inside Google Workspace and Android, ChatGPT for general work and its tool ecosystem. Public leaderboards, such as LMArena's community rankings, give a broad signal but not a verdict on your use case.

## When should I use ChatGPT vs Gemini?

Use Gemini when your work lives in Google's ecosystem: Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, YouTube, Maps or an Android phone. Use ChatGPT for a broad standalone assistant with custom GPTs, projects, memory, image generation and coding agents.

Examples:

- Summarise a long Gmail thread or a Drive folder: Gemini.
- Ask about a YouTube lecture or analyse a video file: Gemini.
- Build a reusable assistant for a repeated task: either, through custom GPTs or Gems.
- Generate and edit images in conversation: ChatGPT is very strong here.
- Work on a code repository with an agent: ChatGPT's Codex, or Google's coding tools.

If your college uses Google Workspace, Gemini in your student account may be the most convenient.

## When should I use ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini?

Use ChatGPT as a broad all-rounder, Gemini inside Google's ecosystem and for video and very long multimodal inputs, and Claude for long documents, careful writing and coding work, including Claude Code for real repositories.

This is a starting point, not a rule. All three are close enough that the prompt and the context you provide often matter more than the brand. For developers, the choice also depends on the API: pricing, rate limits, latency and features such as tool use or batch processing. In RAG.NextUpgrad I built multi-provider fallback, so the product keeps working when one provider is slow or down; that design also lets you switch models when one improves. Students can use the free tiers of all three and keep whichever helps most.

## How does Gemini AI compare to ChatGPT for students?

For students, both are excellent and free tiers go a long way. Gemini is especially convenient with a Google account, Google Docs and YouTube lectures, and Google has run free plan offers for students. ChatGPT is strong as a tutor, writing coach and coding helper.

Study tasks where each shines:

- Turning a recorded or YouTube lecture into notes: Gemini.
- Step-by-step tutoring and quizzes: both, with ChatGPT's study-style prompting a popular choice.
- Studying from your own notes and papers: Google's NotebookLM is excellent and free.
- Debugging programming assignments: both; check by running the code.

Whatever you use, follow your college's rules on AI in assignments.

## What are ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude called?

They are called AI chatbots or AI assistants, and more technically, applications built on large language models, or LLMs. Because they also handle images, audio and video, they are sometimes called multimodal AI assistants.

When they can take actions, such as browsing, running code or using apps to complete tasks, they are described as AI agents. The broader field is generative AI, since they generate new text, images, audio and code. Microsoft Copilot, Meta AI, Perplexity, DeepSeek and Mistral's Le Chat belong to the same category. In job descriptions, building products with these models is usually called GenAI engineering or AI engineering.

## Why do Reddit opinions on Gemini vs ChatGPT differ so much?

Because people test different tasks, different model versions and different plans at different times. A comparison from a few months ago may describe models that have since been replaced, and one person's coding task says little about another's essay.

Online threads are also shaped by strong feelings about companies, by free-tier users comparing against paid-tier users, and by single memorable failures. Treat them as a source of ideas for what to test, not as a verdict. Look for posts that state the exact model, plan, date and prompt, and ideally share the outputs. Then run your own small test: your tasks, your prompts, both tools, side by side. That answer is the only one that applies to you.

# Chroma vs ChromaDB: what Chroma does in Python, examples and common errors
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chroma-vector-database-python/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Chroma, often called ChromaDB, is an open-source vector database for AI applications: it stores text chunks, their embeddings and metadata, and returns the most similar chunks for a query, which is the retrieval step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). It is popular for prototypes because it runs inside Python with a few lines of code. This page covers the name, its role in LLM apps, Python usage and examples, avoiding repeated embedding costs, in-memory versus persistent storage, a common Docker crash, testing RAG with Chroma, and the unrelated colour term.

## What is the difference between Chroma and ChromaDB?

There is no difference: Chroma is the project and company name, and ChromaDB is the common name for the database and its Python package, installed with `pip install chromadb`.

Chroma runs in several modes: embedded inside your Python process, as a client-server setup with a separate Chroma server, or as a hosted cloud service. Tutorials use "Chroma", "ChromaDB" and "Chroma DB" interchangeably. In LangChain and LlamaIndex, the integration is usually called Chroma. If you see "Chroma" in a photography or colour context, that is an unrelated meaning covered at the end of this page.

## What is ChromaDB in LLM applications?

In LLM applications, ChromaDB is the vector store that holds your knowledge: document chunks with their embeddings. When a user asks a question, the app searches Chroma for similar chunks and passes them to the LLM so it can answer from your documents.

Chroma provides collections, which are like tables, with documents, embeddings, metadata and IDs. It can compute embeddings for you with a default or chosen embedding function, or accept embeddings you compute yourself. Metadata filters let you restrict search, for example to one course or date range. It uses an approximate nearest-neighbour index, HNSW, for fast search. For many student projects and internal tools, Chroma is all the vector database you need.

## What does Chroma do in Python?

In Python, Chroma lets you create collections, add documents with IDs and metadata, and query them by text or embedding to get the most similar items, all from a simple API that can run in-process without a separate server.

Typical operations:

- `client.get_or_create_collection(name)` to create or open a collection.
- `collection.add(ids=..., documents=..., metadatas=...)` to index chunks.
- `collection.query(query_texts=[...], n_results=5, where={...})` to search with filters.
- `collection.update`, `upsert` and `delete` to keep data current.

Results include IDs, documents, metadata and distances, which you pass to your LLM prompt with IDs for citations.

## How do I use ChromaDB in Python?

Install `chromadb`, create a persistent client, create a collection, add documents with unique IDs, and query it.

```python
import chromadb

client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path="./chroma_store")
col = client.get_or_create_collection("notes")
col.upsert(
    ids=["os-1", "os-2"],
    documents=["A process is a program in execution.", "Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages."],
    metadatas=[{"subject": "os", "page": 3}, {"subject": "os", "page": 7}],
)
res = col.query(query_texts=["what is paging?"], n_results=1, where={"subject": "os"})
print(res["documents"][0], res["metadatas"][0])
```

The default embedding function downloads a small model on first use; for production, choose your embedding model explicitly and use it consistently.

## What are some Chroma examples?

Common Chroma examples are a chatbot over your PDFs, semantic search over notes or support tickets, a FAQ assistant for a college or product, and memory for an AI agent that stores past conversation summaries.

Project ideas to practise:

- **Study assistant**: index lecture notes by page and answer questions with page citations.
- **Support search**: index past tickets and suggest similar resolved issues.
- **Code search**: embed function docstrings and search your codebase in plain language.
- **Agent memory**: store summaries of past tasks and retrieve them when relevant.

Pair Chroma with keyword search for exact terms such as error codes, which embeddings often miss, and add a reranker when results look plausible but wrong.

## How do I avoid recomputing embeddings with Chroma?

Use a persistent client so embeddings survive restarts, give each chunk a stable ID, and upsert only new or changed chunks, tracking a hash of each document to detect changes. Never rebuild the whole collection when one file changes.

A simple pattern: compute an ID such as `docname#chunkindex` and a content hash; before indexing, check which IDs already exist with the same hash; embed and upsert only those that are new or changed; delete IDs for removed content. If you compute embeddings yourself, cache them on disk keyed by content hash. Remember that changing the embedding model requires re-embedding everything, because vectors from different models are not comparable.

## Is it a problem to store a vector database in memory?

For prototypes, tests and small datasets, in-memory storage is fine and fast. For anything users depend on, it is a problem: data disappears when the process restarts, memory limits cap your dataset, and multiple app instances cannot share it.

Use in-memory clients for unit tests and notebooks, and persistent storage in development and production, with backups. If you run several app instances, use a client-server Chroma or a database such as PostgreSQL with pgvector, so all instances see the same data. Also keep your source documents as the true record: the vector index should be rebuildable from them, which makes recovery and model changes straightforward.

## Why does ChromaDB crash with "illegal instruction" in a Docker container?

"Illegal instruction" usually means a compiled dependency, such as the HNSW index library or an ML runtime, was built for CPU instructions your machine or emulator does not support. It often happens when running an image built for a different CPU architecture, such as amd64 under emulation on an ARM Mac.

Fixes to try:

- Run an image that matches your machine's architecture, or build the image natively on it.
- Avoid emulation for this workload where possible.
- Use the official Chroma server image and connect from your app as a client.
- Rebuild the dependency from source without CPU-specific optimisations, following Chroma's troubleshooting docs.
- Pin versions known to work on your platform.

Check Chroma's GitHub issues for your exact error and platform; others usually hit it first.

## How do you test RAG memory with ChromaDB?

Treat retrieval as testable code: create a fresh in-memory or temporary Chroma collection in each test, load a fixed set of documents, run known queries and assert that the expected IDs come back in the top results.

What to test:

- **Retrieval correctness**: expected chunk IDs appear in the top k for each query.
- **Updates**: changed documents replace old chunks; deleted ones disappear.
- **Filters**: metadata filters exclude what they should.
- **Agent memory**: stored summaries are retrieved in later turns and old ones expire as designed.
- **Regressions**: run the suite on every change to chunking or embeddings.

Automated retrieval tests catch silent failures, such as duplicate chunks or broken updates, long before users notice wrong answers.

## What is colour chroma?

In colour theory, chroma is the colourfulness or intensity of a colour relative to a neutral grey of the same brightness: high chroma colours are vivid, low chroma colours are muted or greyish. It is unrelated to the Chroma vector database.

Chroma is one of the three dimensions in colour systems such as Munsell, alongside hue and value or lightness. "High chroma vs low chroma" comparisons appear in painting, design, photography and fashion; for example, a bright red is high chroma, while a dusty rose is low chroma. In photography, "chroma noise" refers to random colour speckles in images. If you came here for databases, the sections above cover ChromaDB.
