For Vertex AI, you use Google Cloud service accounts and application default credentials rather than simple API keys. How do Gemini API keys work? A Gemini API key identifies your Google Cloud project when calling the Gemini API. Requests include the key in a header, and Google applies that project's rate limits, billing settings and usage tracking to every call made with it. Because the key grants access to your quota and billing, anyone holding it can use your allowance, so treat it like a password. Projects without billing use the free tier; enabling billing moves the project to paid tiers with higher limits. You can create several keys per project, for example one per environment, and delete compromised ones instantly. For production, add API restrictions, monitor usage for spikes and prefer server-side calls so keys never reach users' browsers. What are the Gemini API limits? Gemini API limits are set per project and model, measured as requests per minute, tokens per minute and requests per day. The free tier has the lowest limits, and paid tiers raise them as your billing history grows. Also asked as: what are gemini api limits Limits differ between models: lighter Flash models allow more requests than Pro models. Exceeding a limit returns an error with status 429, so implement exponential backoff and retries. Each model also has maximum input and output token sizes and file size limits for uploads. Google publishes current values on the rate limits page, and they change as models are released, so check them rather than relying on old blog posts. Request higher quotas through Google Cloud if needed. How do you see Gemini API usage? Check usage in Google AI Studio's usage and billing pages, or in the Google Cloud Console under APIs and Services for request metrics and quotas, with costs in Cloud Billing reports. Each API response also returns token counts. Also asked as: how to see gemini api usage For detailed tracking, log the usage metadata from every response, including prompt, cached and output token counts, along with the model and feature that made the call. This shows which parts of your app consume the most tokens. Set budget alerts in Cloud Billing to catch unexpected spikes, such as a loop calling the API repeatedly. Monitoring dashboards that combine these logs with error rates help you tune prompts, caching and model choice. Can the Gemini API read PDFs? Yes. Gemini reads PDFs natively, understanding text, tables, charts and images on each page, not just extracted text. Upload files through the Files API or send smaller ones inline, then ask questions, summarise or extract structured data. Also asked as: can gemini api read pdf Gemini's document understanding handles long PDFs of many pages in one request, which suits contract review, research papers and reports. For structured extraction, combine it with a JSON schema so outputs are validated, similar to how DocuLens AI validates extracted fields. For scanned documents with complex layouts, compare Gemini with dedicated OCR, such as Mistral OCR, which my OCR &amp; Speech Workspace uses in page batches. Can the Gemini API see images? Yes. Gemini models are natively multimodal: send images inline or through the Files API, and ask the model to describe, compare, extract text from, classify or reason about them. Recent models can also return bounding boxes for objects. Also asked as: can gemini api see images Common uses include reading receipts and forms, analysing charts and screenshots, product categorisation, visual question answering and accessibility descriptions. You can include several images in one request, for example to compare before and after photos. Image tokens count toward usage, so resize large images when fine detail is unnecessary. For tasks requiring exact detection or recognition, such as faces, specialised models like those in FaceVision remain more precise and easier to keep private. Can you train or fine-tune Gemini through the API? Fine-tuning Gemini models is available mainly through Vertex AI on Google Cloud, which offers supervised tuning for supported Gemini versions. Tuning through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio has been limited for current models. Before tuning, try prompting with examples, system instructions, context caching for large reference material, and RAG for knowledge, which solve most needs faster. Tune when you need consistent formats, styles or specialised classification at scale. Vertex AI tuning requires a Google Cloud project with billing, a JSONL dataset of input and output pairs, and evaluation against the base model. For full control over weights, open models such as Gemma can be fine-tuned with QLoRA, as in FineTune Studio.

# Is Gemini bad? Memory, iPhone, images, Copilot, NotebookLM, AI Mode and Antigravity
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-bad-memory-iphone-vs-copilot/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24

Gemini is Google's AI assistant and model family, and complaints that it is bad usually come from inconsistent answers, the model version in use, settings that disable memory, or regional limits on features. It improves quickly, but it is not the best at everything. I use multiple providers with fallback in RAG.NextUpgrad, so this page covers why Gemini disappoints, its memory, Gemini on iPhone, image generation errors, and how it differs from Copilot, NotebookLM, AI Mode, Google Assistant and Antigravity. Why is Gemini so bad? Gemini feels bad to many users because of inconsistent answers, overly cautious refusals, hallucinations and differences between models, since faster Flash models trade quality for speed. Results also vary by task: it leads on some and trails on others. Early controversies, such as the 2024 pause on generating images of people after historically inaccurate results, shaped its reputation. Newer Gemini models score highly on many benchmarks, especially with long context and multimodal input, but benchmarks do not match every workflow. Improve results by choosing the strongest model available on your plan, giving clear context and examples, enabling Google Search grounding for facts and starting fresh chats when answers drift. For important work, compare outputs across assistants on your own tasks. Why is Gemini's memory so bad? Gemini's memory often seems poor because personal context features are off, unavailable in your region or account type, or limited to saved details. Within a chat, very long conversations also push earlier details out of focus. Gemini can remember information you save and, where available, refer to past chats, but this depends on settings such as Gemini Apps activity and personal context options. Workspace accounts may have features controlled by administrators. To improve recall, save key preferences explicitly, keep one topic per chat, restate important constraints and use Gems with custom instructions for repeated tasks. Review what Gemini stores in its settings and delete anything you do not want kept, since memory involves privacy trade-offs. What is Gemini on my iPhone? On an iPhone, Gemini is usually Google's Gemini app from the App Store, or Gemini features inside Google apps such as the Google app, Gmail and Google Docs. It is separate from Apple's own Siri and Apple Intelligence features. The Gemini app offers chat, voice conversations through Gemini Live, image understanding through the camera, image generation and connections to Google services. Widgets and Shortcuts can open Gemini quickly from the home or lock screen. If you see Gemini unexpectedly, check which app installed it or whether a Google app added Gemini features in an update. You can remove the app or adjust its permissions in iPhone Settings like any other app. Can you use Gemini on your iPhone? Yes. Download the official Gemini app by Google from the App Store, sign in with a Google account, and accept the terms. You can also use Gemini in Safari at gemini.google.com. Also asked as: can i use gemini on my iphone The app supports text and voice chats, Gemini Live conversations, uploading photos and files, and image generation where available. Some features need a newer iOS version, a supported country, a minimum age or a paid Google AI plan. Add the Gemini widget or an Action Button shortcut for quick access. Allow microphone and camera access only if you need voice or visual features. Keep the app updated, since Google releases new features to iPhone regularly. Why is Gemini not creating photos on iPhone? Gemini may not create images on iPhone because image generation is unavailable for your country, age or account type, the app is outdated, the prompt breaks content policies, or a temporary usage limit applies. Also asked as: why gemini is not creating photo in iphone Check these in order: update the Gemini app; confirm you are signed into a personal Google account, since Workspace administrators can disable features; and make sure you meet age requirements. Rephrase prompts that involve real people, logos or sensitive content, since Gemini refuses some requests. Usage limits on free accounts can pause generation temporarily. Try the same prompt on gemini.google.com in Safari to see whether the issue is the app or your account. Explicitly ask Gemini to create an image to trigger the tool. How does Gemini compare to Copilot? Gemini is Google's assistant built on its own Gemini models and integrated with Google Search, Android and Google Workspace. Microsoft Copilot mainly uses OpenAI's GPT models alongside Microsoft's own and integrates with Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft 365. The best choice usually follows your ecosystem: Gemini suits Gmail, Docs, Drive and Android users, while Copilot fits Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams and Windows workflows. Both offer free tiers, paid plans, image generation, web-grounded answers and voice modes. Quality differs by task, and both update often, so test each on your real work. They are not the same product, and they do not talk to each other directly, though you can use both side by side for comparisons. What is the difference between Gemini and NotebookLM? Gemini is a general assistant that answers from its training, the web and your Google apps. NotebookLM is a research notebook that answers only from sources you add, such as PDFs, documents, websites and videos, with citations to each. NotebookLM is built on Gemini models but designed for grounded study and research: it summarises sources and creates study guides, mind maps and Audio Overviews that turn documents into podcast-style discussions. Because it stays within your sources, it is less likely to invent facts, and every answer links back to passages. Use Gemini for broad tasks, writing and general questions, and NotebookLM for studying a defined set of materials. This grounded approach mirrors RAG systems such as RAG.NextUpgrad. What is the difference between Gemini and Google AI Mode? AI Mode is a conversational search experience inside Google Search, powered by Gemini, that answers queries with summaries and links to sources. Gemini is a standalone assistant for broader tasks such as writing, coding, planning and creating images. AI Mode breaks complex queries into many searches and combines the results, so it suits research questions where you want sources and follow-up questions. Gemini can also search the web but is designed for longer conversations, file uploads, Gems, connected Google apps and creative work. AI Overviews, the summaries at the top of regular results, are a lighter version of the same idea. Use AI Mode when you want to explore the web, and Gemini when you want an assistant to do work. What is the difference between Gemini and Google Assistant? Google Assistant was a voice assistant built for commands, such as timers, smart home control and quick answers. Gemini is a generative AI assistant that understands complex requests, holds conversations and creates content. Google has been replacing Assistant with Gemini across phones and devices. Gemini handles open-ended tasks better: summarising emails, drafting messages, analysing images and answering follow-up questions naturally. Early on, some Assistant features, such as certain smart home routines, worked better in Assistant, and Google added them to Gemini over time. On Android, you can choose Gemini as the default assistant in settings. Gemini Live offers natural voice conversation, while quick commands still work through Gemini's integrations with Google apps and devices. What is the difference between Gemini and Antigravity? Gemini is Google's model family and assistant. Antigravity is Google's agent-first development environment, released alongside Gemini 3 in November 2025, where AI agents plan, write, run and test code across an editor, terminal and browser. Antigravity uses Gemini models, and also supports some models from other providers, to power agents that work on software tasks with less step-by-step guidance. It shows agents' plans, task lists and results, such as screenshots and browser recordings, so developers can review the work. Gemini, by contrast, is a general assistant used through apps, the web and the API. Developers can also use Gemini models in other coding tools, such as Gemini CLI or IDE extensions.

# What does Gemini Canvas do? Notebooks, models and how Gemini helps users
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-canvas-notebooks-models/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Gemini Canvas is a workspace inside the Gemini app where you write and edit documents or code alongside Gemini, with the draft in its own panel and live previews for web code. Notebooks, in Google's ecosystem, usually means NotebookLM, which answers questions only from the sources you upload. This page explains how both work, which Gemini model to pick for general work and for coding, when Gemini launched worldwide and in India, and how Gemini helps draft emails in Gmail and slides in Google Slides.

## What does Gemini Canvas do?

Canvas gives you a dedicated editing space next to the chat. Gemini writes a document or code there, and you refine it together: highlight a section to change, adjust tone or length, or run and preview code such as a web page.

It is useful for longer pieces you will iterate on: an essay outline, a project report, a cover letter, a Python script or a small HTML app. For code, Canvas can show a live preview of web projects, so you can see a landing page or a simple game working and ask for changes. Canvas can also turn content into other formats, such as a web page or quiz, and export documents to Google Docs. It replaces the clumsy pattern of copying code from the chat into a file and back.

## How does Gemini Canvas work?

Select Canvas in the Gemini prompt bar, describe what you want, and Gemini opens the draft in a side panel. You then chat to revise it, or edit the draft directly, and Gemini updates the canvas rather than writing a new answer each time.

Useful moves inside Canvas:

- Highlight a paragraph and ask for it to be simpler, shorter or more formal.
- Ask for a specific change: "add error handling to the fetch call".
- Preview web code and describe what looks wrong.
- Export a document to Google Docs to keep editing there.

Keep the scope small, one document or one small app per canvas, and save versions you like before asking for big changes.

## What are Gemini notebooks?

In Google's AI tools, notebooks usually refer to NotebookLM: a research assistant where you create a notebook, add sources such as PDFs, Google Docs, websites or YouTube videos, and ask questions that are answered only from those sources, with citations.

Google has been connecting NotebookLM with the Gemini app, so you can work with notebook material inside Gemini as well. For students, NotebookLM is one of the best free study tools: add your lecture notes, textbook chapters and past papers, then ask for summaries, explanations, study guides or quizzes. Because answers come from your sources and link to the exact passages, they are easier to trust and check than general chatbot answers. It also creates audio overviews, a podcast-style discussion of your material.

## How do Gemini notebooks work?

You create a notebook in NotebookLM, upload or link sources, and ask questions. NotebookLM retrieves the relevant passages from your sources and has Gemini answer from them, citing each claim back to the source text.

This is retrieval-augmented generation scoped to your own material, the same principle behind the document chat I built in the OCR & Speech Workspace, where answers cite page numbers. Tips: keep one notebook per subject or project, add only sources you trust, and ask specific questions such as "compare the two definitions of normalisation in these notes". Click the citations to verify. Generated study guides and quizzes are good for revision, but check them against the sources before an exam.

## Which Gemini model is best?

For everyday tasks, Flash is best: fast and capable. For hard problems such as complex coding, maths and analysis, the Pro tier or a thinking mode is best. The newest generation of each tier is usually better than the previous one.

The Gemini app chooses a model automatically unless you pick one, and the options shown depend on your plan. Developers choose explicitly in the Gemini API: Flash-Lite for the cheapest high-volume tasks, Flash as the default for most products, and Pro for the hardest requests. A good production pattern is to start with Flash, measure where it fails, and route only those cases to Pro. Google's models page lists the current versions, which change several times a year.

## Which Gemini model is best for coding?

Use the most capable Pro model available to you, ideally with thinking enabled, for debugging, architecture and multi-file changes. Flash is fine for quick snippets, explanations and simple scripts.

For real projects, the model matters less than the tool. Google's coding tools, such as Gemini CLI, Gemini Code Assist in your editor and Antigravity, can read your whole project, run commands and tests, and propose edits, which makes their output far more reliable than code from a chat window. Whatever you use, give precise tasks, include error messages, keep a project context file with build and test commands, and review every change. Compare against other coding tools on one real task before settling.

## When was Gemini AI launched?

Google announced the Gemini model family in December 2023. Its chatbot Bard, launched in early 2023, was renamed Gemini in February 2024, when the Gemini app also arrived on Android and iPhone.

Since then Google has released several model generations with improvements in reasoning, coding, long context and multimodal understanding, added Gemini to Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Android and Chrome, and launched developer tools including AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini CLI and Antigravity. The technical report on the first generation describes models trained to handle text, images, audio and video together, a design choice that shapes how Gemini works with media today.

## When did Gemini launch in India?

Google's AI chatbot was available in India from 2023, under the Bard name, and the Gemini app launched in India in 2024 with support for English and several Indian languages.

Language support has expanded since, and Gemini works in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam and Urdu, among others, which makes it useful for students and users more comfortable in their own language. Google has also run offers in India, including free plans for eligible students and a partnership with Jio. On Android phones in India, Gemini increasingly replaces Google Assistant as the default assistant. Check Google's Gemini help pages for the current list of languages and features.

## How does Gemini help users draft an email?

In Gmail, Gemini drafts an email from a short prompt with "Help me write", suggests replies in context, and can refine a draft to be more formal, shorter or more detailed. It can also summarise a long thread before you reply.

Write prompts that include the recipient, purpose and tone, for example "email my professor asking for a two-day extension for the project, polite and brief, mention I was unwell". Review the draft for facts: Gemini may add details or commitments you did not intend. For important emails, read it aloud once; if it does not sound like you, edit it. In Google Workspace accounts, administrators control which Gemini features are available.

## How does Gemini AI help users in slide creation?

In Google Slides, Gemini can generate slide content and layouts from a prompt, create images for slides, and help rewrite text. It speeds up the first draft, while you still shape the story and check every fact.

A good workflow: write a one-paragraph brief for the deck, its audience and key message; ask Gemini for an outline of eight to ten slides; generate slides one at a time and edit them; add your own data, screenshots and examples; and cut words, since slides work best with very little text. For college presentations, prepare speaker notes in your own words, because evaluators ask questions about what you present. Gemini-generated images should be labelled when they could be mistaken for real photos.

# How many Gemini images per day? ChatGPT and Copilot limits, Gemini models and missions
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-chatgpt-daily-limits/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


AI assistants such as Gemini, ChatGPT and Copilot limit how many images, videos, messages and uploads you can use per day or per rolling time window, and the numbers depend on your plan, the model or feature, and current demand. Because providers change these limits often, their official help centres are the only reliable source for exact current figures. I build AI products that work within provider limits, so this page explains how limits work for each assistant, how to stretch them, Gemini's models and versions, editing, and NASA's Gemini missions.

## How many Gemini images can I create per day?

Gemini's image generation limit depends on your plan: free users get a smaller daily allowance, and paid Google AI plans get more. Limits can also vary with demand and the image model used, and Google updates them over time.

To see current limits, check Gemini Apps Help, which lists usage limits by plan. When you reach the limit, Gemini tells you and suggests trying again later. To make the most of your allowance, write detailed prompts the first time, refine through targeted edits instead of regenerating from scratch, and save good results. Developers needing many images can use Google's image APIs with billing and rate limits. Students may also find promotional offers, such as free plan upgrades through education or telecom partnerships, so check current Google offers in India.

## How many Gemini videos can I create per day?

Video generation with Google's Veo models in Gemini is limited to a small number per day on eligible paid plans, because video generation is computationally expensive. Availability and limits depend on your plan and region.

Some Google AI plans include monthly AI credits used by tools such as Flow for more video generation. Plan your videos: write a clear prompt describing scene, action, camera and style, and use short clips. Check Gemini Apps Help for current video limits, which change as Google updates models and plans. For production video work, Google's developer APIs offer paid access with their own quotas.

## How many ChatGPT prompts can I send per day?

ChatGPT's message limits depend on your plan and the model you choose: free users have lower limits, especially on the most capable models, and paid plans offer much higher or effectively unlimited use of standard models, within fair-use rules. Some limits reset over rolling hours rather than daily.

When you hit a limit, ChatGPT may switch you to a smaller model until it resets. OpenAI's Help Center lists current limits per plan and model. To use fewer messages, combine related questions in one prompt, give complete context upfront, and start new chats for new topics. For heavy usage, a paid plan or the API is more predictable. Long conversations also slow responses and use more capacity, so summarising and restarting chats helps both speed and limits.

## How many ChatGPT pictures can I generate per day?

ChatGPT's image generation limits depend on your plan, with free users receiving a limited number per day and paid plans more, and limits may tighten temporarily during periods of very high demand after new feature launches.

Check OpenAI's Help Center or the message ChatGPT shows when you reach the limit, which states when you can create more. Get more from each generation with detailed prompts and specific edit requests. For bulk image needs, such as product catalogues, OpenAI's image API with billing is more suitable than the chat interface.

## How many files can I upload to ChatGPT per day?

ChatGPT limits file uploads by file size, files per message, and total uploads over time, with free plans more restricted than paid ones. OpenAI's file uploads FAQ lists current limits, which have changed several times.

Tips: combine related documents where sensible, upload only relevant pages of large PDFs, and use Projects or custom GPTs for files you reference repeatedly instead of re-uploading. For large document collections, a dedicated RAG system or a tool designed for many documents is more efficient than repeated uploads in chat. Remove sensitive information from files before uploading to any AI service.

## How many Copilot prompts can I send per day?

Microsoft Copilot's limits depend on whether you use the free consumer Copilot, a Copilot subscription, or Microsoft 365 Copilot at work, and on which features you use, such as image generation or deeper reasoning modes. Limits can change with demand.

Copilot typically indicates when you approach or reach a limit. Microsoft's support pages describe current plans and features. Work accounts with Microsoft 365 Copilot have usage governed by organisational licences and admin policies. For developers, GitHub Copilot has separate premium request limits per plan, and Azure OpenAI APIs have their own quotas.

## Can Gemini edit images?

Yes. Gemini can edit images you upload or create: change backgrounds, colours or styles, add or remove objects, and combine images, through conversational instructions while keeping other details consistent.

Edit step by step for control, describe what must stay the same, and use reference images for objects or styles. Edited images carry SynthID watermarks indicating AI involvement. Editing counts towards image usage limits. Respect consent and copyright: edit only images you have rights to, and avoid creating misleading images of real people.

## How many Gemini models are there?

Gemini is a family of models released in successive generations, each with several tiers, typically a Pro model for complex reasoning, Flash models for speed and efficiency, and lighter variants for high volume or on-device use, such as Gemini Nano on Android.

Google also offers specialised variants, such as models for image generation, live audio and embeddings, and open models in the related Gemma family. Older versions are retired over time. The current list is on Google's Gemini models pages and API documentation, which show model names, capabilities and context lengths.

## How many Gemini versions have there been?

Google has released several Gemini generations since the first Gemini models were announced in December 2023, including Gemini 1.0, 1.5 with long context, 2.0, 2.5 and later releases, each with multiple tiers and updates.

Version numbers mark major improvements in reasoning, multimodality, context length and tool use, while dated releases and "preview" or "experimental" labels mark updates within generations. For developers, pin specific model versions in production and test before switching, since behaviour changes between versions. For users, the Gemini app automatically uses current models.

## How many Gemini missions were there?

NASA's Project Gemini flew 12 missions in 1965 and 1966: two uncrewed test flights followed by 10 crewed missions, each with two astronauts. It came between Project Mercury and the Apollo Moon programme.

Gemini developed the techniques Apollo needed: long-duration flights, rendezvous and docking in orbit, and spacewalks, including the first American spacewalk by Ed White on Gemini 4. The name, Latin for twins, referred to the two-person crew. Google's AI model name nods to the programme as well as to twins, reflecting the merger of its two AI research teams.

# How to edit photos with Gemini or ChatGPT: prompts, best apps, saving, and fixes
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-chatgpt-photo-editing/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


To edit a photo with Gemini or ChatGPT, upload the image, describe the change in plain words, such as "change the background to a library and keep my face exactly the same", then refine with follow-up instructions until it looks right, and download the result. Both handle background changes, style transfers, object edits and enhancements. I build AI products across Google and OpenAI models, so this page covers editing with Gemini and ChatGPT, prompts, the best apps, where photos save, fixing failures, and prompting in Indian languages.

## How do I edit photos with Gemini?

Open the Gemini app or website, upload or attach your photo, and type the edit you want. Gemini returns an edited image; continue the conversation to adjust details, and download the version you like.

Tips for better edits:

- Make one change per prompt: background first, then lighting, then style.
- State what to keep: "keep the face, hairstyle and clothing unchanged".
- Describe the setting and mood specifically.
- Upload a reference image when you want a particular style or object.
- Start a new chat if results drift after many edits.

Edited images include an invisible SynthID watermark and sometimes a visible mark identifying AI editing.

## What are the best Gemini prompts for photo editing?

The best prompts describe the subject, the exact change, the style, lighting and composition, and what must stay identical. Specific, concrete wording works far better than "make it better".

Examples:

- "Replace the background with a softly blurred college auditorium; keep my face, pose and clothes unchanged."
- "Turn this photo into a professional LinkedIn headshot: neutral grey background, soft studio lighting, same face."
- "Restore this old photo: fix scratches and fading, keep it black and white."
- "Make this product photo look like a clean studio shot on a white background."
- "Convert this picture into a watercolour illustration with warm colours."

Save prompts that work and reuse them.

## How do I create a photo with Gemini?

Type a description of the image you want in the Gemini app, such as "a student presenting a robotics project at a college fest, natural daylight, candid photo style", and Gemini generates it. Refine with follow-ups, such as changing angle, colours or mood.

For realistic results, mention the camera style, lighting, setting, time of day and level of detail. For illustrations, name the art style. Avoid requesting images of real, identifiable people without consent, and do not use generated images to mislead. Image generation counts against your plan's limits, so detailed first prompts save attempts.

## How do I edit photos with ChatGPT?

In ChatGPT, upload your photo, describe the edit, and ChatGPT generates an edited version using its image model. Ask follow-up questions to refine, and download the final image from the chat.

ChatGPT is good at style transformations, adding or removing elements, background replacement, and creating variations. For precise edits, select or describe exact regions, such as "only change the sky". Results may alter details you did not mention, so state what to preserve. Generated images follow OpenAI's content policies and may carry provenance metadata indicating AI generation.

## What are good ChatGPT photo editing prompts?

Effective ChatGPT prompts mirror Gemini's: be specific about the change, the style and what to preserve, and iterate one change at a time.

Examples:

- "Change the lighting to golden hour sunset; keep everything else identical."
- "Remove the people in the background and fill naturally."
- "Make this look like a cinematic film still with teal and orange colour grading."
- "Create a cartoon avatar of this photo in a flat illustration style."
- "Expand this image to a wider 16:9 frame, continuing the scenery naturally."

If an edit goes wrong, describe precisely what to fix rather than starting over.

## Which AI app is best for photo editing?

It depends on the task. Gemini and ChatGPT are excellent for conversational edits and creative changes; Adobe Photoshop and Firefly offer precise generative fill with professional control; Google Photos' Magic Editor and Snapseed suit quick phone edits; and Canva works well for social media designs.

For professional work needing accuracy, use Photoshop or Lightroom with AI features. For quick, creative transformations, Gemini or ChatGPT are fastest. For privacy-sensitive images, prefer on-device editing tools. Check each tool's terms on commercial use of generated or edited images, especially for client work.

## Where does Gemini save photos?

Gemini shows generated and edited images in the chat, where they stay in your conversation history while that chat exists. To keep a copy on your device, use the download button on the image; on phones, it saves to your gallery or downloads folder.

If you cannot find an image, open the conversation from Gemini's chat history. Images are not automatically added to Google Photos unless you save them there. If your Gemini activity settings delete chats after a period, download important images promptly. On shared devices, remember that chat history may be visible to others using your account.

## Why is Gemini not creating photos?

Common reasons: the request conflicts with content policies, such as images of real people or sensitive topics; you reached your daily image limit; image generation is not available in your region, language or account type; or there is a temporary service problem.

Try rephrasing the prompt to remove restricted elements, check whether a limit message appears, update the app, switch between the app and web, and try again later. Some school and work accounts have image generation disabled by administrators. If Gemini replies with text instead of an image, ask explicitly: "Generate an image of...".

## Why is Gemini not editing my photos?

Gemini may refuse or fail to edit photos when the edit involves identifiable people in restricted ways, when the upload is too large or in an unsupported format, when you hit usage limits, or when the instruction is ambiguous. Sometimes it generates a new image instead of editing.

Fixes: upload a smaller JPEG or PNG, give one clear instruction, mention "edit this photo" explicitly, and start a new chat if the conversation is long. Check whether your account or region supports image editing. Avoid edits that could create misleading or harmful images of real people, which policies block.

## How do I edit photos with Gemini in Tamil or other Indian languages?

You can write your prompt in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi and many other languages Gemini supports, describing the edit just as you would in English. Gemini understands the request and performs the edit.

For very precise edits, some users find English prompts give more consistent results, because image models are often trained with more English descriptions. A practical approach: describe the edit in your language, and if the result is not right, try the same prompt in English or mix key terms, such as "background blur". Many Indian creators share prompt ideas in their languages, which help with local styles such as traditional attire and festival themes.

# What is Gemini CLI, and why do Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor have limits?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-cli-and-ai-limits/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Gemini CLI is Google's open-source AI agent for the command line. You run it in a project folder, describe a task, and it uses Gemini models to read files, run commands and make edits, asking for approval as it goes. It competes with Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI. The second half of this page explains why Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor all limit how much you can use them, including file and image uploads, and how to work within those limits.

## Gemini CLI vs other coding CLIs: how do they compare?

Gemini CLI, Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI are all terminal agents that read your codebase, edit files and run commands. They differ mainly in the models behind them, pricing and free tiers, and extras such as integrations.

Gemini CLI is open source and offers a free tier with a personal Google account, which makes it popular with students. Claude Code is widely used for complex multi-file work and has a large ecosystem of extensions. Codex CLI is open source and works with a ChatGPT plan or API key. Copilot CLI fits teams already on GitHub Copilot. All support the Model Context Protocol for extra tools. The honest way to choose is one real task in your own repository with each, judged on correctness and how much fixing the result needs.

## How does Gemini CLI work?

Gemini CLI runs a reason-and-act loop: it reads your request, decides which tool to use, such as reading a file, searching code, running a shell command or fetching a web page, observes the result, and repeats until the task is done.

Built-in tools cover the file system, shell commands, web fetch and Google Search grounding, and you can add more through MCP servers. A `GEMINI.md` file in your project gives it persistent context: build commands, conventions and rules. Before risky actions such as editing files or running commands, it asks for confirmation unless you change that setting. Because it sees your whole project and can run tests, its changes are more likely to work than code pasted from a chat window, but every diff still needs review.

## Is there a Gemini CLI tutorial?

Yes. The official repository's documentation covers installation and features, and a first session takes about ten minutes.

```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
cd my-project
gemini
```

Sign in with your Google account when prompted, then try:

- "Explain this project's structure and how to run the tests."
- Create a `GEMINI.md` with the test command and coding rules.
- "Add input validation to the signup route and write a test for it."
- Review each proposed edit and command before approving.
- Run the tests yourself and commit.

Work in a Git repository so you can roll back anything you do not like.

## Is there a course for Gemini CLI?

Google's official documentation and codelabs are the best free starting points, and some online learning platforms offer short courses on Gemini CLI and AI coding agents. A course matters less than using the tool on a real project.

Look for courses that teach transferable skills: writing a good context file, breaking work into small tasks, connecting MCP servers, reviewing diffs and testing agent output. Those apply equally to Claude Code, Codex and Copilot. A practical self-made course: spend a week building a small FastAPI or Next.js app entirely through an agent, keeping notes on which prompts worked, where it went wrong and how you fixed it. That record is also good material for interviews and a blog post.

## Can Gemini CLI handle a complex RAG migration?

It can help a lot with a complex migration, such as moving a RAG system to a new vector store, embedding model or framework, if you break the work into stages, keep tests at every step and review each change.

A workable plan for any coding agent:

- Write the migration plan first and save it in the repository.
- Build an evaluation set of questions with known good answers before changing anything.
- Migrate one component at a time: ingestion, embeddings, index, retrieval, generation.
- After each stage, re-run the evaluation and compare retrieval recall and answer quality.
- Keep the old path working behind a flag until the new one matches it.

When I built RAG.NextUpgrad, the evaluation set was what made changes safe; without one, an agent can produce a migration that looks clean but quietly retrieves worse passages.

## Does Gemini have a limit?

Yes. The Gemini app has daily limits on prompts with the most capable models and on features such as Deep Research, image and video generation. Free accounts have lower limits than paid Google AI plans, and the API has separate rate limits.

When you reach a limit, Gemini usually switches to a faster model or tells you when the limit resets. Limits are counted per feature, so you might still use the fast model after exhausting the Pro allowance. Google lists the current limits in the Gemini Apps help centre, and they change as plans are updated. Developers using AI Studio or the Gemini API see rate limits per minute and per day for their project, which rise with paid usage tiers.

## Does Gemini have a limit for uploading images?

Yes. Gemini limits how many files and images you can upload per prompt and the maximum file size, and some limits differ between free and paid plans. The Gemini Apps help centre lists the current numbers.

If an upload fails, reduce the number of images per message, compress large photos, or combine screenshots into one image or PDF. For many pages of notes, a single PDF often works better than many photos. Image generation also has its own daily limit, separate from uploads. Developers using the Gemini API have different limits for inline images versus files uploaded through the Files API, which suits larger media. Check the documentation for the version you are using.

## Why does ChatGPT have a limit?

ChatGPT has limits because every reply uses expensive computing power, especially with the most capable and reasoning models. Limits share capacity fairly among users, keep the service responsive at busy times, and separate free and paid tiers.

Different features have separate limits: messages with advanced models, image generation, deep research, file uploads and agent tasks. When you hit one, ChatGPT may switch you to a lighter model until the limit resets. To get more from your allowance, write one clear, complete prompt instead of many small follow-ups, use the faster model for simple tasks, and start new chats instead of extending very long ones, which cost more to process. OpenAI's help centre lists the current limits per plan.

## Why does Claude AI have a limit?

Claude has usage limits because running large models costs significant computing resources, and longer conversations cost more, since Claude rereads the whole conversation with each reply. Limits keep the service available for everyone.

Claude's limits are measured over rolling time windows, and long chats with large attachments use your allowance faster than short ones. To stretch it: start a new chat for each task, use Projects to hold reference files instead of re-uploading them, keep prompts focused, and choose a lighter model for simple work. Paid plans raise limits substantially, and Claude Code usage counts against the same plan. Developers using the API pay per token and have rate limits that rise with usage tiers.

## Does Cursor AI have a limit?

Yes. Cursor's plans include a usage allowance for AI requests, with the most capable models costing more of it per request. Free plans have tighter limits, and paid plans include more, with options to pay for extra usage.

Cursor has changed how it meters usage more than once, so check its pricing page and the usage dashboard in your account for the current rules. Agent sessions with large context and premium models use the allowance fastest. To make it last, select a cheaper model for routine edits, point the agent at the right files rather than the whole repository, use a `.cursorignore` file to keep build outputs and data out of context, and keep sessions focused on one task.

# Why Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor keep crashing, plus Gemini courses and Gemini agents
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-crashing-courses-agents/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


AI apps usually crash or freeze for ordinary reasons: very long conversations, outdated apps, browser extensions, low memory, network problems or service outages, and most fixes take a minute. This page covers Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and Copilot crashes, then the best Gemini courses and certificates, including for educators, and how Gemini agents work and why they may be missing. I ship AI products with multi-provider fallback, such as RAG.NextUpgrad, because every provider has bad days.

## Why does Gemini keep crashing?

Gemini usually crashes or stops responding because of an outdated Gemini or Google app, a corrupted cache, a weak connection, very long chats, browser extensions, or a temporary problem on Google's side. On phones, low storage and memory also cause force closes.

Fixes: update the Gemini and Google apps from your app store; on Android, clear the app's cache in Settings; restart your phone; switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data; start a new chat instead of continuing a very long one; and on the web, try a private window to rule out extensions. If it fails for everyone, check Google's status dashboards and wait. Work or school accounts may also be limited by an administrator, which can look like a crash when a feature is simply switched off.

## Why does ChatGPT keep crashing?

Common causes are very long conversations that make the page slow, browser extensions, a full cache, an outdated app, VPN or network issues, and outages or heavy load on OpenAI's servers.

First check OpenAI's status page; if there is an incident, wait. Otherwise, start a new chat, since long threads with many images or code blocks can freeze the browser tab. Clear the site's cache and cookies, disable extensions or try a private window, update the desktop or mobile app, and try another network without a VPN. If uploads crash it, try smaller files. Network errors during long answers often mean the response timed out, so ask for shorter outputs or split the task into steps.

## Why does Claude AI keep crashing?

Claude may fail when conversations reach length limits, large files exceed upload limits, browser extensions interfere, the app is outdated, or Anthropic's service has an incident or high demand. Usage limits on your plan can also stop replies, which looks like a crash.

Fixes: check Anthropic's status page; start a new conversation and carry over a short summary instead of continuing a very long one; split large documents; refresh the page or update the desktop app; clear the cache and try a private window; and switch networks if messages fail to send. For long work, Projects with shared knowledge reduce how much text each chat must hold. If one feature fails, such as file analysis, try again later, since features can degrade independently.

## Why does Cursor AI keep crashing?

Cursor is built on VS Code, so crashes often come from extensions, very large workspaces being indexed, low memory, GPU rendering problems, corrupted settings or an outdated version.

Try these in order: update Cursor; start it with the `--disable-extensions` flag to find a faulty extension; add a `.cursorignore` file to exclude large folders such as `node_modules`, build outputs and datasets from indexing; close unused windows and terminals; disable hardware acceleration if the window goes blank; and check the logs from the Help menu. If agent mode freezes on long tasks, start a fresh chat with a clear, smaller task. As a last resort, back up your settings and reinstall.

## Why does Copilot keep crashing?

It depends on which Copilot. GitHub Copilot in VS Code usually fails because of extension conflicts, outdated extensions, sign-in problems or proxy settings. Microsoft Copilot on Windows or in the browser fails because of app updates, cache, network or service issues.

For GitHub Copilot: update VS Code and the Copilot extensions, sign out and in again, check the GitHub status page, disable other AI extensions that compete for completions, and review proxy or firewall settings on corporate networks. The Output panel shows Copilot logs that reveal errors. For Microsoft Copilot: update the app through the Microsoft Store, use Repair or Reset under Apps in Windows Settings, clear browser data for the web version, and try another network.

## What Gemini course should I take?

Choose by goal. For everyday productivity, Google AI Essentials on Coursera teaches practical prompting and responsible use. For developers, Google's Gemini API documentation, quickstarts and cookbook are free and current. For cloud work, Google Cloud's training platform has Gemini and Vertex AI paths.

Udemy and other marketplaces have many third-party Gemini courses of varying quality; check the update date, since Gemini models and features change quickly, and read recent reviews. The fastest path for builders is hands-on: get an API key from Google AI Studio, call Gemini from Python, then add function calling, structured output and retrieval. Build one small project, such as a document question answering tool, and you will learn more than from hours of video.

## Is there a Gemini course for educators?

Yes. Grow with Google offers Generative AI for Educators, a free self-paced course developed with MIT RAISE that teaches teachers to use AI for lesson planning, differentiation and administrative work, with a certificate on completion.

Google for Education also publishes training on using Gemini in Google Workspace for Education, including guidance on privacy and classroom policies. Educators should check their institution's admin settings, since access to Gemini for student and staff accounts depends on administrators and age rules. Practical starting points are drafting rubrics, creating differentiated reading passages, generating quiz questions and summarising feedback, always reviewing outputs for accuracy before sharing them with students.

## What are Gemini agents?

Gemini agents are AI systems built on Google's Gemini models that plan and take actions, not just answer questions. Google offers agent features inside the Gemini app, business agents in Gemini Enterprise, and developer tools for building your own.

In the Gemini app, Agent Mode can carry out multi-step tasks such as researching and completing web tasks, with availability depending on plan and region; Deep Research is a related agent that browses many sources and writes reports. For developers, agents combine Gemini's function calling with tools, memory and orchestration, often using Google's open-source Agent Development Kit. Like all agents, they need clear goals, limited permissions and human review of important actions.

## Can I build AI agents with Gemini?

Yes. Use the Gemini API with function calling: you describe tools as JSON schemas, Gemini decides when to call them, your code runs them and returns results, and the loop repeats until the task is done.

For more structure, Google's Agent Development Kit, ADK, is an open-source framework for building agents with tools, multi-agent workflows, sessions and evaluation, deployable to Vertex AI Agent Engine or your own servers. Frameworks such as LangGraph and CrewAI also support Gemini models. Start with one agent and two or three tools, log every tool call, add tests for common tasks, and require approval before actions that send messages, spend money or change data.

## Why are agents missing from my Gemini?

Agent features roll out gradually and depend on your plan, country, language, age and account type. If you do not see them, the feature may not be available to your account yet rather than broken.

Check that you are signed in with the right account, since work and school accounts follow administrator settings that can disable features. Update the Gemini app and refresh the web page, check your subscription tier, and confirm your language setting is supported. Gems, which are custom Gemini assistants, are different from agents, so look for them in the Gems section. Google's Gemini Apps Help pages list current availability, which is the reliable source when features change.

# Gemini for research and developers: Deep Research, API keys, files, YouTube and 429s
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-deep-research-api-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Gemini is Google's AI assistant and model family, used both as an app for research and as an API for developers. For research, Deep Research browses many sources and writes a cited report in minutes. For developers, the Gemini API, accessed with a key from Google AI Studio, handles text, files, images, audio and video. I build document AI and RAG products across providers, so this page covers Gemini on desktop, Gems and Deep Research, model choice, API keys and APIs, sending files and YouTube videos, 429 errors, and Gemini versus Document AI.

## Does Gemini have a desktop app?

Gemini is mainly used on the web at gemini.google.com, inside Chrome, and through Android and iOS apps. On Windows and macOS, you can install the web app from Chrome as an app, which gives it its own window and taskbar icon.

Google also integrates Gemini into Chrome, Workspace apps such as Gmail and Docs, and Android. Check Google's official announcements for any native desktop apps in your region, and avoid third-party "Gemini desktop" downloads that are not from Google, since unofficial apps can misuse your account. For developers, Gemini is also available through command-line tools and IDE extensions.

## Can a Gemini Gem do Deep Research?

Gems are custom versions of Gemini with saved instructions and files, while Deep Research is a separate research mode. Depending on your plan and current features, you may be able to combine them; otherwise, run Deep Research and include your Gem's instructions in the request.

A practical workaround: keep your research brief, such as audience, scope, sources to prioritise and report structure, in a document, and paste it when starting Deep Research. After the report is generated, open your Gem to refine, summarise or reformat it. Features change often, so check Gemini Apps Help for the current relationship between Gems and Deep Research.

## How long does Gemini Deep Research take?

Deep Research usually takes several minutes, often around five to fifteen, depending on the question's complexity, how many sources it browses and system demand. It first shows a research plan you can edit, then searches and reads, then writes a report.

You can leave and come back; Gemini notifies you when the report is ready. Broad questions take longer and produce longer reports, so narrow the scope for faster, more focused results. Reports include citations, and you should open key sources to verify claims before relying on them. Deep Research usage is limited per day depending on your plan.

## Which Gemini model is best for research?

For research, use the most capable reasoning model available on your plan, typically the latest Pro model, together with Deep Research for multi-source reports. Faster Flash models suit quick lookups and summaries.

Model names change with each release, so choose by tier: Pro for complex analysis, long documents and careful reasoning; Flash for speed and everyday tasks; lightweight models for high-volume API work. For academic or professional research, combine Gemini with primary sources: verify citations, read the original papers and note publication dates. No model replaces checking evidence yourself.

## How do I get a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio?

Sign in to Google AI Studio with your Google account, open the API keys section, and create a key, which links to a Google Cloud project. Copy it once and store it securely in an environment variable or secrets manager.

Then call the API with Google's SDK:

```python
from google import genai
client = genai.Client()   # reads the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable
resp = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-2.5-flash", contents="Explain RAG briefly.")
print(resp.text)
```

Never put keys in front-end code or public repositories; route calls through your server. Restrict and rotate keys if one leaks. Free tier keys have rate limits suitable for development.

## What are the Gemini APIs?

The Gemini API gives programmatic access to Gemini models through Google AI Studio's endpoint, and the Vertex AI Gemini API offers the same models within Google Cloud with enterprise controls. Both support text generation, multimodal inputs, function calling, structured output and embeddings.

Additional capabilities include the Files API for uploading media, context caching for repeated long prompts, batch processing at lower cost, a Live API for real-time voice and video interactions, grounding with Google Search, and code execution. Choose AI Studio's API for quick development and smaller projects, and Vertex AI when you need Google Cloud security, compliance, regional controls and enterprise billing.

## How do I send files to Gemini models through the API?

For small files, include the bytes inline in the request with the correct MIME type. For larger files or reuse across requests, upload with the Files API and reference the returned file in your prompt.

```python
doc = client.files.upload(file="report.pdf")
resp = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents=[doc, "Summarise the key findings with page references."])
print(resp.text)
```

Gemini reads PDFs, images, audio and video. Uploaded files are stored temporarily, so re-upload for long-term use. For document extraction, ask for structured JSON with a schema and validate it, as DocuLens AI does for its document checks.

## Can the Gemini API watch YouTube videos?

Yes, supported Gemini models accept public YouTube URLs as video input, so you can ask for summaries, timestamps or answers about a video's content. Private and unlisted videos are not supported, and limits apply to video length per request.

Pass the URL as file data in your request, along with your question. For long videos, ask about specific segments with timestamps. Gemini processes both visual frames and audio, so it can describe what is shown as well as what is said. Respect copyright and YouTube's terms when processing videos, especially for commercial use.

## Why does my code get 429 quota exceeded errors from the Gemini API?

A 429 error means you exceeded a rate limit or quota: too many requests per minute, too many tokens per minute or too many requests per day for your tier. Streaming interfaces and generative UI frameworks can trigger extra calls without you noticing.

Fixes:

- Add exponential backoff with retries on 429 responses.
- Reduce concurrency and avoid duplicate calls from UI re-renders.
- Cache results for repeated prompts.
- Use batch processing for bulk jobs.
- Enable billing or request higher limits for production.
- Check the rate limits page for your model and tier.

Log every API call during development to spot unexpected request bursts.

## What is the difference between Gemini and Document AI?

Gemini is a general multimodal model that can read and reason about documents through prompts. Document AI is Google Cloud's specialised document processing service, with OCR, form parsing, layout analysis and pretrained or custom extractors that return structured fields.

Choose Document AI for high-volume, standardised extraction where consistent schemas, confidence scores and enterprise workflows matter, such as invoices and forms. Choose Gemini for flexible understanding, summarisation and questions across varied documents, with structured output for extraction. Many pipelines combine them: OCR and layout from a document service, then a language model for interpretation, validated against schemas before results are trusted.

# What are Gemini Gems? How they work, examples, Deep Research, lag, crashes and meaning
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-gems-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Gemini Gems are custom versions of Google's Gemini assistant that you set up once with instructions, and optionally files, so it behaves the same way every time for a task you repeat, such as a study coach, writing editor or interview practice partner. They save you re-explaining context in every chat. I design system prompts for AI products, which is essentially what a Gem is, so this page covers Gems, how Gemini and Deep Research work, NotebookLM, lag, crashes and hallucinations, and what "Gemini" means.

## What are Gemini Gems?

Gems are personalised Gemini assistants saved with your own instructions and, on supported plans, reference files. Open a Gem and Gemini already knows its role, audience, rules and format, so you can start working immediately.

Google provides premade Gems, such as a learning coach and writing editor, and you can create your own from the Gems manager in the Gemini app. Gems can be shared with others in some plans, which helps teams use consistent prompts. They are similar in idea to custom GPTs in ChatGPT and projects with instructions in Claude: reusable context for repeated work.

## How do Gemini Gems work?

When you open a Gem, Gemini adds your saved instructions, and any attached files, to the conversation as context before your messages. The model then follows those instructions, like a system prompt, for every response in that Gem.

To build a good Gem: describe the role, who it helps, the goal, rules to follow, the output format, and what to do when information is missing. Attach reference files, such as a style guide or syllabus, if your plan supports it. Test it with several real requests and refine the instructions where it goes wrong. Clear, specific instructions with reasons work better than long lists of vague rules.

## What are some example Gemini Gems?

Useful examples include a study coach that quizzes you on uploaded notes, an email editor that rewrites drafts in your tone, an interview practice partner that asks role-specific questions, a code reviewer for your stack, and a content planner that follows your brand guidelines.

Example instructions for a study Gem: "You are a patient tutor for a second-year BCA student. Explain concepts simply with one example each, then ask one practice question. If I answer wrongly, explain why and give a hint before the answer. Use the attached syllabus to stay on topic." Specific roles, audiences and behaviours make Gems far more useful.

## How does Gemini work?

Gemini is a family of large multimodal models from Google. They are transformer networks trained on text, code, images, audio and video, then tuned to follow instructions. When you send a message, the model predicts a response token by token, using the conversation and any tools.

The Gemini app adds features around the model: Google Search for current information, image generation and editing, Canvas for documents and code, Deep Research, Gems, and connections to Google apps. Different model tiers balance speed and capability, and thinking modes reason step by step before answering. For developers, the same models are available through the Gemini API.

## How does Gemini Deep Research work?

Deep Research turns a question into a research plan, which you can edit, then searches the web extensively, reads and analyses many sources, and writes a structured report with citations, typically over several minutes.

It works like a research agent: it iterates between searching, reading and deciding what is missing, rather than answering from one search. Reports can be exported to Google Docs. Use it for multi-source questions such as market overviews or literature summaries, and give it a clear scope, audience and format. Verify key claims in the cited sources, since summaries can misread or overgeneralise.

## How does a Gemini notebook work?

Google's notebook tool is NotebookLM, which uses Gemini to work only with sources you upload, such as PDFs, documents, slides, websites and videos. It answers questions with citations to your sources, and creates summaries, study guides and audio overviews.

It is a form of retrieval-augmented generation: your sources form the knowledge base, and answers are grounded in them with clickable citations. That makes it useful for studying course material, researching from specific papers or onboarding with company documents. Keep notebooks focused on one topic, and check citations for important claims. Gemini can also connect to NotebookLM content in some setups.

## Why is Gemini lagging so much?

Gemini lags when using thinking or Deep Research modes, processing long conversations or large files, generating images or video, during peak demand, or because of slow networks, heavy browser extensions or low device memory.

Fixes:

- Switch to a faster model for simple questions.
- Start a new chat when a conversation gets long.
- Upload only the pages or files you need.
- Close other heavy tabs and disable unnecessary extensions.
- Update the app or browser, or try the mobile app.
- Check your internet connection.

If many users report problems at once, it is likely a service issue that resolves on its own.

## Why does Gemini crash so much?

Crashes or failed responses usually come from very long conversations, large uploads, unstable connections, outdated apps or browsers, conflicting extensions, or temporary service problems. On phones, low memory and battery-saving settings can also close the app.

Try clearing the app cache or browser cache, updating the app, signing out and back in, and testing in a private browser window to rule out extensions. Break large tasks into smaller requests. If errors mention capacity or limits, wait or switch models. Persistent crashes on one device but not others point to a device or app issue rather than Gemini itself.

## Why does Gemini hallucinate so much?

Like all language models, Gemini predicts plausible text and can produce confident errors when it lacks information, misreads sources or is pushed to answer beyond its knowledge. Questions about niche facts, recent events without search, exact numbers and citations are most error-prone.

Reduce hallucinations by asking it to search and cite sources, providing documents to answer from, asking it to say when it is unsure, and verifying important facts. Grounded tools like NotebookLM, which answer from your sources, hallucinate less on those sources. In my RAG systems, retrieval with citations and a confidence threshold that refuses weak answers serve the same purpose.

## What does Gemini mean?

"Gemini" is Latin for "twins". It is a constellation and a zodiac sign associated with the twins Castor and Pollux. NASA's Project Gemini in the 1960s, the two-person spacecraft programme between Mercury and Apollo, used the name too.

Google's Gemini name has been explained by its leaders as a nod to twins, reflecting the merger of Google's two AI teams, Google Brain and DeepMind, into Google DeepMind, and to NASA's Gemini programme as a step towards ambitious goals. In astrology, Gemini is associated with communication and curiosity, but that has no connection with the AI model.

# What is Gemini Live? Using Gemini on your phone, and Gemini tutorials
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-live-and-phone-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-24


Gemini Live is the real-time voice mode of Google's Gemini assistant: you talk naturally, interrupt whenever you like, and Gemini answers out loud; you can also share your camera or screen so it can see what you are looking at. On Android it is built into the phone's assistant; on iPhone it is in the Gemini app. This page explains how Live works, how to find and use Gemini on your phone, whether you can remove it, and short tutorials for Gemini in general, PDFs, Veo video generation and notebooks.

## What is Gemini Live?

Gemini Live is a conversational voice mode where you speak with Gemini in real time, as in a phone call. You can interrupt it, change topic, and ask follow-ups, and it keeps the conversation's context.

Live also lets you share your camera, so Gemini can talk about what it sees, such as a plant, a circuit board or a menu in another language, and your screen, so it can help with what you are looking at. It is useful for practising interviews or spoken English, brainstorming while walking, learning a topic by asking questions aloud, or getting help with something physical in front of you. Transcripts of Live conversations appear in your Gemini history.

## How does Gemini Live work?

Gemini Live streams your voice to Google's servers, where a Gemini model built for low-latency audio understands speech and generates a spoken reply, while listening for interruptions. Camera and screen sharing add a live video feed to the conversation.

Because it is designed for conversation, it uses natural turn-taking: it stops when you start speaking and picks up from where you interrupted. It needs an internet connection and uses mobile data, so expect higher data use on video. Voice options are in settings. Developers can build similar real-time voice and video experiences with the Gemini Live API. As with any assistant, check important facts it states aloud, since spoken answers are harder to verify at a glance.

## Where is Gemini on my phone?

On most recent Android phones, Gemini is the default assistant: hold the power button, swipe up from a bottom corner, or say "Hey Google". It is also an app called Gemini in your app drawer. On iPhone, open the Gemini app from the App Store.

If you do not see it on Android, update the Google app and Play Store apps, or install Gemini from Google Play. Some phones, such as certain Samsung models, also add a Gemini shortcut to the side button. On iPhone you can add Gemini to the Lock Screen or use a Shortcut to open it quickly. Make sure you install the official app published by Google LLC; fake "Gemini" apps exist.

## How do I use Gemini on an Android phone?

Open Gemini from the power button, a corner swipe or the app, then type, speak or tap the Live button for a voice conversation. Use the camera and screen options to ask about what you see.

Things worth trying:

- "Summarise this page" while a long article is on screen.
- Circle to Search on supported phones to ask about anything on screen.
- "Set a reminder to submit the assignment at 6 pm tomorrow."
- Photograph your notes and ask for a summary or quiz.
- Ask about a YouTube video while it plays, where supported.

Connected apps, such as Google Maps, Calendar, Keep and YouTube, let Gemini act on your behalf. Review which apps it can access in Gemini's settings.

## How does Gemini work on my phone?

Gemini on your phone sends your requests to Google's Gemini models in the cloud, uses on-device models for some quick features, and connects to apps such as Calendar, Messages, Maps and YouTube when you allow it.

Most answers come from cloud models, so an internet connection is needed. Some phones also run Gemini Nano, a small on-device model, for features such as summarising recordings or smart replies, which work faster and keep data on the device. When you ask Gemini to do something in another app, it uses that app's permissions. Your conversations are saved to your Google account according to your activity settings, which you can change or turn off in Gemini's privacy settings.

## Can I remove Gemini from my phone?

On most Android phones you can switch the default digital assistant away from Gemini in settings, and disable or uninstall the Gemini app. Whether you can fully remove it depends on your phone and Android version.

Look in Settings, then Apps, then Default apps, then Digital assistant app, to change the assistant. To stop Gemini opening from the power button, change the power button setting. If the Gemini app came preinstalled as a system app, you may only be able to disable it or uninstall its updates. Google has been replacing Google Assistant with Gemini on Android, so switching back may not be available on every device. On iPhone, simply delete the app.

## Is there a Gemini tutorial for beginners?

Yes. Google's Gemini help centre has guides for each feature, and the fastest way to learn is to try five everyday tasks in your first week.

A beginner's week:

- **Day 1**: ask Gemini to explain a topic you are studying and quiz you.
- **Day 2**: upload a PDF and ask for a one-page summary.
- **Day 3**: use Gemini Live to practise answering interview questions aloud.
- **Day 4**: create a Gem, a custom assistant with saved instructions, for a task you repeat.
- **Day 5**: connect Google Calendar and plan your week.

Write prompts with context: who you are, what you need and the format you want. Check facts in every answer.

## How do I use Gemini with a PDF?

Upload the PDF in the Gemini app with the plus button, then ask questions: a summary, explanations of difficult sections, key terms, or practice questions. Gemini can read long documents and point you to relevant parts.

Good prompts for study:

- "Summarise this chapter in ten bullet points for revision."
- "Explain section 3.2 as if I am new to the topic, with an example."
- "List all definitions in this PDF as a glossary."
- "Write five exam-style questions from this document, then check my answers."

For scanned PDFs, Gemini can read the images, but accuracy drops with poor scans. For courses with many documents, NotebookLM is often better, because it keeps sources together and cites the exact passages.

## How do I use Veo 3 in Gemini?

In the Gemini app, choose the video option, describe the scene you want, and Gemini generates a short clip with Google's Veo model, including sound. Access depends on your plan and country, and there are daily limits.

Write prompts like a director: subject, action, setting, camera movement, lighting, style and sound, for example "a slow dolly shot of a student coding at night in a small hostel room, warm desk lamp, rain on the window, soft keyboard sounds". Generate several versions and keep the best. Clips are short, so plan longer videos as several shots edited together. Generated videos carry a visible or invisible watermark; label them as AI-generated when you share them, and never create videos of real people without consent.

## How do I use Gemini notebooks?

Notebooks in Google's AI tools usually means NotebookLM: create a notebook, add sources such as PDFs, Docs, websites or YouTube videos, then ask questions answered only from those sources, with citations. Google has also been connecting notebooks to the Gemini app.

A study workflow: create one notebook per subject, add your syllabus, lecture notes and textbook chapters, and ask for a study guide, a list of likely exam questions, and explanations of the hardest topics. Click citations to check each answer against your material. Audio overviews turn your sources into a podcast-style discussion you can listen to while travelling. Keep sources accurate and current, because answers are only as good as what you upload.
